title.en: Damnern Saduak Floating Market, Grand Palace and Wat Phra KeoTour from Bangkok

overview: Experience vibrant Damnern Saduak floating market on this day-long private tour of Bangkok’s most memorable sights.

Pass through dramatic rice paddies and salt fields, and meet traditional artisans on your way to the market, where vendors in wooden boats sell the fruits and vegetables they’ve brought from the countryside. After dining in this atmospheric setting, immerse yourself in Bangkok’s vivid history. Step aboard a river boat into the heart of the city, then explore the Grand Palace and the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, considered the most sacred in Thailand.
highlights: Private guide for a more personalized experience
Travel by boat and see the sights from the water
All entrance fees included
Lunch included
expect: Enjoy a full-day excursion from Bangkok to the legendary Damnoen Saduak Floating Market, located approximately 65 miles (110 kilometers) west of the Thai capital. Your journey commences with a leisurely and scenic drive through rice paddies and salt fields. En route, visit a farmhouse and watch locals producing sugar from coconut. The tour then continues by boat, passing fruit plantations and Thai houses that reveal a more traditional way of life. Upon arrival at Damnoen Saduak Floating Market, discover boats of all different shapes and sizes, still used by local merchants to ferry their goods along this Venice of the East. Having immersed yourself in thw electric environment, head back towards Bangkok, stopping at a wood-carving factory en route.

After lunch, visit the home of the Kings of Siam of the Chakri Dynasty in the heart of Bangkok. Originally built by King Rama I, and serving as royal residence until 1946, today the palace is used for visiting royalty or special guests of the Kingdom. Adjoining the Grand Palace, admire the Temple of the Emerald Buddha (Wat Phra Keo), the best known of the royal temples, and regarded as the most important temple in all of Thailand. It is used for numerous religious ceremonies in which the King participates, especially at the beginning of each of the 3 seasons when the king personally changes the elaborate robes of the Buddha image, carved out of a single piece of emerald-green jasper.

title.en: Full-Day Floating Market and Ayutthaya Temples Tour from Bangkok

overview: Get a window into both present-day and medieval Thailand on this day trip to Damnoen Saduak floating market and Ayutthaya from Bangkok. Experience the colors and commotion at Damnoen Saduak, sailing past boats piled with food, handicrafts, and more. Then, visit UNESCO-listed Ayutthaya, the ruined capital of Siam to see its old temples including Wat Mahathat and the Buddha wrapped in tree roots. Entrance fees, lunch, and hotel pickup and drop-off included.
highlights: Full-day Damnoen Saduak and Ayutthaya trip from Bangkok
Ride a boat through Damnoen Saduak, Thailand’s most famous floating market
Absorb the atmosphere as you cruise canals filled with boats selling fresh foods, crafts, and more
Visit the ruined medieval capital of Ayutthaya, a UNESCO World Heritage site
View temples like Wat Mahathat and Wat Lokayasutharam, and the Buddha head entangled in tree roots
Round-trip transport, lunch, entrance fees, and Bangkok hotel pickup and drop-off included
expect: After early pickup from your Bangkok hotel, travel west out of the city by air- conditioned vehicle. Your day trip includes a stop for lunch at a convenient point in your travels.
As you leave Bangkok’s suburbs and head into Thailand’s Samut Songkram Province, hear fascinating facts about your first destination: Damnoen Saduak, Thailand’s most famous floating market.

This colorful market runs every morning, and see hundreds of vendors arrive at the canals to sell their wares from boats and waterside stalls. On arrival, take to the water in a traditional boat, and drift through the crowded waterways, passing vessels piled with fresh produce, housewares, foods, crafts, and souvenirs. Be sure to barter for any goods, and soak in the colors and commotion as you sail.

Afterward, continue north to Ayutthaya, home to the ruins of what was an ancient capital of the Kingdom of Siam. View rural Thailand along the way, and when you arrive, stroll around the sprawling, UNESCO-listed ruins, whose origins date to 14th century, and once formed a thriving city of roads, canals, moats, monasteries, and temples. Take in the crumbled, elaborately carved towers (prangs), seeing highlights including the Wat Mahathat, once the city’s most important monastery. The most popular and well-known of these aquatic shopping centers is the Damnoen Saduak, located 62 miles (100 km) southwest of Bangkok in the Ratchaburi province. The market takes place along a canal built in 1868 by King Rama IV that provides a route for critical inter-province travel and irrigation water for local farmers. Get an early start with morning pickup at your Bangkok hotel to experience the peak selling times and avoid the afternoon heat and crowds. The bustling, chaotic market can be overwhelming for first-time visitors, but your local guide will help you navigate the throngs of boats and give tips on bargaining with vendors for any purchases you’d like to make. You can pick up an array of locally grown produce as well as souvenir trinkets, or simply absorb the vibrant atmosphere of traditional wooden boats paddled by bamboo-hatted farmers through the crowded canal.

On the route back to Bangkok, visit Phra Pathommachedi in the town of Nakhon Pathom. This ancient stupa — a type of sacred pagoda with a distinctive mound-like architecture — rises an impressive 395 feet (120 meters), making it the largest of its kind in the world. After this impressive stop, your full-day market tour concludes with drop-off back at your Bangkok hotel in the early afternoon, leaving you free to spend the rest of the day as you please.

title.en: Private Tour: Full-Day Suphanburi Tour from Bangkok

overview: Suphanburi is one of the more rural regions outside of Bangkok, well-known for preserving an authentic farming life style, even during these modern times. Immerse yourself into a world that feels like being ‘stuck in time’ when times were much simpler, allow the historic atmosphere to take you away from the worries of city life.
highlights: Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Led by a local guide
Lunch included
expect: Depart from your hotel in Bangkok in the morning at around 8am and drive in northern direction out of the city center. The province Suphanburi lies around 110km outside of the Thai capital.

Travelling around the Suphanburi province is like drifting through historical novels. Suphanburi is an ancient town (more than 4000 years old), rich in natural and historical heritage. The province was once an important border town involving battles and important wars during the period of the Ayutthaya kingdom.

During the morning, traditional farming techniques at a local buffalo village where farmers continue to preserve a lifestyle that has not changed in decades, is what we encounter. Locals show meticulously how buffaloes are trained to work into the fields and paddy farming. It is not uncommon here to bear witness to various processions and dance performances that play an important part in the lives of these villages. A variety of farming tools are on display at the village as well a collection of Thai houses from the various provinces. After lunch at a local restaurant, we proceed to the 300+-year-old Baan Krang Temple and then continue visit to Pang Muang Chapel. The Baan Krang Temple was constructed during Ayutthaya period. Some stories tell that it has been presumed that the temple must be at least 400 years old yet more signs indicate that it was constructed in the 18th century. The highlight of the temple is a chamber of Phra Khun Paen Baan Krang, made of baked clay. Before heading to your home way from home, we drive to the Don Chedi Memorial, one of the most famous ancient battle sites in Thai history. It was here that King Naresuan, then a prince, defeated the prince of Myanma on elephant in the late 16th century. In doing so he freed Ayutthaya from the Bago (Pegu) kingdom. Bago in these days is no longer part of the Kingdom of Thailand but has moved inside the country borders with neighboring Myanmar. At the end of the tour you will be taken back to your hotel safely.

overview: Koh Kret island is an ideal rural escape from Bangkok, but the picturesque community is difficult to reach by public transport. expect: Begin with pickup from your Bangkok hotel, and travel to a pier on the Chao Phraya river, where you’ll board a ferry to the opposite bank. Travel upriver in a longtail boat — the brightly painted, traditional boats are powered by a car engine, and often wrapped in strips of fabric for good luck — and take in views of riverside settlements. See wooden shacks at the water’s edge while steering past slow-moving cargo barges on their way to upstream markets. Capture images of 19th-century, European buildings juxtaposed with noodle and seafood vendors in wooden sampan boats. When you reach Koh Kret, enjoy free time to walk around and explore local shops, markets, and food stalls. The island was created almost 300 years ago, when a canal was dug to bypass a bend in the Chao Phraya River, and Koh Kret is one of Thailand’s oldest Mon communities, with distinctive culinary treats that are hard to find off-island.

Take a break for lunch, then follow your guide on a sightseeing tour of the island’s highlights, focusing on traditional temples and living conditions in local communities. Board the longtail boat for the downriver trip to Bangkok, and finish the day with return transfer to your hotel.

title.en: Foodie Experience of Historic Bangrak

overview: Savor the flavors and aromas of authentic Thai cuisine on a half-day culinary walking tour of Bangkok’s Bang Rak neighborhood. Join a small group of foodies and eat your way through the historic district, which is a renowned destination for Bangkok’s culinary connoisseurs.

Meet chefs and artisans and explore the diversity of Thailand’s regional, ethnic and “royal” cuisines as you sample roast duck, handmade curries and distinctive Isan salads, along with fresh fruit, holistic herbal infusions and the best of traditional Thai desserts.

expect: Meet with our culinary-trained, fully licensed tour guide at BTS Saphan Taksin station in the morning. Walk your way through the old streets of Bang Rak "the Village of Love" and experience Bangkok's mom and pop food culture and local unseen attractions. Bangrak is the district famous among Thais for its diverse local flavors. The area is a true melting pot, where you can find Thai delicacies from various regions and ethnicity. This walking tour will stop at 5 local restaurants, where you will sample more than 12 items of food and drinks and have a chance to meet and engage with restaurant owners. On this tour, not only you will get full exposure to the Thai gastronomic tradition but your visit will also be a great support to the local community.

From BTS station, our first stop will be a half century old Thai-Chinese eatery serving some of the best Thai-style roast duck. Then, walk along the back streets to visit its hidden gem, Wat Suan Plu temple, and learn about its significance to the community. Continue your food journey and visit one of the oldest eateries in the area, a Thai-Muslim restaurant offering very unique Thai-Halal dishes. Then, it is time to cross the majestic Chao Phraya river to get to the other side of Bangkok as you will visit a hole-in-the-wall eatery serving Northeastern Thai cuisines. You will not be considered completing your visit without tasting something from the "ISAN menu" including the spicy green papaya salad and Thai-style fried chicken with herbs. As the tour guide brings you back to Bang Rak area, you will visit another local institution famous for snacks and sweets. There, you will taste the original pandan flavor custard bun served with the delicious Thai ice tea. Our last tasting location features Royal Thai cuisine serving from a restaurant run by a Thai Royal decedent. You will taste the Royal-recipe green curry served with Thai style roti. Finish your tasting with the refreshing Thai-style ice cream before the tour guide walks you to our ending point at Surasak BTS Station. After the tour, you will be confident to continue your journey in Thailand and eat like a local.

Travel next to Phra Athit Road and encounter Bangkok’s roti expert; sample Thai-Indian cuisine, from this freshly baked bread to uniquely flavorful curries. Indulge your taste buds at Bangkok’s most popular pad Thai restaurant, enjoying the spicy and savory flavors of these delicate noodles topped with crunchy peanuts. Take a short break from eating to visit the illuminated Wat Pho after dark. See the temple’s sparkling gold towers and marvel at the sight of its magnificent Reclining Buddha. Sip a refreshing cocktail at the Eagle Nest, a bar at Sala Arun Hotel, as you take in the splendid views of the Chao Phraya River and the twinkling buildings along the riverbanks. Later, stroll through Pak Klong Talat, Thailand’s largest flower market, which operates overnight. End your 4-hour tour on a sweet note with mango sticky rice.

expect: Your food tour of Bangkok’s Chinatown begins when you meet your guide at Hua Lamphong, located at the border of one of the world’s largest Chinatowns. This neighborhood has been a hub of the Thai-Chinese community for more than two centuries. Your guide provides a brief history of the neighborhood as you set out on foot through the dense tangle of alleys and streets, which are jam-packed with markets, street vendors, restaurants and shops of all sizes. With your guide in the lead, you can absorb the multitudes of scents, sights and flavors as you stop frequently to sample a range of typical and specialty dishes. Learn about the intricacies of dim sum in Thailand, sink your teeth into savory Chinese dumplings, and sample a plate of richly flavored peppered pork noodles. Visit the top-ranked roast-pork and rice restaurant in Bangkok, and slurp a refreshing coconut noodle drink in a renowned shophouse that is frequented by the Thai royal family.

Your guide points out neighborhood mainstays such as Chinatown’s most famous durian vendor. Find out how to select the best fruit, and if you’re adventurous, try the notoriously smelly durian fruit. Some people love the strong sweet flavor while others find its potent scent nauseating.

Stop into a tea shop that carries a variety of teas, including the most expensive tea in Bangkok. Watch a short demonstration of the preparation and service of Chinese tea. Then have a dessert of tasty Chinese doughnuts and try other sweets along Chinatown’s main road. By the end of your tour, you can expect to have eaten the equivalent of a satisfying meal. Your tour ends at a central location, within easy reach of the BTS Station and other transportation. Your guide can assist you with directions to your next destination. overview: Unlock the beauty of Thailand on this 6-day northern Thailand tour from Bangkok to Chiang Mai. Travel through the beautiful countryside, past epic landscapes and ancient ruins, with your friendly, professional guide. Learn about local culture and age-old traditions on your visit to a traditional hill tribe village near Chiang Rai, where you’ll gain a deeper understanding of rural Thai life. Wander the colorful streets of the popular travel destination of Chiang Mai. Head off to the Thai-Mayanmar (Burma) border, where you’ll walk across the bridge (conditions permitting), and check out stunning views from the Golden Triangle—a point where Laos, Mayanmar and Thailand meet. Enjoy an optional boat ride on the famous Mekong River and eat like a local with meals at typical Thai restaurants served up daily.
highlights: 6-day northern Thailand tour from Bangkok to Chiang Mai
Enjoy a comprehensive tour of the northern Thai countryside, including a trip to the
Thailand-Myanmar (Burma) border and the Golden Triangle
Discover ancient palaces, temples and Buddhist shrines in Ayutthaya, Lopburi and
Sukhothai
Admire the craftsmanship of artisans at work in Chiang Mai
Watch elephants and their mahouts at a camp in the jungle
See traditional costumes and customs of several hill tribe villages
Experience a traditional Thai dinner with folk dance performances
expect: Your 6-day northern Thailand Tour of Ayutthaya, Cukhothai, Chiang Mai and Chaing Rai from Bangkok includes 4-start hotel accommodation and traditional Thai meals daily. You’ll follow your guide on an exciting coach tour of ancient cities, historic ruins, hill country villages, craft markets, elephant camps and rural countryside. Make stops in Chiang Rai and the Thai-Mayanmar (Burma) border on this truly memorable small group tour. Itinerary
Day 1: Bangkok– Phitsanulok (L, D)

Begin your tour with an early morning departure from Bangkok, with pickup from your Bangkok hotel or Bangkok International Airport. Then, drive north by air-conditioned coach to Bang Pa-In, a lavish royal summer palace set amid lovely gardens that include charming Thai topiaries cut into the shapes of elephants.

Upon arrival at the palace, your guide will discuss the combination of Thai and European architecture. Admire the elegant Thai pavilion, which stands in the middle of a lake, and see a Thai house constructed entirely out of wood.

Back aboard the coach, head to Ayutthaya – the ancient capital city of Siam – where ruins of splendid temples and palaces once destroyed by the Burmese still remain. As you walk around with your guide, learn about the extensive canal and river network that helped Ayutthaya to flourish.

Enjoy free time to browse the numerous stalls of Thai handicrafts and then have lunch at a local restaurant with your group. Afterward, embark on a scenic drive through the Thai countryside to Lopburi, a former summer capital of Siam during the 6th to 11th centuries. Here, view the magnificent stone carvings of Phra Prang Sam Yod, a block shrine with three spires. See the Kala shrine of Sarn Prakarn, a 13th-century Buddhist temple sanctuary now inhabited by hundreds of monkeys!

In the afternoon, your guide will drive your group further north to the town of Phitsanulok along the banks of the Nan River, where numerous houseboats are moored. Visit the shrine of Wat Mahathat for a glimpse of ancient Thai religious architecture. Then, enjoy dinner with your group before an evening spent at leisure. / Overnight
Day 2: Phitsanulok – Chiang Rai (B, L, D)

After breakfast, you’ll visit Sukhothai, the 13th-century capital of Thailand. Admire numerous standing Buddha statues as you explore the ruined temples and monasteries in the ancient city, which was once protected by rows of ramparts and two moats. Then, head to nearby Si Satchanalai, considered Sukhothai’s twin city, where you’ll have lunch at a local establishment.

In the afternoon, your coach tour will take you through rural Thailand and even further north through jungle-clad hills toward Chiang Rai. Along the way, stop in Phayao, a small 11th- century town where you’ll enjoy refreshments beside a lake.
Arrive at your accommodation in the late afternoon and relax before dinner. / Overnight
Day 3: Chiang Rai (B, L, D)

After breakfast, board a van for an exciting day trip to visit several hill tribe villages for which northern Thailand is famous. Enjoy scenic mountain views on the narrow climb, stopping in the Chinese settlement of Doi Mae Salong (Santikhiri) on the way. When you reach the Akha and Yao hill tribes, where villagers continue to wear traditional garments, learn about some of the customs of rural village life.

Returning to the valley for lunch, your guide will take your group to Mae Sai, Thailand’s northernmost town near the Myanmar (Burma) border. Here, browse for Burmese handicrafts, and watch Thai and Burmese locals walking across the bridge that separates the two countries. Depending on conditions at the Thailand-Myanmar border, your group may have the option to cross the bridge into Myanmar on an approximate one-hour exploratory walk with your guide. (Two photocopies of your passport are required along with a border pass fee.) If you want to explore the marketplace in a different way, hop onto a rickshaw and be taken through its winding alleways aboard this local transport (own expense).

From Mae Sai, drive to the heart of the renowned Golden Triangle where the Ruak and Mekong Rivers meet. Stand on a hilltop and enjoy views of Myanmar, Laos, Thailand and the mighty rivers below. An optional boat trip (own expense) is available for those who want to get closer to Laos, where you may spend approximately 30 minutes exploring the market area here. Afterward, visit Chiang Saen, where evidence of the original 13th-century city can still be seen; enjoy views of lovely old temples and finely carved figures from a tranquil spot on the banks of the Mekong River before your drive back to Chiang Rai. / Overnight
Day 4: Chiang Rai – Chiang Mai (B, L, D)
After breakfast, depart for Chiang Mai with your guide, stopping first in Mae Ka Chan, famous for its hot spring – a favorite bathing spot for the locals who soak there to relieve aches and pains.

After lunch at a local restaurant, drive through more mountain scenery and tropical jungle to visit the hilltop temple of Wat Phrathat Doi Suthep. Climb 290 steps (or ride the cable car) up the hill for outstanding views of Chiang Mai, referred to as the “Rose of the North.” In the evening, after checking in at your hotel, enjoy a kantoke – a ceremonial dinner where traditional northern Thai dishes are served as you watch elegant dancers perform a series of folk stories. After dinner, the show continues with northern hill tribes performing traditional dances in colorful costumes. / Overnight
Day 5: Chiang Mai (B, L, D)

Enjoy breakfast with your group in preparation for a full day touring the Chiang Mai region. In the morning, visit an elephant camp where skilled mahouts (trainers) demonstrate how elephants have worked in the jungles for centuries. Watch in amazement as the elephants reveal their intelligence and strength, and be amused by their play as the elephants relax and bathe in the river afterward.

the district of Sankampaeng, where Chiang Mai’s cottage industries flourish. Watch artisans create beautiful crafts as you browse for the perfect gift or souvenir. See how they weave intricate patterns of silk with their handlooms, carve elegant teakwood ornaments and furniture, and make distinctive Thai ceramics and lacquer ware – using eggshells to create unusual designs. Marvel at the transformation of bamboo, silk and paper into colorful hand- painted umbrellas.
When you return to your hotel, enjoy a relaxing evening with free time to explore Chiang Mai on your own. / Overnight
Day 6: Chiang Mai (B)

Enjoy a final breakfast before saying farewell to your group. Your tour ends in Chiang Mai, where you can choose to spend a few more days, or return to Bangkok by air or rail (own expense). If you have a flight to catch, your guide will drop you off at the Chiang Mai International Airport.

title.en: 5-Day Houseboat Adventure on Khao Laem Lake from Bangkok

overview: Embark on a 5-day houseboat adventure upon Thailand’s Khao Laem Lake. After arriving in western Thailand’s Kanchanaburi province you’ll board a communal houseboat that docks in a new location each night. Spend your days lounging in a hammock, kayaking, interacting with locals and participating in scheduled activities like hiking and visits to hillside villages. This inclusive sojourn includes meals, transportation to and from Bangkok and your choice of a single, double or six-bed dorm room.
highlights: 5-day houseboat stay on Khao Laem Lake in western Thailand
Spend time relaxing in a hammock, kayaking, swimming and admiring the verdant scenery
Explore the lake's villages and natural surroundings like Lijia cave and Coconut
Island
Visit a Mon and Karen hill tribe village, and meet local people
Look for wildlife such as eagles, hornbills and monkeys
Take a short hike and bamboo raft ride near Sangkhlaburi
Includes transportation, guide, meals and activities
expect: Each day the houseboat moves to a new part of this beautiful lake, and you'll take excursions around the lake by smaller boats with your guide. Enjoy the tranquility of misty mornings and sunsets on the lake, which is surrounded by lushly forested mountains. The houseboat holds up to 24 passengers and features a well-equipped lounge area with a large sundeck, lounge chairs and a bar. Provided amenities include kayaks, floating tubes, fishing equipment, hammocks, and coffee and tea. Three meals a day are cooked fresh on board by the staff, and alcohol and soda are available for purchase. You have your choice of a single room, double room or 6-bed dorm room. All rooms have French balconies; bathrooms and showers are shared.
Itinerary
Day 1: Bangkok – Khao Laem Lake (L, D)

In the morning, meet your guide in central Bangkok, and travel by air-conditioned minivan about five hours northwest of the city to reach Khao Laem Lake. Along the way, your guide shares commentary about the Kanchanaburi province, where the lake is located. You’ll stop for lunch at a restaurant near Sai Yok Noi waterfall.

When you arrive at the lake in the mid-afternoon, board the houseboat and cruise to tonight’s anchorage spot. Enjoy a freshly prepared Thai dinner, and chat with other travelers while you watch your first sunset on the lake and soak up the pretty twilight scenery./ Overnight
Day 2: Khao Laem Lake (B, L, D)

Wake up for a healthy breakfast, served each morning between 07.00 and 09.00. Depending on the season and water level you will either do a short jungle walk to beautifully flushing waterfall, or you will explore the Lijia cave and the nearby local village. The waterfall is cascading and impressive when the water level is high (usually Sep-Mar), inviting you for a swim after the short trek through the jungle.

As the water level detracts, you will instead do short trek to Lijia village, where you can get close to local life. Continue to the Lijia cave where you can explore the inside. If you are lucky, you might find a few treasures. It is believed that Japanese soldiers left these treasures, including gold, in the area when they built the Death Railway during the World War II. If time allows, you will visit the nearby school or fisherman village. When back on the Lake House you will be served a nice Thai lunch. The afternoon is free for you to enjoy Lake House Living. Swim in the lake, do a bit of fishing, kayak the calm water or doze the afternoon away. As day turns into night, enjoy a delicious Thai dinner and watch the stars spark high up in the sky./ Overnight
Day 4: Khao Laem Lake (B, L, D)

Enjoy a leisurely morning with the chance to take a boat trip to steep cliffs that jut out of the water, where you might spot monkeys in the treetops or birds like eagles and hornbills. After lunch, the houseboat slowly moves toward Sangkhlaburi. Visit a temple that's hidden away in the forest and known only to a few locals, and then see another temple that has been covered by the lake and is only partially visible. (Depending on the water level it can be fully visible, while at other times fully covered with a meter to spare) Anchor near Sangkhlaburi for the night, with free time in the afternoon to spend at your leisure on the houseboat. /Overnight
Day 5: Khao Laem Lake – Sangkhlaburi – Bangkok (B, L, D)

Enjoy a very early morning breakfast and prepare to disembark your floating hideaway at 09:00 latest. You need to pack all your bags and belongings, as it will be transported to our rest house while you are out exploring. We recommend wearing clothes and shoes that may get wet and a dry bag for your camera.

Around 09:30 you will be picked up and go by local Songthaew or four-wheel drive to the wooden Mon Bridge in Sangkhlaburi town. Not only is it the largest wooden bridge in Thailand that connects the two sides of Mae Nam Kwae Noi, it also connects the three ethnic communities Mon, Karen and Thai. Cross the beautiful bridge by foot and at the other side, continue by car to the outskirts of Sangkhlaburi from where you do a short hike through the forest, along the riverbed. Cross river streams, walk over simple bamboo bridges and through dense grassland. At an opening in the forest, change means of transport to bamboo rafts or rubber dinghy’s, depending on the season and water level. Sit back and enjoy nature slowly passing by, the dense jungle leaning over the river. Occasionally, steer through a small rapid before you reach an opening in the jungle and a simple lunch is served at the river bank. Go back to the rest house in Sangkhlaburi and if you have more energy, explore a bit more of Sangkhlaburi or lean back with a cup of coffee. In the mid afternoon, start your return drive back towards New Road Guest House in downtown Bangkok. You will be back late evening and stop for a quick dinner on the way. If you choose to end in Kanchanaburi, you will be dropped of on the way to Bangkok.
Should you choose to stay in Sangkhlaburi the tour ends here and you have the opportunity to commence your onward explorations.

title.en: 2-Day Mekhala Exotic Siam Cruise from Bangkok

overview: Welcome aboard for an enchanting journey along the historical Chao Phraya River. Cruise either up-stream or down-stream between Bangkok and the ancient capital of Ayuthaya, staying overnight alongside a traditional Buddhist temple. Once a rice barge, the exotic boat is now a floating boutique hotel. There is no better way to sample the leisurely life along the River of Kings. Just one day’s journey can transport you back through hundreds of years of Siamese culture and history. View life along this waterway of Thai life in style.
highlights: Multi-Day Trip
Travel by boat and see the sights from the water
Led by a local guide
Breakfast included
Lunch included
Dinner included
expect: Upstream Itinerary
Day 1:

Transfer from your Hotel in Bangkok to board Mekhala Cruise. Start cruising up the Chao Phraya River. Passing the Grand Palace and the Temple of Dawn. Arriving at Pathum Thani in the afternoon, you will visit a fresh market where locals shop for food. At sunset, the Mekhala will dock at Wat Kai Tia, a Buddhist temple located in a tranquil rural village. An exquisite candlelit dinner of mouth-watering Thai cuisine will be served on the deck. You will spend the night on board the boat, in your air-conditioned cabin.
Day 2

We start the day by cruising to a small village of Baan Saladang, an aged-old Mon community who migrated from Burma to this area in the early 19th century. The villagers here have maintained their traditional life style, customs and natural surroundings. You will also see a collection of well-preserved Thai houses in this charming village. Afterwards, you can enjoy a delicious breakfast. Later in the morning, you will disembark and travel to Bang-Pa-In Summer Palace. The mansions reflect Chinese, Swiss, Khmer, Thai and European styles of architecture. Travel by long tail boat to the capital of Ayuthaya to visit the archeological site of the once glorious capital. After lunch at a local restaurant, return transfer back to your Hotel in Bangkok.
Downstream Program

Transfer from your Bangkok Hotel to Ayuthaya. Visit the archaeological site of the once glorious capital. After lunch at a local restaurant, cruise on a long-tail boat to Bang-Pa-In to explore the Summer Palace. After this visit, our guide will drop you off, to board the Mekhala boat. We now enjoy watching rural life along the “River of Kings” on board the boat. You will visit a small village of Baan Saladang, an aged-old Mon community who migrated from Burma to this area in the early 19th century. The villagers here have maintained their traditional life style, customs and natural surroundings. You will also see a collection of well- preserved Thai houses in this charming village. Soon after sunset, the Mekhala will dock at Wat Kai Tia, a local Buddhist temple set in a tranquil village. An exquisite candlelit dinner of mouth-watering Thai cuisine awaits you on the deck. You will spend the night on board the boat in your air-conditioned cabin.

title.en: 3-Day Nan Tour: The Hidden Gem of North Thailand

overview: Experience the natural beauty and cultural heritage of northern Thailand with a 3-day trip to Nan by air from Bangkok, and explore ancient temples, religious traditions and wild forests. Learn about the history of the remarkable Nan region at a national museum and Nan's most important landmarks. Join the locals to give alms to Buddhist monks then see fossilized trees and tropical blooms at Doi Phuk Ka National Park. Cross the Nan river to see a sacred, centuries-old wat cloaked in copper and brass before boarding returning to Bangkok.
highlights: Informative, friendly and professional guide
Perfect introduction for first-time visitors
Multi-Day Trip
Excellent value for money
Private tour is operated with just your party and a guide/driver
expect: Day 1 Bangkok – Nan

We will pick you up from your hotel in Bangkok and transfer you to Bangkok airport for your flight to Nan (domestic tickets from and to Nan are not included in the program). Upon arrival at Nan, your guide and driver await you at the airport. Before we head off for our afternoon excursion, we include lunch at a local restaurant. After lunch, we start with our Nan exploration by a visit to Nan National Museum. The museum display exhibitions relating to the city’s history and major structures, evolution of local art at different ages, and numerous ancient objects. Continue your visit at Wat Phumin, famous for its ancient mural wall paintings called Pu Man-Ya Man, in Thai Lu style. Conclude with an overnight stay at a hotel in Nan.
Day 2 - Nan

Rise and shine! An early start in the morning is a wonderful chance to make merit with the monks. Thai Buddhists believe that by making merit, they earn happiness, peace in life, and the chance to progress in their next life. This sacred experience creates a harmonious way to start the day for all. Return to the hotel for breakfast.

After breakfast, we leave Nan and head to Wat Nong Bua, an ancient temple built by Thai Lue who migrated from Sib Song Pan Na Province in South China. This temple is famous for its mural paintings that reflect the social status of people during that time. Continue onward to Doi Phuk Ka National Park and see the amazing scenic point called Lan Do Dao (translated as Stargazing Field) located among the primeval forest. This park is also home to the fossilized Phu Ka Tree as well as unusual flowers that bloom only in February Lunch will be given en route at a local restaurant before we meander further into the Bo Klua district, an important salt production region of Nan. Nan has historically been a large source of exported rock salt in the northern portion of Thailand. It is fascinating to watch an activity that is still done exactly the same way as it was for hundreds of years.
Day 3 Nan - Bangkok

We say goodbye to the hotel staff and depart to yet another important sight that cannot be missed. The Wat Phrathat Chae Haeng is a sacred place for worship, situated on the eastern side of the Nan River. From here, we head back to Nan Airport for your flight back to Bangkok (domestic tickets from and to Nan are not included in the program). After arriving at Bangkok Airport, a transfer will occur from the airport to your Bangkok Hotel.
Itinerary

We will pick you up from your hotel in Bangkok and transfer you to Bangkok airport for your flight to Nan (domestic tickets from and to Nan are not included in the program and customers are required to book these tickets), we recommend a morning departure. Upon arrival at Nan, your guide and driver await you at the airport and before we head off for our afternoon excursion, lunch is provided at a local restaurant. After lunch, we start our Nan exploration with a visit to Nan National Museum and then continue to Wat Phumin which is famous for its ancient mural wall paintings called Pu Man-Ya Man, and are in Thai Lu style. We also visit Wat Chang Kham Woravihan which is a must see temple in the area, the Chedi inside the temple reflects the influence of Sukhothai arts.

We return back to the city and stop at Wat Pratard Noi, which located on top of the hill offering the best panoramic views over Nan. There is an optional short bicycle tour here (to be paid locally) around Nan and it is a great way to finish off a cultural enriching day. No dinner included in this package. Overnight at a hotel in Nan.
Day 2 Nan

Rise and shine! An early start is a wonderful chance to make merit with the monks. Thai Buddhists believe that by making merit, they earn happiness, peace in life, and the chance to progress in their next life, while this sacred experience creates a harmonious way to start the day for all.

We return to the hotel for breakfast before heading to Wat Nong Bua. This is an ancient temple built by Thai Lue who migrated from Sib Song Pan Na Province in South China. This temple is famous for its mural paintings which reflect the social status of people in that time. After a short drive, we reach Nong Bua Thai Lue; its villages are renowned for making beautiful local fabric hand weaving.

One of the primeval forests in Thailand has an amazing scenic point called Lan Do Dao (translated as Stargazing Field) at Doi Phuk Ka National Park. This national park is home of the fossilized Phu Ka Tree, which is extremely rare and has an array of unusual flowers growing upwards that bloom only in February.

Lunch is en-route at a local restaurant and will be a welcome stop before we meander further into the Bo Klua district, this an important salt production region of Nan and we return back to your hotel in Nan.

After breakfast, we leave the hotel and depart to another important temple that cannot be missed. The Wat Phrathat Chae Haeng is a sacred place for worship, situated on the eastern side of the Nan River.

From here, we head back to Nan Airport for your flight back to Bangkok (domestic tickets from Nan are not included in the program, we recommend an afternoon departure). No lunch is included on this day.

title.en: 6-Day Central and Northern Thailand Discovery Tour

overview: This 6-day tour showcases the best of central and northern Thailand. Whether you are a first time traveler or have been to Thailand numerous times this tour is bound to show you the immense diversity of this unique region. We have guaranteed departures each week.You will experience close-up the beauty and grace of Thailand. There is no other way to show you this amazing destination before going off to your next destination or hitting the beaches.
highlights: Multi-Day Trip
All entrance fees included
Travel by boat and see the sights from the water
expect: Day 1: Bangkok-Phitsanuloke

Early in the morning we drive to the grounds of the Bang Pa-In Summer Palace of King Rama V near Ayutthaya. Continuing by boat we reach the ancient city of Ayutthaya, which is one of the former capitals of the Siam Kingdom. After lunch at a riverside restaurant, we use the afternoon to reach Phitsanuloke. Upon arrival in Phitsanuloke we visit a private museum, representing Thai rural life from the past.
Day 2: Phitsanuloke-Lampang

Visit Phra Buddha Jinaraj at the Wat Pra Sri Rattana Maha Dhat and then head to Sukhothai. Visits include the Wat Sri Chum (‘The Temple of the Bodhi Tree’) and Sri Satchanalai Historical Park. We continue to the town of Lampang, where a tour around the old part of the city by horse-drawn carriage is included. Before checking in, stop for a walking tour to visit some of the most remarkable colonial style houses
Day 3: Lampang-Chiang Rai

Today starts early, as we bear witness and partake in the daily ritual of making merit at a nearby temple. After breakfast, we journey further north and make a stop at a local pineapple plantation. We travel further north via Phayao Lake to Chiang Rai, making coffee stops and enjoying lunch on the way. We continue to Chiang Saen, the former capital of the first Thai kingdom, where we board a long tail boat and sail up upriver on the Mekong to the Golden Triangle. Our journey then takes us to the border town of Mae Sai, in northernmost Thailand.
Day 4: Chiang Rai-Chiang

Mai Checkout from the hotel will 8am. Before leaving Chiang Rai, we stop at the famous Wat Rong Khun or ‘White Temple’. Along the way to Chiang Mai, a stop at the community-based tourism development center of Ban Lorcha can't be missed and then it is time for lunch. In the afternoon we stop at the San Khampaeng Handicraft Center where we observe artisans practicing the art of keeping this generation-old tradition alive. The evening is reserved for a “Khan Toke” dinner. During dinner, entertainers will perform traditional dances and songs by various hill tribes from the region
Day 5: Chiang Mai-Night train to Bangkok

We have selected a sustainable elephant camp outside of Chiang Mai, where visitors receive a demonstration of how mult-talented these trained animals are. A short visit to one of the local orchid farms shows you the variety of orchids from the area. Our next stop is Wat Phra Dhat Doi Suthep, the most sacred Chiang Mai temple which provides a superb view over the city. Head back into Chiang Mai and we transfer you to the train station to board the 5pm night train back to Bangkok (2nd class air-conditioned train with sleeping berths).
Day 6: Bangkok

We will arrive early in the morning at Bangkok’s Hua Lumpong Railway Station at approximately 6am and transfer to your hotel in Bangkok. This is where your journey of Central and Northern Thailand ends.

title.en: 7-Day Thailand Cultural and Lifestyle Tour

overview: This 7-day tour of mainland Thailand explores its natural and historical highlights, but also adds some off-the-path gems from central and northern Thailand. While much of the journey is by cool, air-conditioned vehicle, you'll also travel by boats, tuk tuk, and trishaw for an authentically Thai experience. Departing from Bangkok, you'll visit Ayutthaya, Sukhothai, Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai and more, help cultivate rice, visit an elephant camp, and discover Thailand's traditional Buddhist culture and handicrafts.
highlights: Multi-Day Trip
All entrance fees included
Led by a local guide
Free hotel pickup and drop-off included
expect: Your journey begins in Bangok and covers the ancient cities of Ayutthaya and Sukhotai, as well as Chiang Rai, Chiang Mai, and more. Along the way you'll visit elephant camps, caves, and orchid farms, ride tuk tuks and long-tail boats, explore Buddhist temples and hill-tribe villages, and discover a wealth of authentic Thai cuisine.
Itinerary
Day 1: Bangkok-Ayutthaya-Phitsanulok (L,D)

Depart at 6:30am for Ayutthaya to tour the remains of the ancient city using classic Thai tuk tuk three-wheelers. Next, you'll head to Lopburi to see the famous Monkey Temple and Prang Sam Yot before checking in to your hotel in the city of Phitsanulok. After dinner, clamber aboard a pedal-powered trishaw for an evening ride to the night market
Day 2: Phitsanulok-Sukhothai (B,L,D)

In Phitsanulok, you'll visit the Wat Mahathat, a royal temple that’s home to one of the most beautiful Buddha images in the country, before setting out by road for Sukhothai. You'll explore ancient Sukhothai before stopping at the Sangkhalok pottery village. End the day by visiting Si Satchanalai, the striking remains of the northern outpost of the historic Sukhothai Kingdom.
Day 3: Sukhothai-Lampang-Chiang Mai (B,L,D)

The day begins with a live presentation on rice cultivation: you have the chance to try your hand at growing rice. Next, you'll set out for Lampang, to see the Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, housing the only Emerald Buddha other than the one in Bangkok. Finally, you'll drive to Chiang Mai, Thailand's cultural capital, check in to your hotel and enjoy dinner at a riverside restaurant that doubles as an art gallery.
Day 4: Chiang Mai (B,L,D)

An early-morning visit to a nearby temple to give alms to the monks is common practice in Thailand's Buddhist culture: this morning you have the chance to join them. After breakfast, you'll drive the steep road to Wat Phra That Doi Suthep, a sacred temple with superb views over the city. Continue to the Talat Warorot, Chiang Mai’s largest market, and ride a rickshaw to Wat Chedi Luang, one of the city's most celebrated temples. In the San Kamphaeng handicraft district you'll watch artisans practicing ancient Thai arts and crafts, and keeping generations-old traditions alive. For dinner, you'll eat khan toke style, dining off low tables while seated on the floor, and watch traditional dance and song performances.
Day 5: Chiang Mai-Chiang Dao-Thaton (B,L,D)

The day begins with a drive to a sustainable elephant camp outside Chiang Mai: you'll learn how elephants are used in the timber industry, and their role in Thai heritage. A side-trip to a nearby orchid farm will give you a stunning impression of just a fraction of Thailand's rich variety of orchids. En route to your hotel in Thaton, you'll stop at the dramatic Chiang Dao cave complex.
Day 6: Thaton-Kok River-Chiang Rai (B,L,D)

Your first stop on the journey to Chiang Rai is the hill-tribe village and community center of Ban Lorcha, where you'll have the chance to witness traditional Akha lifestyles and buy handicrafts. From here, you'll drive to Ban Pha Tai and board motorized long-tail boats for the 3-hour journey down the Kok River. It's back on the road again to complete the journey to Chiang Rai, where you'll visit the famous Wat Rong Khun or White Temple and see the statue of King Mengrai who built Chiang Rai.
Day 7: Chiang Rai-Bangkok (B,L)

From Chiang Rai, you'll visit the famous Golden Triangle, where the borders of Thailand, Myanmar, and Laos meet, and enjoy a short boat ride before heading to Chiang Rai Airport for your Bangkok flight after lunch. The cost of the flight is not included, though transfer to your Bangkok hotel is. You are also free to end the tour in Chiang Rai.

title.en: 3-Day Discover Central Thailand Tour From Bangkok

overview: Leaving Bangkok behind you, the next 3 days will be spent exploring the diverse lifestyles and culture of Thailand's spectacular central region. With 2 night’s accommodation and meals included, this intimate tour takes in the simple life on the river, amazing temples and wetlands filled with wildlife.
highlights: Small-group tour
Informative, friendly and professional guide
See native wildlife in their natural environment
Travel by boat and see the sights from the water
expect: Day 1: Bangkok to Suphan Buri to Uthai Thani (D)

Depart Bangkok Hotels and drive north to Suphan Buri visiting the city pillar shrine, built in Chinese style, then continue to an orchid farm. Next stop is the 100 years old Sam Chuk riverside market - influenced by Chinese architecture, these modest shops are full of charm and character.

Enjoy exploring the market and be sure look out for the photograph shop which still takes pictures with a century-old camera and take some time for Thai coffee by the river. Then proceed to Wat Tasung Temple, the biggest and most famous temple in Uthai Thani, serving as Buddhist meditation center.

Enjoy a boat ride on the Sakaekrang River and relax as you watch "river life" in many forms. From typical raft houses of the local fishermen to their fish farms built on the river. Transfer to your accommodation, the Country Lake Nature Resort, surrounded by beautiful forest. Simple yet comfortable, these country style bungalows have private facilities, air condition and fan. / Overnight
Day 2: Ban Rai Village to Hub Patad (B,L)

After breakfast, drive to Ban Rai. Visit Wat Tham Khao Wong, a Buddhist temple built in 1987 with its two-story Thai-style hall and unique landscape. Further onwards is the Lao- Krang community, whose ancestors migrated from Laos hundred years ago and brought with them unique silk weaving tradition and patterns. Then proceed to Hub Pa Tad Valley, surrounded by the old limestone mountains. Explore the hidden forest of rare big palm trees that resemble "Jurassic Park" / Overnight
Day 3: Bung Boraphet Swamp to Ayutthaya to Bangkok (B,L)

After breakfast, proceed to Nakorn Sawan province, the gateway to the North of Thailand. Drive to Bung Boraphet, the largest single wetland site of Thailand. The area is a wonderful non-hunting bird sanctuary suitable for bird watching and sight-seeing. Enjoy a boat trip to spot many different wetland bird species and water plants such as water lilies and lotus flowers.

You will have an opportunity to visit the nearby aquarium and crocodile breeding pond. Then continue to the UNESCO world heritage site of Ayutthaya to visit the historical park. Visit the historic ruins of the temple Wat Yai Chai Mongkol before driving back to Bangkok. After lunch at a local restaurant you can transfer to your hotel in Bangkok or the airport.

title.en: 8-Day Burma Backdoor Explorer to Yangon from Bangkok

overview: Travel over 516 miles (832km) from the bustling city of Bangkok to Yangon, Myanmar (Burma). With accommodation, some meals and various modes of transportation included, this small group, 8 day tour, takes you through stunning untouched countryside and across the Thai – Burmese border.

Whilst there is no overall tour guide traveling with you, each leg of this spectacular journey is hosted by 'station guides' . These wonderful characters look after you until its time to hand you to the next 'station guide' as you move through your itinerary.
highlights: Cross the Thai - Burmese border
Kayak over rice fields
Hike to the Golden Rock
Small group ensures personal service
expect: Itinerary:
Day 1: Bangkok – Mae Sot
Meet your station guide at 8pm at New Road Guesthouse. Then set off to Bangkok’s Northern bus terminal. Settle in for your overnight journey to Mae Sot.
Day 2: Mae Sot – Hpa An, Myanmar (B)

5am arrival and after a quick fresh up and a bite to eat, you will be escorted to the Thailand- Myanmar border. On the other side at 8:30am, your driver takes you to Hpa An. Check in to your hotel then wander Hpa An’s small streets at your leisure. Stop for the local curries and the colorful fruit in stock.
Day 3: Hpa An (B)

A spectacular day kayaking through the rice fields with limestone mountains as the backdrop. You will meet local villagers and converse with the Kayin tribesman guide. Although no English, you are sure to feel welcomed by his huge smile. Make a very personal visit to another welcoming local villager's home for fresh fruit.
Next is Saddar Cave, the size of a football stadium, decorated with hundreds of Buddha figures, is a magnificent sight with pagodas and clay wall carvings.
Day 4: Hpa An – Mawlamyine (B)
Cruise along the Thanlwin river, stopping at the U Na Auk village. With your station guide, you will be greeted by dozens of children, curious to learn more of the foreign guest in their village.
Day 5: Mawlamyine (B)
Free day to roam at your leisure and own expense.
Day 6: Mawlamyine – Kyaiktiyo – Kinpun (B)
Board the train to Kyaiktiyo and take advantage of the time available to interact with friendly locals. Upon arrival into Kyaiktiyo hire a Tuk Tuk to Kinpun, where you will overnight.
Day 7: Kinpun - Yangon (B)
Visit to The Golden Rock, hanging on its tip, high above the plains. Take the afternoon bus from Kinpun to Yangon.
Day 8: Yangon (B)
At your leisure. After check out, continue your journey according to your own plans. Notices

title.en: 7-Night Northern Thailand Tour: Sukhothai, Lampang and Chiang Mai from Bangkok

overview: Depart Bangkok for 7-night tour of northern Thailand to experience a land of vast culture and exquisite natural scenery. You’ll explore the many wonders of Chiang Mai, Thailand’s northern capital, visit the temples of Lampang, tour the ancient ruins of Sukhothai Historical Park on two wheels and enjoy a meal with dancing. A highlight of this multi-day guided journey is a stop at the Friends of the Asian Elephant organziation, where you’ll learn how you can help care for these magnificent creatures. Round-trip transport from Bangkok is included.
highlights: 7-night northern Thailand tour, round-trip from Bangkok
Visit the gorgeous temple of Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai) in Phitsanulok
Take a bicycle tour of ancient ruins in the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Sukhothai
Historical Park and visit the Sukhothai night market
Visit the Friends of the Asian Elephant organization and learn how you can help these animals
Enjoy a homestay with khantohk dinner and dancing in a local Thai village
Soak in thermal hot springs near Chiang Mai and relax at leisure in the northern capital
Small-group tour limited to 16 people ensures a personalized experience with your expert guide
expect: Your exciting journey through northern Thailand includes travel by minibus, songthaew (open pickup truck), taxi and train, plus round-trip airport transport (if option selected). Enjoy seven nights accommodation including single or twin-share rooms at 2- to 3-star hotels, a guesthouse, a homestay and a sleeper train from Chiang Mai to Bangkok. With plenty of free time built into your itinerary, you can explore Thailand’s northern highlights at a leisurely pace!
Itinerary
Day 1: Bangkok

Start your northern Thailand adventure in Bangkok with a welcome meeting at 6pm. Arrive at your hotel at any time, as there are no activities planned prior to your evening orientation with your guide. Please look for a note in the hotel lobby or ask reception where it will take place. If you’ve chosen to upgrade your tour to include a round-trip airport transfer, a tour representative will meet you at the airport and transport you to your accommodation in Bangkok.

It is recommended that you arrive early to explore Thailand's magnificent capital. Located on the banks of the Chao Phraya River, Bangkok is famous for its tuk tuks, canals and street vendors serving up delicious Thai food. Consider taking a riverboat to explore the bustling streets of Chinatown, visiting the stunning Grand Palace and its Emerald Buddha, watching a Thai kickboxing match or simply indulging in a Thai massage in preparation for the journey ahead. / Overnight
Day 2: Bangkok – Sukhothai

Board a train for an approximate six-hour ride north to Phitsanulok. En route, get to know fellow travelers in your small group as you take in the scenery of the Thai countryside. Upon arrival in Phitsanulok, visit Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai) -- one of Thailand’s most important and beautiful temples, known for its 14th-century bronze Buddha image cast with a flame-like halo.

After touring the temple with your guide, board a songthaew for the exciting one-hour journey to Sukhothai. Established as Siam’s first capital in the 13th century, Sukhothai is a friendly town with a wealth of fabulous sights to see, including the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Sukhothai Historical Park, which showcases some of the most impressive ruins in Thailand. Relax in the tranquil town of Sukhothai, set amid leafy forests, perfumed gardens and fertile rice paddies on a fertile plain. If you’d like, head to the fascinating night market and try a local dish such as Sukhothai noodles, fried rice or even fried insects! Or, enjoy some pampering at Sukhothai's herbal sauna and massage center. / Overnight
Day 3: Sukhothai – Lampang (B, L)

Board another songthaew for an approximate 30-minute ride to the historical ruins of Old Sukhothai, set amid beautiful lakes and gardens. Upon arrival at Sukhothai Historical Park, hop on a bicycle and enjoy a few leisurely hours touring the site. Ride past four large ponds often filled with stunning lotus flowers in full bloom, and learn about Thailand’s Golden Age from your guide.

Admire the Sukhothai-era religious art and architecture – including the ruins of 21 historical sites with awe-inspiring Buddha images – considered to be the most classic of Thai styles. Along the way, you’ll stop for a home-cooked picnic lunch and visit a local ceramics factory if there’s enough time.

Afterward, embark on a three-hour bus trip to Lampang, a northern Thai city where you can still ride a horse and cart for transport. Check out Lampang’s interesting temples, such as Wat Phra That Lampang Luang, or relax in one of its great bars. / Overnight
Day 4: Lampang (D)

Visit the Friends of the Asian Elephant organization, a private group that aims to protect and conserve the welfare of both domesticated and wild Asian elephants. Here, you will learn about the living conditions of these animals and what you can do to encourage and promote their humane treatment.

After you disembark, your guide will take your small group to a small Thai village, located approximately 1.5 hours from the elephant center. Experience a warm welcome at your homestay and get a first-hand look at Thai rural life. Enjoy a traditional northern Thai khantohk dinner – a customary northern Thai style of dining with food served in large platters at low tables – accompanied by live music and traditional Thai dancing. / Overnight
Days 5-7: Lampang – Chiang Mai – Bangkok (Day 5 - B, L)

Rise early to offer alms to the monks before traveling by songthaew to nearby thermal hot springs, where you can soak in the mineral pools or enjoy a traditional Thai massage. After your relaxing morning, continue to Chiang Mai, located about 40 minutes away. Known for its beauty and the friendliness of the local people, Chiang Mai is awash with stunning temples, fabulous markets and a lively city center. Situated at the crossroads of one of Southeast Asia's most important trade routes, Thailand's northern capital is a legendary center of ancient culture.

Enjoy hours of free time exploring Chiang Mai: go on a cycling tour, riding to gold-gilded temples; visit the hilltop temple of Doi Suthep for stunning views over the city; attend a Thai cooking class; browse the crafts markets; or take a river tour aboard a bamboo raft. On your final evening in Chiang Mai, board an overnight train for the 13-hour ride to Bangkok. In your soft sleeper-class train, settle into your air-conditioned multi-share compartment and bunk bed. Sheets and a pillow are provided, and food and drink service are available for purchase aboard the train. / Overnight
Day 8: Bangkok

Arrive in Bangkok in the early morning and transfer back to Viengtai Hotel to conclude your trip through northern Thailand. You are free to depart at any time, with shared day rooms available for use until noon. Perhaps you’ll stay a few extra days to explore Thailand’s amazing capital

title.en: 3-Day River Kwai Tour from Bangkok: Ayutthaya, Kanchanaburi and Thai-Burma Death Railway

overview: See the ancient temples of UNESCO-listed Ayutthaya, the royal summer palace at Bang Pa- In, and the terraced waterfalls of Erawan National Park — all on this 3-day small-group tour from Bangkok. Stay overnight in Kanchanaburi on the River Kwai, where your guide highlights the region’s World War II history. You’ll visit the War Museum, the Allied War Cemetery and the Thailand–Burma 'Death Railway’ Hellfire Pass Memorial Museum. With numbers limited to 12 people, you’ll receive undivided attention from the guide.
highlights: 3-day tour of western Thailand, round-trip from Bangkok by minivan
Admire temples in the ancient capital of Ayutthaya, a UNESCO World Heritage Site
Dip into rock pools at Erawan National Park and view Erawan Falls
Cross the famous bridge over the River Kwai
Learn about the Thailand-Burma 'Death Railway’ at Hellfire Pass and the Allied War
Cemetery
Take a saamlaw (tricycle rickshaw) tour around Kanchanaburi
Small-group tour limited to 12 people ensures personal attention from your guide
expect: This comprehensive journey into western Thailand covers three fascinating days with a knowledgable guide. Step into Thailand’s ancient past at Ayutthaya Historical Park, a temple- strewn World Heritage site, and witness the remnants of WWII along the River Kwai’s Thailand–Burma Death Railway.
You’ll travel with a small group by minivan, round-trip from Bangkok, and stay two nights in Kanchanaburi with 2–3-star accommodation (including two breakfasts and two lunches). Itinerary
Day 1: Bangkok – Kanchanaburi (L)

After pickup from your hotel in the morning, travel by minibus with your small group to Bang Pa-In, just 37 miles (60 kms) north of Bangkok. The royal summer palace, a former residence for Thai kings, is situated on the banks of the Chao Phraya River. Your knowledgeable local guide will conduct a tour of the magnificent grounds and lovely gardens set around an ornamental pond. Admire the combination of European and Thai architecture and the topiaries shaped into elephants.

Next, head to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Ayutthaya, an ancient capital of Siam, to see impressive ruins once destroyed by the Burmese. At Ayutthaya Historical Park, explore several temples such as Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon, where you may be told your fortune by a fortuneteller.

Then, visit Wat Phanan Cheoeng, one of Ayutthaya's oldest temples — often compared to the Taj Mahal — where a 62-foot-high (19-meter-high) Buddha image resides. Your guide will point out an 18th-century shrine and tell you about the Chinese princess in whose honor it was built.

After a delicious Thai lunch, visit the ruins of the 13th-century Wat Phra Mahathat, which includes an ancient Buddha head statue surrounded by Banyan tree roots. You’ll enjoy many photo opportunities before heading west to Kanchanaburi — an approximate four-hour drive — and checking in to your hotel. For your dinner, your guide will happily provide suggestions of local restaurants. / Overnight
Day 2: Kanchanaburi – River Kwai (B, L)

After breakfast, your guide will take your small group by minivan to the Hellfire Pass Memorial Museum. As you read the inscriptions and tour the exhibit, learn about the allied POWs and Asian laborers who perished at Hellfire Pass while they constructed the Thailand- Burma Death Railway during WWII.

Next, head to nearby Erawan National Park, home to seven gorgeous waterfalls — including the terraced Erawan Falls — and a series of turquoise rock pools. Your guide will recommend the best pools for swimming, where you can take a refreshing dip. Or, embark on one-hour hike to the seventh and highest story of one waterfall for amazing views. At the park, enjoy a Thai-style picnic lunch before returning to Kanchanaburi in the late afternoon to relax. Don’t miss a sunset stroll across the famous bridge over the River Kwai, part of the Death Railway constructed by allied prisoners of war. In the evening, you’ll have the option to visit Kanchanaburi's night market to try a variety of Thai dishes for dinner. . / Overnight
Day 3: Kanchanaburi – Bangkok (B)

After breakfast, enjoy a sightseeing tour around Kanchanaburi aboard a traditional saamlaw (tricycle rickshaw), visiting several historical sites along the way. See the WWII War Museum and the Allied War Cemetery, and cross the bridge over the River Kwai before retuning by minivan to your Bangkok hotel, where your trip ends in the late afternoon.

title.en: 2-Day Tour Cycling Khao Yai Wine Trails from Bangkok

overview: Escape Bangkok’s bustle for a serene, 2-day cycling tour of Khao Yai’s wine, food and farms. Stroll through tropical vineyards, sample wines and linger over traditional Thai meals as you ride a gentle, 23.5-mile (38 kilometer) route that’s fully supported by an air-conditioned van. Sleep at a mountain resort that supports community development, pedal past sugar and tapioca fields and duck into the hushed sanctuaries of rural Buddhist temples. Visit the Prapatsorn grape farm, enjoy a hearty lunch then take a final spin along the broad Asoke valley.
highlights: Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Ideal choice for families
Romantic experience, perfect for couples

expect: Ideal for couples, families, and anyone who enjoys good food, good wine, and stunning nature. Cycling Khao Yai Wine Trails takes you on a wine tasting journey where we ride a total of 23.5mi (38km) on quiet country roads through rolling hills with mountainous backdrops, passing quaint dairy farms and remote temples along the way, and visit Khao Yai's fruitful vineyards where we break for a taste of local wine and take in the breathtaking scenery of the Thai countryside.

From Bangkok we drive north and east and start our trip by visiting the impressive 147ft (45m) tall white Buddha statue at Wat Theppitak Punnaram. We ride through patchwork countryside that could almost be France, if it wasn't for the banana trees and occasional coconut palm. We visit the birthplace of the acclaimed Khao Yai wine, which is locally grown and processed in a stunning valley plain sitting at an elevation of 1150ft (350m) above sea level, and just a short bicycle ride away from the serene Khao Yai National Park. After a well- deserved lunch paired with a glass of wine, we take a tour of the wine making facilities and vineyard before riding to our resort.

We spend the night at the charming Cabbages & Condoms resort, surrounded by majestic limestone mountains and nature at its very best. Owned by the Population, Community and Development Association, a Thai government organization set up by Khun Meechai Viravaidya, the PDA operates a wide variety of programs designed to serve and assist the rural poor of Thailand. These programs cover such diverse activities as free vasectomies, income generation programs at village level, forest replanting schemes, vegetable banks, industry relocation into rural areas, mobile health clinics, environmental education programs, and a democracy project.

On our second day we will be climbing a bit on the bike as well as off the bike as we make our way to the very top of two stunning temples and later, cycle uphill as we pass tapioca and sugar cane fields and a rock quarry. We break and enjoy refreshments at the Prapatsorn grape farm before a hearty lunch is in order. Afterwards we ride through Asoke Valley before heading back to Bangkok (two hour air-conditioned van transfer). An air-conditioned minivan travels behind the group to support us and participants can cycle as much or as little as they like and still enjoy the same views as the rest of the group. This is a 2-Day/1-Night tour with breakfast-1, lunch-2 and dinner-1 included.

overview: Pedal through the best of central Thailand on a 4-day bicycle tour from Bangkok. Follow a scenic, 75-mile (120-kilometer) route: ride alongside canals to the vibrant Damnoen Saduak floating market and visit Kanchanaburi’s poignant World War II-era sites. Cycle through the majestic ruins of Ayutthaya and travel along jade-colored rice paddies to Bang Pa In, where the ancient Siamese King’s spent the summer months. title.en: 5-Day Kanchanaburi Family Adventures by Bike

overview: Discover Kanchanaburi’s vivid history and landscape on a 5- day bicycle tour that’s an unforgettable family adventure.

Follow a 71-mile (114-kilometer) route along gentle country roads, canals and rice paddies to visit Khmer temples and World War II-era sites, include the infamous ‘Death Railway.’ Immerse yourself in rural Thai life at the village of Ban Nong Khao, and spend a day with the elephants in a local sanctuary. Enjoy the full support of an air-conditioned minivan so you can ride as much, or little, as you’d like.
highlights: Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Ideal choice for families

expect: Take a break from the busy city life and bring your family on a fun 5-day cycling trip to Kanchanaburi on this fun. This action-filled tour takes you on an exploration of some of Thailand's best historic attractions, such as Wat Prasat Muang Singh, a 12th-century Khmer temple and the memorable and historic Hellfire Pass.

We cycle on scenic country back roads, surrounded buy majestic limestone mountains and refreshing rivers, along irrigation canals and through vibrant green rice paddies. Visit the cultural village of Ban Nong Khao and explore the rural Thai's way of life, hop on a train and travel on the infamous death railway built by prisoners of war during WWII, and spend a memorable day with elephants at a sanctuary for sick, old, abused and former street elephants. With its variety and diversity of activities, Kanchanaburi has certainly become a haven for adventure seekers, nature lovers and those seeking peace and serenity. We cycle a total of 71mi (114km) over the course of 5 days and visit famous sites and interesting places off the beaten path, exposing you to true Thailand, and turning this trip into the perfect getaway for active families.

An air-conditioned minivan travels behind the group to support us and participants can cycle as much or as little as they like and still enjoy the same views as the rest of the group. This 5- Day/4-Night tour includes breakfast-4, lunch-5 and dinner-4.

title.en: 3-Day Tour Exploring the Golden Triangle by Bike

overview: Explore the Golden Triangle by bike on a 3-day tour from Chiang Rai, and discover the former heart of the ancient opium trade. Trace a 73-mile (118-kilometer) route along country roads with the support an air-conditioned van as you pedal to the Mekong river town of Chiang Saen, learn the history of the region’s drug trade at the Opium Museum and experience rural life in an isolated Thai village. Ride through the border country of Chiang Khong, where Thailand, Laos and Myanmar converge in a verdant landscape.
highlights: Ideal choice for families
Romantic experience, perfect for couples
Instant Confirmation
Multi-Day Trip
Perfect for all ages and skill level
expect: This Golden Triangle Adventure Tour by Bike is a wonderful way to explore the famous area known as Sop Ruak, the official center of the Golden Triangle. It is here in Chiang Rai where the Nam Ruak and Mekong rivers meet, and where the area has for centuries served as the crossroads for border trade between Thailand, Burma and Laos. We start the trip from Chiang Rai, the most northerly of all the 76 Thai provinces, and cycle north towards our hotel, which is located on the beautiful Mekong River. After checking into our hotel we head out for a cool afternoon ride through the scenic countryside and to the ancient river town of Chiang Saen.

We set out after breakfast the next morning and visit the Opium Museum which documents the history of opium trade. We then follow the Mekong River towards Chiang Khong, taking in expansive views over the Mekong, the natural border that separates Thailand from Laos. Our third and final day we ride west towards Chiang Rai to areas usually overlooked by most visitors, and experience true Thai village life on the way.

We cycle a total of 73mi (118km) over the course of three days, and will be fully supported by an air-conditioned vehicle that has been specially modified for cycle tours. The vehicle follows us the whole time and it is very easy to get bikes on and off, so you can rest when you are tired and cycle whenever you feel like it. This 3-Day/2-Night tour includes breakfast-2, lunch-3 and dinner-2

title.en: 3-Day Hua Hin Bike Tour from Bangkok

overview: Pedal through market scenes, mountain scenery and the azure coast of Hua Hin on a 3-day bicycle tour from Bangkok. Ride 58-miles (94-kilometers) with support from an air-conditioned van as you explore three dramatically diverse regions: visit the Damnoen Saduak floating market, trace the scenic trails of Kaeng Krachan and cycle through Hua Hin’s seaside fishing villages. Enjoy a gentle pace throughout the trip, as well as frequent stops to discover shimmering temples and mountain lakes, or linger in the shade of a tropical orchard.
highlights: Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Excellent value for money
Ideal choice for families
Romantic experience, perfect for couples
Instant Confirmation
Multi-Day Trip
expect: Only a few hours South of the capital city lies a green fertile lowland with a network of canals, orchards and a huge forest reserve – a peaceful land and lifestyle that is an important facet of Thailand that most visitors do not get a chance to experience. We start our 3-day cycling adventure by visiting the Damnoen Saduak floating market where we take a long tail boat ride through the network of canals towards Wat Amphawan Chetiyaram temple. We ride along scenic back roads, cycling through coconut plantations, fruitful orchards and stunning temples, finishing at a canalside hotel where we check in for the night.

Day two of cycling starts after breakfast on quiet traffic-free trails surrounded by beautiful scenery as we enter Kaeng Krachan National Park. We cycle over a large dam and alongside a crystalline lake, and spend our second night at a secluded hotel in the hills where we will have free time for a swim or massage before dinner.

On our third and final day we cycle through quaint fishing villages, passing local schools and temples, and ride along the coast for excellent views of the sea. We arrive at Khao Kalok and lunch at a local restaurant before transferring back to Bangkok. We ride a total of 58mi (94km) over the course of three days, and are fully supported by an air-conditioned minivan which travels behind the group, allowing participants to cycle as much or as little as they like and still enjoy the same views as the rest of the group. title.en: 5-Day Golden Triangle Tour

overview: Set out to explore Thailand’s Golden Triangle on a private, 5-day tour from Bangkok. Travel from the Mekong River to mountain highlands, step to the edge of the Thai-Myanmar border and meet locals in isolated hill tribe villages. Board a longtail boat for a journey on the scenic Kok River, and discover Thailand’s extraordinary cultural diversity; encounter Hmong, Akha and Meo people, each with distinctive dances, language, costume and handicrafts. Visit elephants at home, watch artisans weave silk, and take in the Golden Triangles most iconic temples and vivid markets.
highlights: Enjoy fantastic aerial views
Family friendly

expect: Tuesday

Depart Bangkok by flight (airfare is not included) Arrive Chiang Mai Airport. Drive to Chiang Rai and lunch at local restaurant. Continue to Chiang Saen, former capital of the first Thai Kingdom, situated directly on Mekong River at border between Thailand and Laos. Visit Wat Phra Dhat Jom Kitti by climbing 383 steps to top of hill. Also visit Wat Chedi Luang and small museum nearby. Continue by longtail speedboat upriver on the Mekong toward Golden Triangle where borders of Thailand, Myanmar and Laos meet. Check in at imperial golden triangle or similar hotel.
Wednesday

Depart from Chiang Saen Visit Lisu Village at Ban Mae Kaotom and continue to Yao and Akha hilltribe village. Proceed to Doi Mae Salong, passing through beautiful mountain scenery. View takes in a stunning view of Thailand, Myanmar and the Mekong Valley. Lunch at Mae Salong Villa in Doi Mae Salong. Depart Doi Mae Salong to Mae Sai, the northernmost Thai town on the Myanmar border. Walk around local market with opportunity for shopping. Before returning to Chiang Rai, short stop at fish cave. Check in at the legend chiang rai boutique river resort & spa or similar hotel.
Thursday
Leave hotel for boat landing.

Board simple longtail motorboats for three-hour journey up Kok River, passing tiny hilltribe villages, bamboo huts and jungle scenery. Disembark at Ban Pha Tai and continue by bus to visit Ban Lorcha, a Phami Akha hilltribe community center. This community-based tourism development project promotes sustainable, self-reliant development to improve the quality of life of villagers of this Akha Community, and is a model for tourism in Hilltribe villages. Lunch at local restaurant. Proceed to Mae Rim via Fang and Chiang Dao. Continue to Hmong Hilltribe Lodge.
Dinner followed by presentation of Meo dances and overnight stay.
Friday

Drive to elephant Camp watch elephants taking timber in forest. Their strength and strategic teamwork will amaze you. Continue visit to orchid farm and lunch at local restaurant. Afternoon visit to Handicraft Villages to see manufacture of lacquer-ware, spinning and weaving of Thai Silk and watch how paper umbrellas are made. Visit a well-known Thai wood-carving factory, with possibility of buying Burmese antiques. Check in at Furama Chiang Mai hotel or similar hotel.
Saturday

City Tour Visit the most interesting temples in Chiang Mai, like Wat Phra Singh with its famous Buddha image, Wat Chiang Man, oldest temple in Chiang Mai and built by King Mangrai, and Wat Suan Dok, housing remains of many generations of the old Chiang Mai Royal Family. Visit Wat Doi Suthep, tucked away in the mountains at 1,056 meters above sea level. Lunch at local restaurant. Transfer to Chiang Mai Airport.
