title.en: 5-Day Wild Jungle Ranger Adventure Tour from Bangkok

overview: Take on the ultimate jungle adventure on a 5-day tour from Bangkok to Khao Yai National Park. Explore the UNESCO World Heritage-listed reserve with an experienced ranger as you trek across the rugged terrain, sleep beneath the stars and swim in lush waterfall pools. Eat rustic camp meals and dine at the park’s ecolodge where you’ll relax before and after your trek, and learn about wildlife conservation. Learn the names of jungle plants in the untouched reserve, where you’ll spot elephants, macaques and barking deer in their natural habitat.
highlights: Get up-close to native wildlife
Led by a local guide
See native wildlife in their natural environment
Small group ensures personal service
Multi-Day Trip
expect: Khao Yai National Park is part of a UNESCO World Heritage–listed wilderness where there are still occasional sightings of wild animals like elephants, leopards, tigers, bears, otters, barking deer, gibbons, macaques, pythons and many colorful birds. Your 5-day tour in Khao Yai National Park includes two nights of accommodation at Eco Valley Lodge and two nights of tent camping during your trek. You’ll hike with experienced guides who were once poachers and are now committed to wildlife conservation. Camping gear such as a flashlight, compass, backpack, hammock, sleeping bag and cooking equipment is provided, and you can store extra luggage at the lodge during the trek. The trek is suitable for people with a good level of fitness. Expect to hike for several hours each day while carrying your own backpack, taking trails that cross uneven terrain and elevation changes; hiking shoes that can get wet are recommended for river crossings. You will help with setting up camp and preparing simple meals during the trek. All meals during the trek and breakfasts at the lodge are included; you can purchase additional meals at the lodge’s open-air restaurant. During your free time, enjoy the lodge's swimming pool and gardens, and perhaps treat yourself to a massage treatment (own expense). Itinerary
Day 1: Pak Chong – Khao Yai National Park

In the morning, make your own way to Pak Chong, located about 100 miles (160 km) from Bangkok. Upon arrival, you'll be picked up at the bus or train station and transferred to Eco Valley Lodge. After checking in, have time to eat lunch and relax before taking a bike ride with a guide to see nearby farmland and foothills. Spend the evening at your leisure, and get ready for an early start in the morning. / Overnight
Day 2: Trekking (B, L, D)

Have an early breakfast at the lodge before you meet your trekking guide, who provides a briefing and your camping gear. When your gear is packed, start hiking from a small village on the edge of Khao Yai National Park. Ascend for about three hours through evergreen forests and open grassland until you arrive at a ridge with breathtaking views. During the day, you’ll have plenty of time to swim and splash in waterfalls and natural pools. At night, set up camp with your guides, and fall asleep to the sounds of the jungle. / Overnight
Day 3: Trekking (B, L, D)

Begin your first full day in the remote jungle by having breakfast, preparing lunch for later and packing up camp. When ready, set off with your guides through beautiful sections of the forest, learning about the plants and wildlife that you see. Spend the evening near a towering waterfall that has two levels with deep and shallow pools. You can swim at the waterfall, the perfect way to refresh yourself after a day on the trail. . / Overnight
Day 4: End of trek (B, L)

Today you’ll follow a river valley through a lesser-known section of Khao Yai National Park. Enjoy great photo opportunities, and be prepared to get your feet wet, as you will be crossing the river several times. Have lunch next to the river, and then complete the final part of your trek in the afternoon. At the end, you will be picked up and transferred back to the lodge. Bid your trekking guide farewell, and spend the rest of the evening at your leisure. / Overnight
Day 5 : Khao Yai National Park – Pak Chong – Bangkok (B)

Sleep in if you wish and have breakfast when you wake up. Check out of the lodge by noon, and then you will be transferred back to Pak Chong and provided with a bus ticket to Bangkok (Mo Chit or Victory Monument stations) to end your tour. / Overnight

title.en: 8-Day Central Thailand Adventure from Bangkok

overview: This 8-day Thailand Adventure starts in Bangkok and visits the most beautiful palaces and temples. Experience a cycle ride through hidden alleys, dine on board a cruise and see the famous Floating Market. We visit Ayutthaya, Thailand's former capital city, destroyed in 1767 during the war with Burma. At the River Kwai you will stay in a fairy tale floating hotel lit with candles. This tour ends on the beaches of Hua Hin.
highlights: Flexibility to customize your itinerary to your own preferences
Family friendly
Breakfast included
Perfect for all ages and skill level
expect: This 8 day tour will give you a great insight into Bangkok and central Thailand. All accommodation and meals are included where indicated. Our guide and the tours listed are also included.
Itinerary
Day 1-4: Arrive in Bangkok and transfer to your hotel.

The rest of the day is free. The following morning we visit Bangkok's most famous landmarks: the Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew with the Emerald Buddha and dine on a river cruise boat, an old rebuilt rice barge. During a quiet romantic candle lit tour you can enjoy the traditional Kim (Thai xylophone) music.

On day three we explore Bangkok by bicycle. This tour will take you to places hardly visited by tourists. You will ride through markets and little alleys. Take a boat trip across the Chao Phraya river and continue your tour through a green landscape scattered by fruit plantations and typical Thai style houses. Listen to the singing birds and get a friendly hello from everyone you meet. No cars, no traffic jams.

The following day we go to Ayutthaya & River Kwai. We visit the most important ruins and remaining historical attractions of Ayutthaya. Back to Bangkok by cruise boat over the mighty Chao Phraya river.
Day 5:

Drive through the rural landscapes outside Bangkok towards Kanchanaburi and the River Kwai. A long tail boat first takes you to the famous Floating Market of Damnoen Saduak. See, feel and smell the old style and traditional way of selling and buying vegetables and fruits from small boats. Visit the Bridge over the River Kwai in Kanchanaburi, the Jeath war museum and the war cemetery. A long tail boat will take you, along the River Kwai, to a floating hotel. This place is magic. The floating bungalows are built on bamboo-rafts surrounded by magnificent jungle.

The accommodation is basic with private bath and shower. There is no electricity but oil lamps and a very cosy atmosphere. See Burmese Mon dancing or take a swim in the river. Overnight on the River Kwai.
Day 6:

Visit the wonderful waterfalls in the Erawan National Park. The falls cover 7 levels over 1550 meters. They belong to the most beautiful falls in Thailand. You can walk up to all 7 levels. The highest levels require some creative walking but the climb is more than worth the effort. You can swim at various locations. Around the park there are various caves with impressive and sometimes bizarre stone formations. In the early afternoon you will take a train ride on the famous Death railway. The scenery is stunning, especially over the bridge itself. Make sure that you have your cameras ready. Onward to Hua Hin. You will arrive at your hotel in Hua Hin in the early evening.
Day 7 and 8:

Hua Hin. Two free days in Hua Hin to enjoy the beach and the sun. On day 8 you will travel comfortably by private air-conditioned minivan to Bangkok's international airport. There you will arrive on time for your connecting flight back home. This tour ends upon arrival into Bangkok.

overview: This Flight of the Gibbon treetop adventure is an ideal introduction to a thrilling zipline experience near Chonburi. With the assistance of two guides per group of nine, you’ll soar through a pristine rainforest on one of the longest and highest zipline courses in the world. Enjoy premium views from 24 platforms, plus scenic sky bridges and adrenaline-inducing rappelling. Thai lunch and Khao Kheow Open Zoo access are included on this full-day tour with round-trip transport from Bangkok.
highlights: Flight of the Gibbon treetop adventure at Khao Kheow
Soar to 24 platform stations on Thailand’s highest zipline course
Travel across two hanging sky bridges and rappel down two descents
Enjoy a Thai lunch and tram tour around Khao Kheow Open Zoo

Considered one of the largest canopy ziplines in the world, the course includes two hanging sky bridges and two rock faces to rappel down. Back on firm ground, eat a provided Thai lunch followed by a visit to Khao Kheow Open Zoo aboard a tram. Stop at various tram stations to watch the animal shows, feed the wildlife and explore the exhibits. See exotic birds display their talents and be captivated by wild cats among the more than 300 animal species in the 2,000-acre (810-hectare) wildlife park. Complete your full-day tour with drop-off at the starting point in Bangkok.

title.en: 5-Night Umphang Trekking Tour from Bangkok

overview: Embark on a 5-night tour from Bangkok to the jungles of Thailand’s Umphang district for a multi-day trekking adventure. This active excursion forgoes creature comforts for one-of-a-kind experiences. Camp overnight in a Karen hill tribe village close to the Myanmar (Burma) border, and hike through tropical wilderness. The beauty of rural Thailand awaits on this guided group tour with no more than 10 participants.
highlights: 5-night tour from Bangkok to the Umphang district
Travel to the border towns of Mae Sot and Umphang, where Karen people are the dominant ethnic group
Spend three days trekking through the jungle wilderness
Admire the immense Thi Loi Su waterfall and take a refreshing dip in its pools
Stay overnight in a Karen village homestay, a tent campsite and simple guesthouses
Small-group tour with a maximum of 10 people ensures a more customized experience with a knowledgeable guide
expect: This action-packed trekking tour and cultural adventure includes three days of hiking through mountainous jungle terrain at a moderate level of difficulty. As you must carry your own backpack and belongings, a decent level of fitness is required to participate. Accommodation includes one night at a homestay in a Karen hill tribe village, where living conditions are basic. You'll also spend your nights on an overnight drive by luxury bus, a campsite in Umphang Wildlife Sanctuary, a simple hut and a local guesthouse. You may store any extra luggage during the trekking portion in order to lighten your load. Itinerary
Day 1: Bangkok – Mae Sot

Meet a tour representative in the evening in central Bangkok, and head to the to the Northern Bus Terminal where you'll be escorted to a VIP luxury bus for the overnight journey to Mae Sot. The bus ride is unguided. / Overnight
Day 2: Mae Sot – Umphang (B, L, D)

When you arrive in Mae Sot, your local guide meets your bus to welcome you. You have a couple of hours to nap or freshen up at a nearby guesthouse (basic shared accommodation), and then take a short ride to a market on the Thailand-Myanmar border next to the Moi River. Have lunch at the market and enjoy the opportunity to try some authentic Thai-Burmese dishes before hopping in a songthaew (truck taxi) for the drive to Umphang. The journey takes about four hours and includes numerous twists and turns on a road that winds through the dense green foliage of the mountains (anti-motion-sickness pills can come in handy!). Your accommodation tonight consists of basic huts. / Overnight
Day 3: Umphang town – Umphang Wildlife Sanctuary (B, L, D)

After breakfast, your guide provides a safety briefing and instruction for your rafting excursion on the Mae Klong River. Pass by tall limestone cliffs, dense jungle and bamboo trees as you glide downriver; after a few hours, disembark to start trekking along a trail that leads through the jungle. Your guide shares informative commentary on the plant and animal life around you as you hike.

After about four hours of trekking, arrive at your campsite, located in Umphang Wildlife Sanctuary. Your guide pitches tents and cooks dinner, and you spend the evening relaxing under the stars. / Overnight
Day 4: Umphang Wildlife Sanctuary – Ko Tha (B, L, D)

In the morning, take a short hike to towering Thi Loi Su waterfall, the largest waterfall in Southeast Asia, measuring up to 1,640 feet (500 meters) high. Bring a towel and swimming gear for a dip in the pools formed by the waterfall, and then continue walking through bamboo forests and until you reach the village of Ko Tha, a Karen ethnic hill tribe settlement. Spend the night in a traditional Karen home with a local host family. Your guide explains Karen traditions and history, and helps translate so that you can talk with the villagers that you meet. / Overnight
Day 5: Ko Tha – Mae Sot (B, L, D)

Wake up to a scrumptious jungle breakfast. Then say farewell to your village hosts and tackle the final section of your trek: about three hours of walking along the river to the town of Palatha. From there, take a songthaew back to Umphang where you have the option to shower before returning to Mae Sot. The bus from Mae Sot to Bangkok leaves at 8pm. Your guide will not join the overnight bus. / Overnight
Day 6: Mae Sot – Bangkok (B)
Expected arrival on the Northern bus station Mochit early morning around 5.30am. The tour ends at the bus station and from here you continue your own journey.

overview: Visit enthralling temple ruins in the Historic City of Ayutthaya, a UNESCO World Heritage site, on this private day trip from Bangkok. Travel with your own personal guide to the ancient Thai capital and visit one of its long-standing markets along with an elephant sanctuary. This full-day itinerary packs in culture and cuisine, including lunch on a docked rice barge and traditional food tastings of local specialties. Round-trip hotel transport by air-conditioned minivan is included.

expect: After pickup from your Bangkok hotel, get comfortable in your private minivan for the drive to the ancient capital of Ayutthaya. Your tour begins at one of Ayutthaya’s oldest markets where you'll sample traditional boat noodles from a local vendor, among other authentic bites. Next, visit emblematic temples, such as Wat Yai Chai Mongkol with its 196-foot-tall (60- meter) stupa. See the ancient ruins of Buddha images at Wat Mahathat (Temple of the Great Relics), and stop by Ayutthaya’s most historically important temple, Wat Phra Si Sanphet. Then savor lunch aboard a docked rice barge on the Chao Phraya River. In the afternoon, visit Ayutthaya Historical Park, home to Wat Chai Wattanaram, one of Ayutthaya's most renowned temples. Go behind the scenes of the production of roti sai mai to see how this spun sugar dessert is made and taste some yourself. Then discover another local snack at a temple market. Your day trip ends with return by private vehicle to Bangkok for hotel drop-off.

title.en: Private Tour: Full-Day Bangkok City Tour

overview: Book this full-day Bangkok City Tour to visit some of the most amazing destinations including Temple of the Golden Buddha (Wat Traimit), Pak Khlong Talat (Flower Market), Grand Palace, Temple of the Emerald Buddha (Wat Phra Kaew), The Chao Phraya River, Temple of Dawn (Wat Arun) and many other places.

expect: Your English Speaking guide will meet you at your Bangkok City hotel at 8am. From here, you will travel to your first stop, the Temple of the Golden Buddha (Wat Traimit). The Buddha Image is the largest Golden Buddha Image in the world. It was made of pure gold with the price value 28.5 million pounds and over 700 years old. You will be at this temple for more than an hour, allowing you to soak in the atmosphere, and the good luck! You guide will then take you on a short walk to Chinatown. You will see there are many shops selling gold, garments, textiles, stationery, souvenirs, second-hand parts and equipment, electric goods, computer parts, antiques, imported musical instruments and local delicacies. Drive to Pak Khlong Talat (Flower Market). You will amaze by visiting the biggest wholesale and retail fresh flower market in Bangkok. The market has all kinds of popular flowers and flora-related items, including roses, forget me nots, orchids, lilies and more. Most of them sold in packs of 50 or 100 flowers in each, and prices are amazingly cheap. Visit to the Grand Palace and Temple of the Emerald Buddha (Wat Phra Kaew). The temple is popular among visitors and locals alike.

Enjoy lunch before hopping on a long-tail boat along the Chao Phraya River where you will see the lifestyle of Thai people during an hour long ride. The Boat will drop you off at Temple of Dawn (Wat Arun).

This temple it consists of a massive elongated Prang (Khmer Style Tower). The temple derives its name from the Hindu god Aruna, often personified as the radiations of the rising sun. Wat Arun is among the best known of Thailand's landmarks. Although the temple had existed since at least the seventeenth century, its distinctive prang were built in the early nineteenth century during the reign of King Rama II.

Then cross the river to visit Temple of the Reclining Buddha (Wat Pho), its official name is Wat Phra Chettuphon Wimon Mangkhlaram Ratchaworamah. The temple is also known as the birthplace of traditional Thai massage. The temple was created as a restoration of an earlier temple with the work beginning in 1788. You can see the image of Reclining Buddha, which is an impressive 15m high and 43m.
Finally, it’s time to return. You will be dropped off you at your Bangkok City hotel at approximately 5pm.

Start your adventure with Wat Trimit, considered the temple of the Golden Buddha because the statue is crafted from 5.5 tons of solid gold. overview: Not many know that the canals of Bangkok are a source of infinite exploration possibilities beyond the standard Klong tour. This Bangkok canal tour dives deeper into the cultural and way of life of Bangkokians who still call the canals their ‘home’.

expect: Your guide and driver for the day will be waiting for you in your hotel lobby at approximately 8am. From here, they will bring you to the main boat pier along the Chao Phraya River. Your long tail boat for the day and its driver are eagerly waiting to show you the lesser-known side of Bangkok’s water ways.

Start the journey crossing over to the other side of the Chao Phraya River to a Chinese Shrine near Wat Anongkharam. The Shrine is established over 200 years ago during Thonburi period and has maintained as much of its glory and amazing decorative items at the time of its construction.

We embark back onto the boat and sail upstream to the site of where the Queen Mother resided until her passing; to commemorate her, the house has turned into a memorial museum with artifacts and displaying her immense dedication to serve the people of Thailand as good as she can. We follow the river banks and enter the Wat Santa Cruz, with references to the time the Portuguese entered the former kingdom of Siam.

After this visit, we walk around the surrounding village of Kudi Chin where we admire the finer traits of how old baking techniques are used to make bread and snacks. We head back to our boat and continue our journey to Wat Rakang. This was the former house of King Rama I and with its unique, triplex scripture hall more than 200 years old; this is a hidden gem that many visitors do not know about.

Without seeing more of the area, this excursion would not be complete – there are a few historical sites around the temple that we will include (time depending). Your journey ends at the Phatravadee Theatre, a small theatre that is commonly used for private Thai classical performances with a beautiful location along the river. Here is where the Supatra River House is located – one of the finer Thai restaurants along the Chao Phraya River, where lunch will be served.

After a Thai set lunch, we board our long tail boat and sail back to our starting point of the day where our driver awaits your arrival and will bring you back to your booked hotel in the heart of Bangkok. We expect to be back at your hotel at around 3pm.

overview: Get a cultural experience like no other on this private tour of Amphawa Floating Market and key temples from Bangkok. expect: Your day will begin with a pickup form your hotel. You will then be taken to Wat Chulamanee.

This ancient temple sits on the canal-side where the Amphawa Canal converges with the Phi Lok Canal. The temple was built in the Ayutthaya period during the late reign of King Prasatthong. The back of the temple once contained the residence of KhunNak (or Queen Ammarinthramat of King Rama I) and KhunBunrot (Queen Si Suriyenthramat of King Rama II).

We will then take a visit to Wat Bangkoong, honored as one of the unseen temples of Thailand. Wat Bangkoong is a Buddhist temple with a large statue of Nin Mani Buddha inside. Locals and people from further afield come to worship here to honor Luang Phor Dum from the late Ayutthaya kingdom and enjoy the existence of root wood. There is also a mural showing late the Ayutthaya kingdom with Buddha's stories.

Finally, you will be taken to the Amphawa Floating Market – also known as the River Walk. This afternoon-only floating market is located near a temple, Wat Amphawan Chetiyaram. On the weekends, the Amphawa Canal brims with boats loaded with drinks like O-Liang (Thai iced black coffee) and food such as fried sea mussels, noodles, and sweets. Bank-side wheelbarrows also offer goods for sale. Visitors can explore the market, tasting the local food, as well as hire a boat at night to watch as pretty fireflies light up the air.
Once the tour is complete, you will be taken back to your hotel.

title.en: Bangkok Night Bike Tour

overview: Explore Bangkok at night on a bike tour that shows the bustling metropolis in a new light. Admire Wat Arun and Wat Pho lit up at night, wander through legendary Pak Khlong Talat flower market and taste delicious bites made fresh by street vendors. Your knowledgeable local guide shares the magic of the Thai capital when the air cools down, traffic eases and local people enjoy good food and company all along the streets. This small-group bike tour has a maximum of ten people, ensuring a more personalized experience.

expect: Meet your guide near Khao San Road in the cool of the early evening to begin your four-hour bike tour of central Bangkok. Receive a safety briefing, bike and helmet, then set off on two wheels with your expert guide.

Pedal over a bridge across the Chao Phraya River, gazing at the skyscrapers, ancient temples and humble fishing shacks along the riverbanks. Then turn down narrow streets and bike over to 17th-century Wat Arun (Temple of the Dawn), before continuing through backstreets to the renowned flower market, Pak Khlong Talat. Though the market operates 24 hours per day, it is busiest in the evening when locals shop for flowers and produce. Sample some classic street food snacks, then wheel over to Wat Pho, aka Temple of the Reclining Buddha, the oldest temple in Bangkok. Dismount from your bikes and explore the temple grounds for about 20 minutes. Without the crush of daytime tourists around the shimmering stupas, you can get another perspective on the exquisite temple. Enjoy the ambiance of Bangkok at night on this bike tour, which is suitable for people who are comfortable riding a bike in the city and have a reasonable level of fitness. Ride along city streets at a leisurely pace, with frequent stops for photo ops and light refreshments. At the end of the tour, your guide returns you to your starting point in central Bangkok.

expect: Your friendly driver will collect you from your Bangkok hotel and transport you to the famed Siam Niramit Theater. If you’ve chosen the dinner upgrade, enjoy a beautiful spread of savory regional and western dishes. Pile your plate high with Som Tap (papaya salad) or tasty pad Thai while you sip on complimentary soft drinks (alcohol is available for purchase at the bar). Travelers who haven’t opted for dinner (or those who have a bit of time after their meal) can explore the gorounds of Siam Niramit known for. Wander through the replica Thai village that showcases rural life, or enjoy a traditional Thai massage in a tiny open-air house. When the clock strikes 8 pm, head to the theater, where you’ll settle in for the internationally known Siam Niramit show. Talented performers grace the Guinness Book of World Record- holding stage dressed in colorful costumes and epic scenes are complete with ground- breaking special effects. You’ll learn about Thailand’s art, history, culture and heritage in this three-act, 80-minute mind-blowing performance.

Act 1 includes stunning live performances showcasing highlights from Thailand’s numerous geographical areas, including cultural history and traditions from the North, Central Plains, South Seas and Issan regions.

Act 2 grants deeper understanding of the Law of Karma, which says that Earthly deeds will dictate next lives. Three memorable performances depict the realms of Karma, which include Hell, Heaven and the Mustical Forest in between.
By Act 3, you’ll revel in the joy and peace of Buddhism as the stage explodes in a colorful celebration that results in a show-stopping finale.
Once the curtains close, you’ll be transported back to your Bangkok hotel with vivid memories of one of the city’s top attractions.

Family friendly
Skip the line

Created by acclaimed director Ekachai Uekrongtham, Muay Thai Live: The Legend Lives is a spectacular stage show about the history of Thai Boxing, from its origins to present day. The program includes now Muay Thai: Warriors Rising: Two Thai Boxing matches.

You'll be picked up at your hotel and transferred to The Stage at Asiatique, home of Muay Thai Live. Be prepared to experience the history and action of this world-renowned sport. After the live show bringing the spectacular history of Muay Thai back to life, the audience will be treated to seeing the sport in action as it is practiced today with 2 live fights per night.
After the action packed evening, guests will be transferred back to their respective hotels. Itinerary
Act1: The Tiger King:

1699, Kingdom of Ayutthaya: At a temple fair while the villagers are enjoying the festivities, a stranger appears. Who is he? Why does he exude so much charisma and demonstrate such kickboxing prowess?
Act 2: The Prisoner With Eight Limbs

1767, the Kingdom of Ayutthaya lies in ruins after protracted wars with fierce enemies. Many Thai soldiers are taken prisoners. Among them is a Siamese warrior with unmatched skills in Muay Boran (the ancient form of Thai Boxing). Being unexpectedly released from his prison cell, he realizes he must defeat barbaric killers before he can truly earn his freedom.
Act 3: The Warrior With Broken Swords

1773, War against enemies intensify across the land. The best swordsmen are recruited for a final battle to protect the motherland. Led by General Pichai, the revered warrior of the double swords, the battle takes a dramatic turn when one of his sword is shattered.
Act 4: The Lethal Art of Muay Thai
An illustration of the most dangerous techniques of the Ancient art of Muay Thai, which have not been performed in more than a century because they are too dangerous as a sport.
Act 5: The Modern Action Hero

When the son of a police chief sees the girl he loves kidnapped by thugs seeking revenge for his father's actions in service of the Law, our Action Hero has no other choice but to bring his other passion in life, Muay Thai, to the rescue.
Epilogue Muay Thai Forever

From yesteryear until today, Muay Thai evolves, changes and spreads across the globe. But three things have remained the essence of Muay Thai: Respect for Ancestors, Sacrifice for Families, and Upholding the Honor of the Country.

A Float Tank Is A float tank is like a large bathtub filled with mineral salt water and has a closable door allowing you to shut off from the outside world. The tanks are filled with ten inches of water and almost one ton of Epsom salt creating an extremely dense salt-water mixture that allows you to float effortlessly on its surface. The float tank is more than just a tub, it is a sophisticated piece of equipment capable of filtering, disinfecting and cleansing the water as well as regulating its temperature at the same time.

The water in the tank is what we call ‘skin receptor neutral’; meaning you cannot feel it. The water and air are the same temperature as your body inside the chamber. This embryonic environment prevents your brain from distinguishing where your skin and the water actually meet. A float tank is a lightproof, soundproof, zero gravity, temperature neutral space of total solitude where there are no disturbances from the outside world on your brain and no muscle tension on your body. This wonderfully comfortable environment creates what is known as the sensation of ‘floating’, as you lie suspended on a pillow of silky soft water in the stillness of the peaceful quiet.

expect: The staff are highly trained to guide you from the moment youwalk through the door, to the moment you leave. Staff members themselves are avid float enthusiasts who have personally experienced the many physical and psychological benefits derived from floating, and are eager to share that knowledge to both first time floaters, and fellow enthusiasts. The relaxation experience begins with a personalized 10-15 minute orientation geared toward the floaters level of experience, no question will go answered and any anxiety is calmed before you first step foot into the Dream-pod room. You will be led to you private relaxation area and shown all the amenities available to you including massage chair, neck massage, toiletries, teas and coffee, and even snacks. Only after you are ready, will you then receive a step by step walk through of what to expect before, during, and after your float. After showering, the 60 minute session begins with the first 10 minute of soothing Celtic music to further the relaxation process. You will be provided with earplugs to ensure a level of silence in the pod, and you will be shown how to turn the lights inside the tank on and off. Generally the first 15-20 minutes of a first-time float session are spent acclimating yourself to the physical boundary of the pod, and to the experience of letting go of control and enjoying the feeling of weightlessness.

Depending on the visitor's open-mindedness and readiness, users report a multitude of physical, physiological, and even spiritual benefits for their sessions. At the very least, the vast majority of all floaters report a feeling of total relaxation comparable to an intense yoga or meditation session, and even report a feeling of restfulness that comes after many hours of sleep. At the conclusion of your session, the meditative Celtic music will permeate the tank for the final 5 minutes, after which the session concludes. title.en: Half-Day Siam Boran Cultural Bike Tour of Bangkok

overview: Explore the back streets and local communities of Bangkok by bike during this half-day cultural tour of the city. Follow your local guide through Chinatown, explore colorful flower markets, navigate ancient Chao Phraya River and get an insider's look at the former capital of Thailand. This easy-going tour is the perfect way to see the sites and landmarks of Bangkok.
highlights: Half-Day Siam Boran Cultural Bike Tour of Bangkok
Explore the city’s top neighborhoods on two wheels
Enjoy the personalized attention of a professional guide
See the city like a local
Photographs of this fun-filled day included with tour
expect: After relaxing with a complimentary tea or coffee in our peaceful Clubhouse garden in the heart of the city, you will be introduced to your friendly tour guide who will show you a short safety video and then select a suitable bike for you.

Cycling along the quiet back streets, through many small local communities, you will get a truly unique insight into daily local life in Bangkok. Our first stop is the Old Customs House, built in the 1890’s it was once the gateway to Thailand levying taxes on traders moving in and out of the kingdom. There are plenty of photo opportunities whilst your guide takes you on an interesting tour of this beautiful majestic building.

After passing through a Muslim community and a mind-blowing maze of turns we arrive at the ancient Chow Sue Kong Chinese Shrine. Tucked away in Talat Noi this shrine is the center of the 200-year-old Chinese community that is one of the oldest in Bangkok. ‘Enter the Dragon’, the vibrant and seemingly chaotic Chinatown, the center of the 1782 Chinese settlement where it is said you can find just about anything. Cycling through the busy market streets is exhilarating; enjoy the vibrant colors and activities of the busy stalls and the fabulous scents from the famous street food vendors.

At Pak Khlong Talat, the biggest fresh flower and vegetable market in Bangkok, you will be stunned at the array of dazzling fauna from across Thailand. Here you can walk among this truly amazing area and try some delicious local Thai snacks that your guide will buy for you. On the ferry across the River of Kings, the lifeblood of Bangkok, you can relax and watch the beautiful city sights unfold. On the other side you will visit Wat Arun, also known as the Temple of Dawn this is one of the most striking riverside landmarks in Bangkok. Also, not to be missed is Wat Prayoon in the Old Portuguese community; its large white chedi is the only one of this style in Bangkok.

As you meander along the river cycle path you can enjoy the refreshing cool breeze and the fantastic views back across the city. Back at the Clubhouse treat yourself to a free fish foot spa, we also have a licensed bar and if time permits we will present a slide show of your tour photographs taken by your guide.
Finally, when you return home, you will have received an email with a free link to download the tour photographs taken by your guide on your fantastic Bangkok bike tour.

Hop back on your river boat as you make your way to the next stop, using the transit time to observe daily life on the Bangkok river system that some describe as the “Venice of the East.” Check out the cozy wood houses lining the intricate network of canals, and watch Thai locals as they ferry a cornucopia of goods like rice along the waterway. Meander through the Palace’s stunning grounds, admiring the intricate gold-covered buildings that dot the complex, and visit the temple housing the sacred Emerald Buddha, carved from a single piece of jade. Conclude your river excursion at Bangkok’s Gems Gallery, one of the world’s largest jewelry shopping centers, where you can shop for exquisite custom made items.

expect: This tour will offer you the chance to enjoy a pleasant tour through Bangkok where you will see beautiful temples and pagodas that are representative of the history and culture. The most predominant religion in Thailand is Buddhism, with approximately 95% of Thai people practicing the Theravada discipline of Buddhism. Due to this, it is very common to see Monks wandering the Bangkok streets. It is also the reason why Thailand has approximately 26,000 temples (aka Wat’s).

On this half-day tour you will visit 3 of the most significant temples in Bangkok and learn why this city is so renowned for its culture and Buddhist sacredness. The first temple you will visit is Wat Traimit. This temple is also known as the temple of the Golden Buddha. The reason for this is because the temple is home to a 3m (10 feet) tall statue of Buddha crafted from 5500kg (5.5 tons) of solid gold. It is believed to be the largest solid gold statue in the world.

The tour will continue through Chinatown, where you will come across the second temple of the day, Wat Pho. Possibly one of the most well-known temples in Thailand, Wat Pho is home to the famous Reclining Buddha. 46m (151 feet) in length and 15m (49 feet) tall, this Buddha is the largest in Bangkok.

Last but not least, you visit Wat Benchamabophit. Also known as the Marble Temple, this monastery was built out of white Italian marble from Carrara in the 19th century and houses one of the country's most beautiful Buddha images.
After this, you will be taken back to your hotel safely.

expect: You will be collected from your hotel at 7.30am and head towards the Chao Phraya River to board a traditional long-tailed boat for Thonburi.

Chao Phraya River with its many canals had originally given Bangkok the name “Venice of the East.” Passing by boat along the canals you will see the life of Bangkok’s waterways unfold with busy morning activity. See impressive sights such as the Royal Barges Museum and the Wat Arun, which literally means "Temple of the Dawn". The Grand Palace is the “must see” attraction in Bangkok. It is an architectural wonder of golden stupas, walls and pillars encrusted in shining and colorful mosaics. Having served as the residence of past Kings of Thailand between the 18th and mid-20th centuries, the architecture is predominantly Thai, although there are many European influences throughout its halls.

The most famous building within the palace grounds is Wat Phra Kaew and this is regarded as the most sacred Buddhist temple in Thailand. Construction of the temple began when King Rama I moved the capital from Thonburi to Bangkok in 1785. The main temple building houses the Emerald Buddha. The Buddha is carved from a single piece of jade and is the most revered object in Thailand.

expect: At 10am we leave from our office/lounge in Yannawa, a non-touristy district in Bangkok. We make a first stop at a typical local Thai temple with Chinese influences. The guide can give you a lot of information about the temple and Buddhism in general. After visiting the temple we walk at a relaxed pace through one of the poorest neighborhoods of Bangkok. By our own Western standards, the people you meet don’t have much, but they are so friendly and warm hearted. Their lifestyle remains an authentic part of the Thai way-of- life. The way people live along the many canals in Bangkok can’t be seen while passing by in a tourist boat. Only walking alongside them gives you that experience. Next, we go for a short long tail boat ride across the Chao Phraya river. Once on the other side, we enter a jungle of banana, mango, papaya and coconut trees. This part of Bangkok seems out of place, but it is here, part of this vibrant metropolis. You are surrounded by lush vegetation and the best way to enjoy it is on foot, nature lovers will feel at ease here. A little further on, we arrive at a superbly designed park, where we rest a while and feed the hundreds of fish waiting at the pond. This lake also serves as a home to the park’s largest inhabitants, monitor lizards. Keep your eyes peeled near the water, if you’re lucky you may catch a glimpse of one of them.

After enjoying the beauty of the park, the birds, squirrels and butterflies, the next surprise awaits and we continue our journey in a real ‘samlor’ (Thai rickshaw or ‘bicycle taxi’) on a cycling trip through the greenest part of Bangkok. The samlors make a stop at another temple, the oldest temple in this area, before heading to a riverside restaurant. Here we will enjoy our Thai lunch overlooking the majestic River of Kings. Soak up the river view and breeze while watching the boats plying up and down the river.

From the restaurant it is only a short rickshaw ride to the pier where a public boat brings us back to the familiar concrete side of busy Bangkok. This tour will give you lasting impressions of a Bangkok not always seen!!

Inside the park you will find small villages, lavish gardens, winding water ways, a small floating market and of course food and drinks. There are push bikes available for rent, a health care center, wedding and filming facilities, as well as comprehensive guides to the park with interesting historical facts.

Covering 200 acres, the grounds of Ancient Siam correspond roughly to the shape of the Kingdom, with each of the monuments lying at their correct places geographically. Some of the buildings are life-size replicas of existing or former sites, while others are scaled down. This vast park also houses several ethnological displays of artifacts and antiques. There are rural arts, ancient tools, hunting equipment and evidence of the long-term survival of a native culture.

The tour will explore the history of the Rattanakosin period and some of the area’s most famous landmarks. You will also discover more about the different kings who had an impression on this area. As you walk you will pass famous places like, the Amulet Market, Thammasat University, Wat Mahthat, Sanam Luang, City Pillar Shrine, and Wat Pho (Temple of the Reclining Buddha). However, in addition to these you will also visit some lesser-known places.
highlights: Great overview and orientation of the city
Explore the local streets on a walking tour of the city
Led by a local guide
Small-group tour
expect: You will meet your guide at 8:30am at the meeting point near Tha Tien pier, and after a short introduction you will head off to explore Rattanakosin Island. As we walk you will pass famous places like, the Amulet Market, Thammasat University, Wat Mahthat, Sanam Luang, City Pillar Shrine, The Grand Palace (and Temple of the Emerald Buddha) and Wat Pho (Temple of the Reclining Buddha). However, we will also take you to a few off the beaten track places too.

While the tour does not go inside all these places it will give you a great overview of the area for you to then explore on your own after the tour. Specifically, it will not enter the Grand Palace or Wat Pho Along the way we will stop for a cold drink and a chance to cool down. The tour will finish approximately 11am at Tha Maharaj, which is conveniently located for you to continue exploring further or for you to get the public ferry back to your next destination.
This is a walking tour and you will walk approximately 3km. It is hot in Bangkok so please dress appropriately.

title.en: Full-Day Life as a Fisherman Experience from Bangkok

overview: A short ride by train and local truck away from Bangkok, the world of hard-working, friendly fishermen await you. Pick cockles, learn how to make Thai desserts and get a hands-on experience of life around beautiful mangrove forests and hidden canals.
highlights: Small-group tour
Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Lunch included
Led by a local guide
expect: You will be picked up in the morning from the meeting point at Exit 1 of Wong Wian Yai BTS Station at around 8am. Transfer from your hotel to the Skytrain and to the BTS Skytrain station is on own arrangement.

From here, your local guide will bring you to the local train station that rails away from Bangkok and follows the coastline to Bang Khun Tian, a small community that lives and works what the sea is giving them. Surrounded by mangrove forests, small hidden canals and the sea just a stone’s throw away, a more local presentation of Thailand simply cannot be given. From this train station, board a ‘song Taew’ (local truck) to the farm, just a few kilometres away from the sea.

Your day starts with a visit to a shrimp and cockle farmer who will show you how this very traditional means of labor is still very much effective. It is a delight to see each guest partaking in this maritime farming method and you will be certain that this is a very fun-filled activity when joining the locals.

A workshop is next on the program: using only natural dye and material and under the guidance of one of the teachers and apprentices, making tie dye handkerchiefs will be easy and something to take home with you as a souvenir.

A freshly cooking seafood lunch by one of the local families will break up the day to exchange the morning experiences with your fellow travelers before your host for the day, guides you from a local boat pier for a scenic canal tour where the Gulf of Thailand meets the provincial borders of Bangkok and Samut Sakorn, He is very happy to even show you his home at the San Taw community prior to boarding his friend’s boat! Cockle picking, relaxing and kayaking through the canals are all part of the package after this interesting local experience.

If you really want to get further into the cockle picking, bring some clean clothes as to understand the hard labor that goes into this, one has to go waist-deep in the muddy waters to fine-tune your cockle picking skills. There are also a couple of kayaks you can row to explore the community along the canal.

This is a very much local vibe orientated tour, where you will be given the chance to understand the local community and environment and the importance of planting mangroves in the area. This trip supports the local fisherman family and helps keep the spirit of agro- tourism strong in his community.

Finally it is time to say goodbye as you embark on the boat, bus and train journey back to city life in Bangkok and the place where we started in the morning. Arrival at Wong Wian Yai BTS Station and transfer on own arrangement to your Bangkok hotel.

title.en: Half-Day Off the Beaten Track Bangkok Tour by Walking and Rickshaw

overview: A behind-the-screen tour of authentic Bangkok. Away from modern Bangkok, this exploration touches the essence of what Bangkok truly is. From local temples to plantations, a tour where a ‘samlor’ and your feet are the means to see what others may not see.
highlights: Once-in-a-Lifetime Experience
Lunch included
Led by a local guide
expect: Your driver will pick you up from your hotel in Bangkok and drive you to the meeting point, south of the city center. Meet you guide and head out into the authentic part of Bangkok at approximately 10am. You will be surprised what happens behind and away from the concrete walls and buildings of Bangkok. The places you can't even reach by bicycle. You never see this side of Bangkok in brochures and travel magazines.

Walk towards a typical local Thai temple with Chinese influences. Your guide can give you a lot of information about the temple and Buddhism in general. Buddhism plays a very important role in the daily lives of the people who have lived here for centuries. Continue at a relaxing pace deeper into one of the poorest neighborhoods of Bangkok, also known as the slums. You will immediately notice the friendliness and smiles they give you when you pass by their houses. An essential and authentic part of the Thai belief cannot be better described when calmly walk around this district.

These people live along the many canals in Bangkok – something that one cannot find on any tourism map. Only by walking alongside these waterways, for some an important means of transport, gives you that experience that you are really looking after. Crossing the Chao Phaya River is our next part of the exploration. At the other side of the river, enter a jungle of trees, bearing fruits such as banana, mango, papaya and coconut. This part of Bangkok looks like it seems out of place, but it is here, part of this vibrant metropolis we call Bangkok. You are surrounded by lush vegetation and the best way to enjoy it is to walk. Nature lovers will feel really at ease here.

A little further, you will arrive at a beautiful maintained park, where you will rest a while and feed the hundreds of fish. This lake also serves as a home to the park’s largest inhabitants, huge monitor lizards. After enjoying the beauty of the park, continue your journey in a real ‘samlor’ (Thai rickshaw or ‘bicycle taxi’) on a cycling trip through the greenest part of Bangkok.

The ‘samlors’ make a stop at another temple, the oldest temple in this area, before heading to a riverside restaurant. A simple, yet delicious Thai lunch overlooking the majestic River of Kings awaits you. From the restaurant it is only a short rickshaw ride to the pier where a public boat brings us back to the familiar, more modern side of busy Bangkok. You surely will return to your hotel with many new impressions of the Thai capital! You will agree that this adventure gives a totally different view and experience of the city. After returning to our meeting point, you will be taken back to your hotel Notice: On Saturdays and Sundays the samlor make an extra stop at an authentic Thai market along one of the many canals.

title.en: Bangkok Sunset Tour by Bike

overview: Take advantage of Bangkok’s cooler evening hours on a 5.5-hour sunset biking tour around the Chao Phraya River with hotel pickup and drop-off, dinner, and snacks in a local food market. Visit some of the city’s markets, temples, pagodas, and quiet neighborhoods as Bangkok lights up after dark, and get the perfect introduction to key sites by exploring with a local guide.

Visit key sites at sunset
Great overview and orientation of the city

expect: Begin with pickup at your accommodations, then get fitted with a bicycle and safety gear by the Chao Phraya River. The guide will set a gentle pace throughout the bike tour, with plenty of stops to snap photos, refuel with snacks, and take in views of the Chao Phraya at sunset. Hop a ferry to Thonburi, then follow back streets and alleys to the Klong San market and an eight-story Chinese pagoda at the edge of the Chao Phraya River. Stop by a second market for a light snack at one of the food stalls, then ride to the Temple of Dawn, which is illuminated with glowing lights after dark.

Visit a small eatery near the temple for a light dinner, then pedal towards Wat Rakhang Khositaram, a temple that dates to the Ayutthaya period. Cross back to the Bangkok side of the river, then follow the Royal Fields to the exterior of the Grand Palace and Wat Pho, where you’ll hop off your bike to explore the temple compound. Visit Bangkok’s 24-hour a day fresh flower market, then ride back to the central meeting point. This tour concludes with drop-off at your hotel at roughly 10:30pm.

overview: Explore Bangkok like a local on a half-day tour of the city’s neighborhoods, markets and sites on foot and by public transport. Follow your guide through the bright stalls of the local flower and vegetable market, then visit a series of religious landmarks, from the stunning Wat Prayoon to an 18th-century catholic church, Chinese shrine and the Temple of Dawn. Get the perfect overview and orientation of the city and the Chao Phraya River.

Continue onto a riverboat taxi for a ride to one of Bangkok’s most vibrant markets, where vendors from around the country display mounds of ripe fruit, herbs and vegetables, and flower sculptures.

Walk across the landmark Memorial Bridge to Wat Prayoon, a snow-white temple that tourists often miss, then tour the Catholic Santa Cruz Church and Kuan An Keng, a Chinese shrine with intricate wood carvings and mural paintings.

Cross the Yai Canal to Wat Arun, the Temple of Dawn, where you can circle the Khmer-style prang, or tower, that’s one of Bangkok’s most recognizable sights. Continue back to your hotel by taxi boat and Skytrain, or get tips on places to eat, drink, and explore in this bustling, waterfront neighborhood.

title.en: Bangkok Temple and Floating Market Tour

overview: Look beyond Bangkok’s headline attractions and explore two of the city’s lesser-known treasures on this 6-hour tour. Tour the Temple of Dawn (Wat Arun), a distinctive, high-spired temple overlooking the Chao Phraya River. Then, ride a longtail boat around hidden canals to Taling Chan floating market, a jumble of waterfront stalls, eateries, and boats selling fresh foodstuffs and snacks. A canalside lunch, entrance fees, and hotel pickup and drop-off included.
highlights: 6-hour Temple of Dawn (Wat Arun) and Taling Chan floating market tour in
Bangkok
Guided visit to the Temple of Dawn, considered the most striking in Bangkok
Admire the elaborate architecture and towering, mosaic-encrusted spire

expect: After pickup from your Bangkok hotel, settle inside a comfortable, air-conditioned vehicle with your guide, and set off into the city’s vibrant streets. Head first for the Temple of Dawn (Wat Arun), widely considered to be one of Thailand’s most beautiful temples. Set on the west bank of the Chao Phraya River, this ornate Buddhist place of worship is known locally as Wat Arun or Wat Chaeng, and distinctive for its riverside location and unusual design, complete with four towers (prangs) and a central spire (prang) measuring more than 229 feet (70 meters).

Take a tour of the temple to view the main hall and spires. Admire the richly decorated main spire, with its coatings of tiny colored glass and Chinese porcelain mosaics, and explore the main hall with its Buddha images and murals.

Having explored here, enjoy a ride on a traditional longtail boat along the city’s canals (klongs) and River Bang Khun Si. Chug down the waterways, navigating locks and passing old temples and houses that reveal the hidden side of Bangkok. Visit the Taling Chan floating market, a collection of waterside stalls, restaurants, and boats selling fresh fruits, vegetable, snacks, and other goodies.

Stop for lunch at a canalside restaurant and absorb the bustling scenes as you eat and relax. Watch the locals go about their daily rituals, and see vendors cooking up seafood and other snacks on their boats moored along the water.
Finally, return to central Bangkok, where your tour finishes with a hotel drop-off.

overview: Immerse yourself in Thailand’s rich cultural heritage with this half-day tour of the Sampran riverside from Bangkok. After a scenic journey through the Thai countryside, head to the Rose Garden to be dazzled by a 1-hour Thai Village Cultural Show. See dramatic displays of martial arts, Thai boxing and sword fighting; attend a re-enactment of a traditional Thai wedding; and witness a lavish Buddhist ordination ceremony. That’s not all: you’ll also get chance to watch a parade of elephants and enjoy performances of the Bamboo dance, Kala Dance and Yoev Dance.

title.en: Bangkok Walking Tour: Chao Phraya Riverside Paths of Thonburi

overview: Experience life alongside the Chao Phraya River during this 3.5-hour walking tour of Thonburi. After a boat ride from Bangkok, stroll the riverside paths and alleyways in search of local food. Your guide introduces you to Thai snacks and drinks as well as cultural diversity represented by the area’s Thai temples, Chinese shrines, churches and mosques. You’ll stop at Princess Mother Memorial Park and visit Wat Kalayanamit on this small-group tour, limited to a maximum of 10 participants to ensure personalized attention.
highlights: 3-hour Bangkok walking tour of local life along the Thonburi riverbank
Ride a boat across the Chao Phraya river to explore Thonburi’s back streets on foot
Learn about the religious and cultural diversity of the Bangkok

expect: This tour avoids the tourist crowds and gives a glimpse at local life in Bangkok’s original communities.

Make your way to Yodpiman River Walk in Bangkok where you will meet your guide. After a short introduction you will take the public ferry to cross to Thonburi, situated on the western bank of the Chao Phraya River.

After you disembark, start your small-group walking tour around the area of Khlong San and Kuddeejeen, known for its diverse community of Buddhists, Christians and Muslims. During your 3-hour excursion you’ll pass several shrines, mosques and sites of both ethnic Chinese and Portuguese Catholics, as well as view the early 19th-century temple of Wat Kalayanamit. You will stroll along riverside walks and small backstreets and learn about the area’s history. You will stop to explore the quaint community of Kudeejeen and sample their famous snack. When you reach the Princess Mother Memorial Park, stop to visit a replica of the late royal mother's childhood home. The lush public space features gardens, a pavilion and exhibition halls with royal memorabilia on display. Your tour will conclude at Tha Din Daeng, a local foodie's paradise. From here you can either grab some lunch or head back across the river to Chinatown.
Please note: The walking tour covers about 2 miles (3.5 km), and the pace is suitable for anyone with moderate fitness.

title.en: Colors of Bangkok

overview: Discover Bangkok on a half-day cycling tour of the city’s most intriguing neighborhoods. Explore quiet, winding streets lined with coconut palms and banana trees, far from busy thoroughfares and tourist districts. Meet the locals at a community kindergarten, sewing workshop and Buddhist temple, then watch students train in traditional Muay Thai fighting. Dine alongside residents at a neighborhood restaurant, and experience Bangkokian warmth and generosity at every turn.
highlights: Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city

expect: Exploring Bangkok by bicycle is an exciting way to experience Thailand’s capital. The half- day tour shows you a part of Bangkok that you’ll never see from the sky train, tuk-tuk or taxi ! A part where there is almost no traffic, just narrow streets and backyards. Bangkok as you have never imagined !

During the first part of the tour we see stand alone villas, luxurious apartment buildings, townhouses and in between shops, companies and stall factories. First stop is at one of the many hidden local communities in Bangkok. This area of Bangkok, some call it a slum, but the local people call it 'home'. The people who live here belong to the poorest people in Bangkok, but they are friendly, polite, generous and give us a warm welcome every day. Walk through this small community and stop at the slum kindergarten. The poorest children receive education here while their parents are working. Visiting slum areas makes you remind that life is not that easy for everyone.

Next, continue your bicycle adventure in the 'City of Angels' and make another stop at a sweatshop where they make t-shirts for the local market before arriving at the pier. Here you'll board a typical Thai long-tail boat to cross the mighty Chao Phraya river, the River of Kings. At the other side of the river you'll find yourselves back in the 'Jungle' or the 'Green Lung' of Bangkok, a very green area just a stone's throw away from the hustle and bustle of Bangkok. Here you'll cycle on elevated pathways through lush vegetation and in the shade of coconut palms and banana trees.
Halfway through the tour you will stop at a local restaurant where you will be provide with a small Thai meal.
After lunch, visit a very old non-touristy Buddhist temple where the guide can tell you everything about Buddhism.
Last but not least, make a stop at a small open-air Muay Thai (boxing) school. Then, head back to the heart of Bangkok where your tour finishes.
Notice : The itinerary is subject to change, since schools and local shops may be closed during the weekend, school holidays or national holidays.

title.en: Bangkok’s Hidden Treasures Walking Tour

overview: See a different side to the city as you discover Bangkok like a local on this 5-hour tour. Soak up the scenery as you cruise along the Klong Saen Saeb canal, stroll around the historic Pom Pra Satru Pai district and marvel over little-visited treasures like the Silver Pagoda, the Giant Swing and the Golden Mount. Then, get a taste of local life as you browse the shops along Bamrung Muang, ride a tuk-tuk through the alleyways of old Bangkok and relax with traditional 30-minute foot massage.
highlights: 5-hour tour of hidden Bangkok
Get a glimpse of local life as you cruise Klong Saen Saeb canal and stroll down

expect: Meet your guide at the National Stadium BTS (Skytrain) station and walk to the Elephant Head Bridge to board a boat on Klong Saen Saeb, a canal that connects you to a district of the old city known as Pom Phra Satru Pai, translated as Fort to Defeat the Enemies. Your first stop is the Silver Pagoda, built during the reign of King Rama III for the princess granddaughter in 1846. The temple is best known for its 37 metal spires, signifying the 37 virtues toward enlightenment. Then it's off to the Golden Mount at Wat Saket, a pagoda situated on an artificial hill that commands a panoramic view of Bangkok. Continue on foot to Bamrung Muang, Bangkok's first shopping street, which caters to temple supplies. Here, you'll find monks' robes, candles, incense sticks, and a variety of Buddha statues for sale. Down a small side street you'll reach Ban Baat, where handmade alms bowls are produced then purchased by devotees and donated to monks. Arriving at the Giant Swing, learn about its 18th-century construction and symbolic significance, then stroll through the prominent royal temple of Wat Suthat. Next, hop aboard a motorized tuk-tuk for a ride to Wat Pho, home to the first school of medicine in Bangkok and the Reclining Buddha.

Finally, head to a nearby Thai massage school where you'll receive a 30-minute foot massage, effective in stimulating the functions of the internal organs. Once you are relaxed, it's time for a boat ride down the Chao Phraya River, before you connect to a Skytrain back to the meeting point.

title.en: Old Bangkok City Walking Tour

overview: See the royal temples of Thailand on this half-day walking tour of Bangkok. Wander the streets of this wonderful city and listen to your guide’s informative commentary. Stroll to Wat Ratchanatdaram, the Golden Mount at Wat Saket, the Giant Swing in front of Wat Suthat and Tiger God Shrine (Chao Phor Seua). Morning tea plus hotel pickup and drop-off are included.

expect: Start your 3-hour morning tour with pickup from your hotel in Bangkok and set off with your guide on a walking tour of royal and religious monuments. Your first stop is Wat Ratchanatdaram, a Buddhist temple popular for its multi-tiered brazen palace, or Loha Prasat, one of just several bronze-roofed palaces in existence.

A short walk brings you to the Golden Mount, which is located in the compound of Wat Saket. Built by King Rama IV, this golden chedi is reached by a 344-step spiral stairway. While on top, you'll have a wide view of the older part of Bangkok. Next up is Baan Bat, the last of a series of villages established in the 18th century by King Rama I to create alms bowls for monks. After a look around, your guide accompanies you to the Giant Swing (Sao Ching Cha) that stands outside of Wat Suthat, among Thailand's most significant royal temples.

Take a break for morning tea, coffee, or a soft drink, then visit the Tiger God Shrine (Chao Phor Seua), which is dedicated to the spirit of a tiger that once inhabited the surrounding jungle. Learn about the festivals, operas, and puppet shows held here year-round. After a stroll to Ratchadamnoen Klang Road you're transferred back to your hotel.

This was the first stop for ancient travelers entering Bangkok and the perfect place to start your journey! From there you’ll weave through the maze of woven streets and alleys that make up Bangkok’s vibrant and bustling Chinatown. Following your well-informed guide through the diverse cultures that make up this lively part of the city, you’ll discover all it has to offer. You’ll cross the magnificent Chao Phraya River by ferry and continue your journey by exploring the Historic Thonburi side of the river, stopping at the incredible Wat Arun, with many flower gardens and exhibitions for you to leisurely enjoy. Pedal past local villages lining the riverbank and enjoy Thai dishes during a scenic riverside lunch. Follow your guide past the royal palace, and then board a cargo ferry to cross the Chao Phraya River. Continue your journey to the island of Ayutthaya, pedaling along back lanes and riverside settlements north to the ancient city established in 1350. You’ll pass by Wat Phutthai Sawan and the 17th-century St Joesph’s Church before a visit to the vast complex of Wat Chai Wattanaram, one of Ayutthaya's best- known temples based in Ayutthaya Historical Park. After a look at this 16th-century temple, take a break for a riverside Thai lunch with a scenic view of Sri Suriyothai Park and the ruins of the royal palace. After lunch, cross the river to explore the city's ancient monuments on your bike, starting with Wat Lokayasutharam (Temple of the Reclining Buddha). Your guide points out a Buddha image cradled by a strangler fig at Wat Mahathat (Temple of the Great Relics) before taking you back to Bangkok by minivan to end your day trip.

expect: Colors of Damnoen Saduak is a relaxed bicycle ride from Damnoen Saduak floating market through Amphawa district. The transfer from our office to Damnoen Saduak floating market, is in a fully equipped air-conditioned car/minivan, taking about 1-1.5 hours. At Damnoen Saduak we start with a long-tail boat ride through a maze of canals cutting through local villages and plantations and you will be able to see how the locals live here. After we’ve visited Damnoen Saduak floating market, our bicycles are waiting for us to continue this adventure.

We ride along quiet country back roads, plantation trails and unpaved flat roads. Depending on the season, we’ll see grapes, lychee, pomelo and coconuts growing in trees and plants, ready to be harvested. Besides the overwhelming nature along the Mae Klong River delta there are a few beautiful temples we would like to show you and tell you more about. We visit a coconut plantation where they make palm and coconut sugar in a traditional Thai way. We then head to “Wat Bang Kung”, which dates out of the Ayutthaya period and is more than 500 years old. It is famous for a small chapel that is completely enclosed within the roots of a banyan tree, called Bot Prok Po. It’s like the tree itself is the pillar of the temple and without it will fall. This is an amazing sight.

“Wat Bang Kae Noi”, built in 1868, inside is covered with wood carving depicting the life of Buddha. Three life sized wax statues of famous Thai monks complete this remarkable temple. The ride continues over small wooden bridges hanging over canals along the Mae Klong River until reaching the ferry to cross us to the Amphawa market. Here you will have a chance to stroll the local market and/or visit King Rama II park before heading back to Bangkok by car/minivan.

overview: Escape the city for a full-day back-to-nature adventure from Bangkok and explore the island of Koh Kret on the Chao Phraya River. This is one tour where the journey is as fun as the destination, so soak up the scenery as you cruise down the river from Bangkok, then transfer to the island by local bus and ferry. Next, explore car-free Koh Kret by bike and long-tail boat; visit temples, artisan villages and floating markets; and try your hand at pottery and candy making.
highlights: Full-day tour of Koh Kret Island from Bangkok
Travel by boat, local bus and longtail boat
Enjoy an easy 7km (4 mile) bike ride around the island
Visit the island’s artisan villages and have a go at making pottery or candy
Tuck into a typical Thai lunch on the island
Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Small-group tour ensures a personalized experience
expect: See another side of Bangkok on this day trip to the historic man-made island of Koh Kret. First, hop aboard the express shuttle boat down Chao Phraya River, sailing by the majestic architecture of the city as you cruise out. Arrive at Nonthaburi Pier and stretch your legs with a stroll around the market before catching a local bus bound for Pak Kret. A short ferry ride will take us to Koh Kret and we disembark at Wat Poramai Yikawat, the island’s main temple famous for its collect of Mon-style stupas. Although only 20 kilometers from the metropolis, the only forms of transport here are bicycles, boats or two feet! Grab your bicycle and set off on the 7 kilometer circuit of the island - the perfect front row seat to watch local life unfold as you cycle past rural scenery. Ride to a nearby artisan village to learn about the traditional Thai art of pottery making, before taking a turn on the potter’s wheel before lunch.

Then, leave your bicycle behind for a long-tail boat ride around the island and the ‘dessert canal’ to learn the secrets behind the island’s sweet treats! While you're here, roll up your sleeves and try your hand at making some of your own candy creations. We then explore Wat Saeng Siritham and the nearby floating market before wrapping up your journey with a public bus ride back to Bangkok city center.

title.en: Countryside Bike Tour Including Floating Markets and Canal Boat Ride

overview: Follow an informative guide on a bicycle ride through the countryside outside Bangkok. Your full-day itinerary includes a canal boat ride and a riverside lunch, plus stops at Tha Kha and Damnoen Saduak floating markets. Cycle alongside the Mae Khlong River and stop at fruit plantations en route to Wat Bang Kung, a temple built during the Ayutthaya era and shrouded by an impressive banyan tree. Snacks, beverages and round-trip hotel transport from Bangkok are included.
highlights: Full-day bike tour outside Bangkok, led by a local guide
Visit Tha Kha and Damnoen Saduak floating markets, plus the heritage market of
Amphawa

expect: Meet your experienced guide upon hotel pickup in Bangkok, and begin your full-day tour with a drive to Tha Kha Floating Market, located 37 miles (60 km) outside the city. Take a boat ride through the canal, stopping at a local home that makes coconut sugar the old- fashioned way.

Return to the market by boat with your guide, and enjoy the opportunity to stroll around for a bit of browsing before departing by bicycle. Once you’re fitted with your bike and helmet, pedal through the countryside to the second floating market of the day, Damnoen Saduak, where you can stand on a bridge and observe the variety of goods being sold from the boats. Then continue riding along the banks of the Mae Khlong River, and stop for a sumptuous riverside lunch at a first-rate Thai restaurant. In the afternoon, cycle through coconut plantations and orchards with many varieties of tropical fruit. Along the way, you’ll visit Wat Bang Kung, a temple dating back to the Ayutthaya period, now overgrown with the roots of a banyan tree.

From here, pedal with your guide to the preserved heritage market of Amphawa. Leaving your bike with the driver, take a walk through the market along the canal before returning to Bangkok in your tour vehicle for hotel drop-off.

The mild bike route includes flat terrain, small roads and easy trails, some of which are dirt. The day's total biking distance is 26 miles (42 km), and the pace is leisurely. A support vehicle is on hand at all times so you can take a break if you get tired.

overview: Get an up-close look at daily life in Bangkok on a walking tour that introduces you to the diversity of local cultures and atmospheres as you visit Muslim, Catholic, Chinese and Buddhist neighborhoods. Stroll along hidden alleys, cross the Chao Phraya on a ferry, check out a flower market, and enjoy coffee and muffins at a café. Walking distance is about 1.25 miles (2 km).

Gain authentic insight into the local lifestyle and diversity of cultures
Take a ferry ride across the Chao Phraya

title.en: Countryside Bangkok and a Floating Market Tour by Bicycle Including Lunch

overview: Check out a floating market and experience the countryside outside of Bangkok on this bike tour. Gain insight into the daily lives of local residents as you visit a small community, ride past plantations and stop at an off-the-beaten-path floating market known for its fresh snacks, often called as ‘Thai tapas.’ Walk through the market with a guide, and sample some of the goods before continuing the bike tour, which includes a freshly prepared Thai lunch.
highlights: Bangkok countryside bike tour
Escape the bustle of the city for an exploration of its more tranquil outskirts
Visit a floating market to sample some Thai snacks
Chat with people who live here, and enjoy a homemade lunch
Get a look at the daily lives and culture of Bangkok-area residents
expect: We will guide you through all layers of society, from sky scrapers to Bangkok's biggest, jaw dropping fresh market. We cycle under the highway where a small community has risen up, to arrive at a local pier. Here we will cross the Chao Praya river with our long tail boat where we will arrive in the green heart of Bangkok. Your bicycles will be carried out of the boat and here we cycle through a lush green part of Bangkok you never knew existed. The city of center feels so far away while we cycle over elevated pathways through the nature where we occasionally spot a monitor lizard or turtle bathing in the sun. Passing old plantations we stop at a hidden local floating market. This old floating market is only open during the weekends and is famous by the locals for all the freshly prepared snacks, so called “Thai Tapas”. Here, you will find almost no other tourists. We will take a nice stroll through the market while your guide gives you a variety of delicious snacks to try. After this nostalgic market walk, we will get on the saddles again to cycle further through this beautiful area.

Later on we will stop again to sit down and enjoy a delicious home-made lunch which is freshly prepared by the locals. After this delicious lunch we cycle back to our long tail boat and cross the river where you can experience a stunning and completely different view of Bangkok's high-rise buildings. We then cycle back to where we began.

title.en: Bangkok Sunset Ride

overview: Set out on a sunset bicycle ride through Bangkok and view famous landmarks lit up at night. Pedal at a leisurely pace along back roads and laneways through the capital with your guide. You’ll cross the Chao Phraya River to the Thonburi side and enjoy dinner at a Thai restaurant with views of illuminated Wat Arun (Temple of Dawn). Ride past the Grand Palace and explore Wat Pho on foot before finishing at Pak Khlong Talat flower market.
highlights: 6-hour bike tour of Bangkok with dinner
See the sunset and illuminated landmarks at night
Cross the Chao Phraya River to Thonburi
Whet your appetite at a market food stall
Feast on a Thai meal at a riverside restaurant

expect: After a quick bike fitting, we’re on the way to the first river crossing that brings us to the Thonburi side of Bangkok.

Together with our bicycle we walk across the Klongsan market. From here we cycle in a relaxed pace to a Chinese pagoda located on the riverbanks of the Chao Praya River. The inside of the 8 stories pagoda is finished in granite and bronze. The windows have delicate etched designs of birds and other animals.

We continue the Bangkok Sunset ride through a quiet neighborhood and stop at the second market. They only sell food here and it is the place where we’ll have our “starter” tonight. There are many food stalls and our guide will explain to you what is offered, how it is cooked, and what’s in it.

We continue along the river until our stop at the Temple of Dawn. It’s almost magical the way Wat Arun is lightened and gives you a new impression. Now it’s time for our main dish and we will sit down at a typical local Thai restaurant.

After our meal we ride along Wat Rakhang Khositaram and take a boat back to the Bangkok side. We ride pass Sanam Luang and the Grand Palace until we reach Wat Pho for a visit and stroll the temple compound.
We continue the ride to “Pak Klong Talad” or Flower market. Where you’ll see a kaleidoscope of bright colors as vendors showcase fresh floral goods from every corner of Thailand.
We then take you back to the Sheraton where the Bangkok Sunset Ride ends and we have to say goodbye. You will return to your hotel with new impressions and experiences of Bangkok!

overview: Wander among the tiny alleyways and peruse the wholesale shops of Sampeng Market on a 3.5-hour walking tour within Bangkok’s bustling Chinatown. With a knowledgable guide leading the way, you and your small group of no more than eight will have the opportunity to bargain hunt, sample delicious snacks and even enjoy a sit-down meal composed of popular Thai dishes. Of course, no Thai tour is complete without a visit to a local temple and shrine.

Navigate the hustle and bustle of Sampeng Market's small alleys and shops with an informative guide
Sample a Chinese herbal drink and street vendor snacks

expect: Meet your guide and small group at Saphan Taksin BTS Station, and hop aboard the local ferry for the ride to nearby Ratchawong Pier, Bangkok's riverside gateway to Chinatown. As you delve into Chinatown's busy streets to make your way to Sampeng Market, your guide provides a brief introduction to the neighborhood, which dates back more than 200 years and remains a vibrant part of the modern city.

Enter the sprawling market, where you’ll see all sorts of items for sale, from hair accessories, stickers and school supplies to clothing, household wares and electronic knickknacks. Jewelry, gem and gold shops fill an entire area. Many store owners in Bangkok visit Sampeng Market regularly to purchase goods for their own shops.

As you walk around, your guide points out notable old shophouses, spice markets, tea shops, Chinese temples and shrines, and popular eateries. Learn about Chinese spiritual practices, and stop to sample herbal drinks and favorite snacks prepared by street vendors. After a couple of hours taking in the sights and history of Sampeng Market and Chinatown, enjoy a typical Thai-Chinese lunch at a local restaurant. If you want to shop, your guide can assist you in the art of bargaining like a local. Your tour ends in Chinatown, where you can make your own way to your next destination.
