title.en: City-to-Shore Biking Adventure on the Gulf of Thailand from Bangkok

overview: Set out on a guided city-to-shore bicycling tour along the Gulf of Thailand, where you’ll meander quiet coastal roads, explore a mangrove forest and encounter local wildlife. This full- day adventure from Bangkok is ideal for anyone who enjoys a moderate challenge and a unique small-group experience. While the bulk of your day involves bicycling, there is also a scenic train ride to Mahachai, a ferry excursion and a delicious seafood lunch to keep you refueled and refreshed.
highlights: 9-hour bike tour along the Gulf of Thailand from Bangkok
Ride down quiet city streets and rural coastal roads with an experienced guide
Take a scenic train trip between Bangkok and Mahachai
Explore Mahachai Market, known for its seafood and its location right next to the train tracks
Visit a mangrove forest, and look for wildlife like monitor lizards and mudskipper fish
Includes bike and helmet, train and ferry rides, lunch, water and snacks
Small-group tour limited to eight people ensures a more personalized experience
expect: Meet your guide in the morning at the bike shop in Bangkok to be outfitted with your high- quality mountain bike and helmet. After a safety briefing, cross the Chao Phraya River by ferry, and bike along quiet back roads to reach the train station. Enjoy the scenery that rolls by the train windows during the 1-hour journey to the coastal town of Mahachai. Upon arrival, check out the local market, which sits within arm's reach of the train tracks and is one of the largest traditional fresh-seafood markets in Thailand. Then take another ferry across the Tha Chin River, hopping back on your bike afterward. Before long, you’ll hit the beginning of some seriously fun cycling tracks. Follow your guide down dirt roads that take you past mangrove forests, shrimp farms and salt ponds along the sparkling Gulf of Thailand. Look for wildlife such as kingfisher birds and water monitors, large lizards that can measure up to 6.5 feet (2 meters) in length. You may also even spot the small but impressive mudskipper fish, which has adapted to living mostly on land. Stop for a seafood lunch at a waterside restaurant, and then continue along the gulf shore to a mangrove conservation center, where you'll learn about local ecology. Take in a bit more of the beautiful countryside and coastline before returning to Bangkok by train and ending your day trip back at the starting point.
Biking details:

Expect to ride a total of about 32 miles (52 km) at a leisurely pace, with frequent stops for water breaks and photo ops. Drinking water and snacks are provided throughout the day. In Bangkok, you’ll ride through alleyways, away from the big roads; along the gulf, you’ll take quiet, flat country roads. The tour is not recommended for novice cyclists. You must be able to carry your bike on and off the train and over footbridges at times.

title.en: Chinatown Bike Tour in Bangkok

overview: Bring the family on a two-wheel guided tour of Bangkok’s Chinatown. This half-day bike excursion takes you across the Chao Phraya River and on to Thonburi’s back streets to visit some of the area’s lesser-known sights. You’ll stop for a stroll through Princess Mother Memorial Park, ponder the incredible architecture of Wat Arun, and get to sample traditional Portuguese dessert at Santa Cruz Church. Flat terrain and a small group size make this an ideal tour for all ages.
highlights: Half-day bike tour of Bangkok's Chinatown
Cross the Chao Phraya River to Thonburi with an informative guide
Cycle back streets on an easy ride to city highlights and lesser-known sites
Stroll the tranquil gardens of Princess Mother Memorial Park
Stop for traditional Portuguese dessert at Santa Cruz Church

Hotel pickup and drop-off included (if option is selected)
expect: After hotel pickup (if option is selected), assemble in Chinatown to get your gear and a safety briefing. Begin your half-day bike tour at a bustling street market and local temple before crossing the Chao Praya River to Thonburi. Your guide takes your small group along Bangkok’s meandering back streets during the easy, 9-mile (15-km) ride over mostly flat tarmac. There are plenty of stops along the way, making for a perfect family outing. Cycle to Princess Mother Memorial Park and hop off your bike to explore its tranquil gardens and quaint historical museum. Dedicated by His Majesty the King to honor the childhood home of the late Princess Mother, the large park features a reconstructed house and exhibition halls that offer visitors a glimpse of her life.

See photographs and mementos on display, including small Buddha images she sculpted for the royal family, before riding to Santa Cruz Church. Established by a Portuguese community — Thailand’s first European settlers — the Catholic church is a monument to the country's religious freedom and cultural tolerance.

Note the Chinese architectural influences of this imposing landmark that looms above the river’s western bank, and enjoy a taste of traditional dessert from an old Portuguese recipe passed down for generations.

Then continue to Wat Arun, aka Temple of Dawn, built on the riverbank in the 17th century to catch the early morning light. Gape at the pagoda-style temple, studded with Chinese porcelain, and discover from your guide the significance of its design. Dare to climb Wat Arun’s steep stairs to the towers for a fantastic view of the temple grounds and river life below, before your bicycle tour ends with drop-off at your hotel (if option is selected).

overview: Leave modern Thailand for ancient Siam on a full-day road bike tour from Bangkok to Ayutthaya. Ride 46.6-miles (75- kilometers) along back roads and canal-side paths that travel through vibrant local communities. Explore Ayutthaya’s historic palaces and shining chedis as you explore the ruined city, discover the extraordinary architecture of a 17th-century Buddhist temple at Wat Chaiwatthanaram, and relax over a riverside lunch before catching an air-conditioned van to Bangkok.
highlights: Cycle the city streets to absorb the local atmosphere
Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Excellent value for money
Family friendly
Step back in time on a history tour
Day trip (destination A to B)
expect: Hop on your road bike tour and experience a peaceful atmosphere of the historic city that is Ayutthaya. Set off on and escape from the city vibes from your hotel in Bangkok, then head north along canals ('Klongs' as they are called in Thai) where local communities lie on both sides, and take the back roads to the former capital city of the Thai Kingdom. On this smooth 46.6mi (75km) ride you can witness the distinctive transformation of lives and communities along the way.

With no fuss and little busy traffic, it's time to take in the beauty of the scenery as you cycle to the past and history comes to life. Once you arrive at the destination, you will find it's hard to believe you have cycled from the modern world back in time over 400 years in one day! Enjoy the charm of those temples you will never find in any guide book, and visit the exquisite Wat Chaiwattanaram, a landmark in the UNESCO World Heritage site of Ayutthaya.
Enjoy plenty of light refreshments on the way and take a nice lunch break by the river. Have fun with your ride and return to Bangkok safely in our comfortable air-conditioned van.

title.en: Bangkok City Culture Tour by Bike

overview: Explore Bangkok’s back streets and bustling markets on a 3-hour guided bicycle tour of the city’s neighborhoods. Ride from local temples and train graveyards to the gleaming skyscrapers of the Thanon Witthayu district, and get off your bike to explore the vibrant Khlong Toey produce market. Discover the quiet paths of Lumpini Park, where imposing monitor lizards share space with local Tai Chi clubs, and get a street-level view of one of one of Asia’s most dynamic cities.
highlights: Excellent value for money
Cycle the city streets to absorb the local atmosphere
Small-group tour
Choice of morning or afternoon departure
Led by a local guide
All necessary equipment included
expect: Start your tour choosing a bicycle that fits your body-length. Once on the way you'll stop at a typical local temple, ride along the train-graveyard, through slum areas and visit the biggest daily fresh-market “Talad Klongtoey”. Here, the group will park the bicycles and have a stroll on the market. All your senses will awaken while walking here, leaving you very busy with your camera.

After the market visit, cross the Rama IV Road that brings us to Queen Sirikit Convention Center and the tranquil Benjakitty Park. In Benjakitty Park, a small, but very nicely designed park, have a break and rest a little while enjoying the views. Continue our Bangkok City Culture ride along the Tobacco Monopoly. This is the place where cigarettes are made. Sometimes you even can smell the scent of tobacco-leaves when cycling in the area. A little further, pass one of the most expensive streets of Bangkok “Thanon Witthayu” where many embassies are located. It also has an entrance to the famous, “Central park of Bangkok”, Lumpini Park.

While taking a break in this beautiful park, you can see locals doing Tai Chi or Yoga and other outdoor activities. If you are lucky, you might meet the famous permanent residents of Lumpini Park, the huge monitor lizards! Although they look scary, they’re actually harmless. After the break continue the Bangkok City Culture ride through small communities and finish where your tour started with a totally new Bangkok Biking experience.

title.en: Bangkok Chinatown Cycle Tour

overview: Climb on a bike for a 5-hour ride, departing the bustling lanes of Bangkok for the greenery of Phra Pradaeng on the opposite side of the river. Follow your guide to Khlong Toey Market, then cross the Chao Phraya River by long-tail boat. You’ll escape the big crowds and noisy streets as you pedal along elevated pathways through the mangroves. Enjoy provided snacks, fruit, beverages and lunch at a local home or restaurant.
highlights: Half-day Bangkok bike tour with an experienced guide
Take a leisurely ride through the city to Khlong Toey Market
Ride a long-tail boat across the Chao Phraya River
Pedal past mangroves on a narrow bike path
Enjoy refreshments and a local lunch
expect: The tour begins on Sukhumvit Road. Follow your guide away from the jam-packed roads of Bangkok. The route takes us through a working-class neighborhood rarely visited by tourists, where you can experience yet another side of the metropolis of Bangkok into the lively Khlong Toey market. Here we find a colorful blend of Thai and Chinese goods. You’ll also head through “Little Chinatown” on your way towards the river, where children and locals enthusiastically wave and shout “hello” at the unusual sight of foreigners on bicycles. We cross the Chao Praya river in a long tail boat and enter a green park area called Phra Pradaeng, where we cycle on narrow elevated pathways through the mangrove and traditional Bangkok communities. We then dine at a local home or restaurant, where you will feel the hospitality for which Thais are known.

title.en: Siam Chiva Food Tasting Bike Tour of Bangkok

overview: Discover the diversity of Bangkok through its cuisine and glimpses of daily life on a full-day bike tour, which starts with a cup of coffee or tea while you meet your guide. Pedal through the city along quiet back roads, stopping at local landmarks and food sites where you’ll enjoy tastings. See markets, ride along the river and learn about the array of cultures in this vibrant destination.
highlights: Bangkok bike tour
Cycle through the city to take in the local atmosphere
Witness daily life in different neighborhoods, and sample a variety of food items
Enjoy a longtail boat ride on the river
Learn about Bangkok from a local guide
expect: After relaxing with a complimentary tea or coffee in the peaceful Clubhouse garden located in the heart of the city, you will be introduced to your friendly tour guide who will show you a short safety video and then select a suitable bike for you.

Cycling along the quiet back streets and through local communities you will arrive at an old Chinese cemetery. Surrounded by the encroaching city skyscrapers this charming cemetery is a serene and peaceful public park, a retreat for the local residents. Continuing towards the Bang Rak district, known as the Village of Love, you will pass through a Muslim community where we will stop and refuel with a delicious Muslim breakfast.

Your journey continues along the quiet back streets that follow the river up stream and along the way you will discover and explore many hidden gems. Entering Chinatown you will cycle through the busy market streets and watch the locals get on with their day. Get among the vibrant atmosphere and sample a fantastic variety of local street-side dishes. Crossing the mighty Chao Phraya River to the Old Portuguese community, you will visit two very unique temples and enjoy a delicious lunch at a local Thai street restaurant. After a short ferry ride back across the river you will discover the huge vegetable and flower markets where you can sample some refreshing exotic fruits and Thai delicacies. On the long tail boat trip back down the River of Kings, the lifeblood of Bangkok, you can relax in the refreshing breeze and enjoy a completely different perspective of the city. Back at the Clubhouse treat yourself to a free fish foot spa or visit the licensed bar and if time permits, watch the slide show of your tour photographs taken by your guide. Finally, when you return home, you will have received an email with a free link to download the tour photographs taken by your guide on your fantastic Bangkok bike tour.

title.en: 6-Hour Siam Ratree Night Bike Tour of Bangkok

overview: Explore Bangkok at night on a bike tour with a knowledgeable guide. Cycle leisurely through the city to take in the after-dark atmosphere, and make stops to sample street food. Bike tours are a great way to get a feel for local culture and daily life, and with an evening tour, you can skip the heat of the day.
highlights: Bangkok nighttime bike tour
Pedal through the city with a guide to soak up the evening ambience
Enjoy tastings of street food
Visit local landmarks and communities like Chinatown, a flower market and a temple
Cross the Chao Phraya River by ferry
expect: Make your way to the meeting point and relax with complimentary tea or coffee in the peaceful clubhouse garden, located in the heart of the city. You will be introduced to your friendly tour guide who will show a short safety video and then select a suitable bike for you. Cycling along the quiet back streets of the city through small local communities, you will discover many hidden treasures that take on a new life as the sun starts to set. Visit the Kuan Yin Shrine that is filled with spiritual mystique and incense smoke, watch the local worshipers chant Buddhist scriptures.

Continuing along the Chao Phraya River up stream, you will arrive at Chinatown and enjoy a fantastic street-side diner whilst you soak in the vibrant, colorful and exciting atmosphere. After your relaxing diner you will cycle through the busy market streets up to Pak Khlong Talat. This huge flower market is packed with dazzling flora from across Thailand and is an energetic hub of night time activity so get ready for a sensory overload. The next stop is Wat Pho, an absolutely amazing experience at night where you almost feel completely alone in this wonderful birthplace of the traditional Thai massage. A little further on you will reach Sanam Luang, the royal cremation ground, where you can enjoy the cool evening breeze and the poetic views of the Grand Palace in the background. Crossing the mighty Chao Phraya River to an old Portuguese community where you will cycle around two very unique temples. Meander back to the ferry crossing and and take the final ride back to the clubhouse.
You will have received an email with a free link to download the photographs taken by your guide, during your fantastic Bangkok bike tour.

title.en: 5-Day Bangkok to Samui Island Electric Bike Tour

overview: Explore the beautiful scenic coastal roads of South Thailand, a wonderful combination of nature, culture, climate, and friendly people. Vacation on the beautiful beaches, swim in the warm ocean, do some sun bathing, and cycling. This guided tour is designed for a half-day of riding and another half-day for activities, such as chilling on the beach, or you may design your own relaxing time. A self-guided option is also available.

All entrance fees included
All necessary equipment included
Informative, friendly and professional guide
Led by a local guide
Once-in-a-Lifetime Experience
expect: An electric bike allows you to enjoy the ride. You can set the electricity depending on how hard you want to push yourself. You do have to pedal, like a normal bike, but the sensors will work to make it easier for you when you need it.
Your ride is easy and consists of back roads. Only two short sections are along a main road. However, If you feel uncomfortable, you can skip them by taking the support car. Tour itinerary
Day 1: Hua-Hin - 30km (L, D)

Your guide will pick you up from the hotel in the morning and transfer you to Hua-Hin. The ride follows a quiet back-road passing farmland, small villages and a beautiful beach. The area has many activities like ATV rides, wind-surfing, kite-surfing, or squid fishing at night (own expense). Overnight in a 4-star beachfront hotel with large swimming pool.
Day 2: Sam Roi Yot National Park - 64km (B, L, D)

This morning, you will cycle through Sam Roi Yot National Park and take a boat ride into canals of the mangrove forest. The route is along the coastal road down South through limestone mountains and coconut plantations. Your hotel is in the provincial town with a long curved beach in the front. Weather permitting, have dinner on a Catamaran boat with the beautiful city's bay view. Overnight
Day 3: Wahkor Aquarium - Ban Krut - 70km (B, L, D)

Today is the longest ride of this tour. Start by cycling along the beach and across the runway of the military airport. Then visit the Langur monkey families. They are friendly and you are welcome you to feed them some fruits. The next stop is Wahkor Aquarium to explore the underwater world of the Thai gulf. Ride on the back-roads and some trails through the narrowest part of Thailand (11km), passing fishing villages, temples and farmland to your cozy resort in Ban Krut. Overnight at a 4-star beachfront hotel with swimming pool.
Day 4: Ban Krut - 55km (B, L, D)

Cycle out from the resort and cruise along the coastal road. Today's scenery is more beautiful along undulating roads, with mountains to your right and ocean to your left. You will stop at a coconut factory and visit a rubber plantation to see where tires come from. After lunch at the beach restaurant, transfer to the beach resort near the ferry pier. This golf course resort has a spa, fitness area, hot spring bath and many activities for you to enjoy on the last day before leave the main land. Overnight at a 4-star beach resort with swimming pool and golf course.
Day 5: Return (B)
Your ferry to Samui, Phanngan or Tao island will leave in the morning and afternoon. You can choose to come back to Bangkok or other town on the way.

title.en: Hot Air Balloon Ride with Champagne Breakfast from Chiang Mai

overview: Experience the beauty of northern Thailand from the skies with a morning hot air balloon ride and sparkling wine breakfast. You’ll depart Chiang Mai as the sun ascends, drifting high above magnificent temples and jungle forests and taking in photo-worthy views. Upon landing you’ll enjoy a sparkling wine toast and morning meal. Your pilot will even present you with a flight certificate verifying your journey. Pickup and drop-off hotel transportation is included.
highlights: Hot air balloon ride from Chiang Mai
Marvel at breathtaking vistas above the treetops during your flight
Enjoy preflight coffee or tea, and dine alfresco with a breakfast buffet featuring Thai and Western dishes
Celebrate your magical flight with sparkling wine

expect: After an early morning pickup from your hotel in Chiang Mai, depart for the launch site for your hot air balloon ride. Upon arrival, hot coffee or tea is served while a professional crew prepares the equipment for your flight, which lasts just over an hour. Once the colorful balloon is inflated, climb into the two-passenger basket with your expert pilot and feel the thrill as you gently lift off the ground. As the balloon rises and you gracefully drift along roughly 500 to 2,000 feet (150 to 610 meters) above the ground, the stunning panoramic view offers a perspective you won’t soon forget. While your pilot navigates, you float over treetops and soar above the verdant countryside of northern Thailand. Enjoy the tranquility as the sun rises and reveals picturesque vistas as far as the eye can see.

Once your pilot spots a suitable landing, you’ll soon find yourself on firm ground. Then it’s time to relax as a buffet breakfast is served alfresco, including a mix of Thai and Western dishes with fruit juice, coffee or tea.

Celebrate with provided sparkling wine and receive a flight certificate signed by the pilot in remembrance of your magical hot air balloon ride, followed by drop-off at your hotel with bragging rights in hand.
(Note: Hot air balloon flights from April to October depend on weather conditions.)

title.en: Long-Neck Karen Hill Tribe Tour Including Elephant Ride from Chiang Mai

overview: Spend the day exploring northern Thailand on this Long-Neck Karen Hill Tribe Tour including elephant ride from Chiang Mai. You’ll see majestic elephants at work during a visit to Maesa Elephant Camp, and after learning more about this impressive operation, you’ll hop atop one of these gentle giants for a truly memorable hour-long trek through the Thai jungle. Make your way to the Karen hilltribe village, where residents are known for their well-jeweled long necks. Explore the village with your expert guide who will help you to gain a deeper understanding of customs and culture. Enjoy lunch at a local orchid farm and make a stop at the well-known Queen Sirikit Botanical Gardens. Your small-group tour includes round-trip transport and is limited to 16 guests to insure personalized attention.
highlights: Chiang Mai day trip to Padong long-necked hill tribe with elephant ride
Observe elephants moving timber at Maesa Elephant Camp
Take a one-hour elephant ride through the jungle northwest of Chiang Mai

expect: Your friendly local guide will collect you from you Chiang Mai hotel and transport you in the comfort of an air-conditioned minivan to the Maesa Elephant Camp. Located just 15 miles (25 km) outside of northern Thailand’s capital, this popular stop offers travelers a look at Asian elephants at work. You’ll learn about the history of elephants in Thailand as you tour the grounds. These gentle giants have been used as much for transportation a they have for hauling logs and other heavy items. Feed your new animal friends bananas and sugarcane before climbing atop their backs for a journey into the jungle. Your one-hour trek through thick tropical forest concludes at the Padong long-necked hilltribe village of Baan Thong Luang. (Travelers who prefer not to ride can travel by minivan with their guide.) Explore this interesting village where local residents who migrated from nearby Myanmar live and learn about the customs and traditions that make them to unique. Gain a deeper understanding of the brass rings that women wear around their necks to identify their tribe and hear about the subsistent farming and traditional handicrafts that offer commerce for this community. Once you’ve had your fill of village life, head to a nearby orchid farm in Mae Sa. Enjoy a typical lunch before heading to Sirikit Botanical Gardens, where you’ll be able to explore the grounds and learn about the unique flora indigenous to northern Thailand. After a truly memorable day exploring, head back to your Chiang Mai hotel with your guide.

title.en: Chiang Mai City and Temples Half-Day Tour

overview: This half-day Chiang Mai temple tour explores the most famous and picturesque of the city’s 36 Buddhist Wats, the perfect introduction to Northern Thailand’s cultural and religious capital. Experience Chiang Mai’s most visually stunning Buddhist temples, including the gorgeous 600-year-old Wat Phrathat Doi Sutep atop the 5,300-foot (1,615 meter) Doi Suthep Peak, plus plenty of great photo-ops. The tour includes the services of a friendly, knowledgeable guide, entrance fees, air-conditioned transport and hotel pick-up and drop-off from central Chiang Mai.
highlights: Visit the impressive temples of Chiang Mai including the 600-year old Wat Phrathat
Doi Suthep

expect: The Chiang Mai temple tour is the perfect chance to sample the most famous and beautiful of the city’s 36 Buddhist temples (Wats), both inside the city walls and in the nearby countryside.

Start your Chiang Mai temple tour with a pick-up from your hotel in the city about 30 minutes to an hour before the start of the tour. From there you’ll visit Wat Chedi, an ancient structure in Central Chiang Mai first constructed in 1411. The temple once rose over 278 feet (84 meters) above the city before it was partially destroyed by an earthquake in 1545. Glance inside the temple to observe statues of guardian spirits that some say protect the temple to this day.

The tour will also ascend the rolling hills surrounding the Chiang Mai to experience the immaculate Wat Phrathat Doi Sutep, perched high above the urban center near the summit of the peak of Doi Suthep. The final staircase leading to the site is adorned with the impressive body of the mythical dragon-headed serpent, or Naga, snaking its way down 306 steps. Over the course of the tour, gain first-hand insight into habits of the temples’ Buddhist monks as they go about their daily routines, plus plenty of opportunities to photograph historic environs of Chiang Mai and the majestic views from the foothills surrounding the city.

title.en: Morning Buddhist Almsgiving and Temples Tour in Chiang Mai

overview: See the golden pagodas of Wat Phra That Doi Suthep before the crowds arrive, following an early-morning almsgiving to local Buddhist monks. title.en: 4-Night Experience in Chiang Mai: Palong Villages Stay and Chiang Dao Trek

overview: Set out from Chiang Mai to trek through northern Thailand’s mountainous jungle on a three- day private tour. With an experienced guide by your side, you’ll explore the area around Chiang Dao, visiting Karen, Akha and other remote hill tribe villages, dining on (and if you like, helping prepare) northern Thai cuisine, and bedding down in bamboo huts. You’ll even have time to enjoy Chiang Mai and its offerings at your own pace with sightseeing tips catered specifically to your interests.
highlights: 4-night northern Thailand private tour with three-day trek round-trip from Chiang Mai
Strap on your backpack and follow your expert guide into the jungle near Chiang Dao
Stay overnight in two Palong villages and visit several more
Identify the ingredients used in northern Thai cooking at a local market and in the forest
Take a mini-cooking class from your guide and have the option to help prepare meals
Enjoy free time in Chiang Mai with sightseeing options tailored to your interests
Chat with locals as your guide translates
expect: Immerse yourself in the Chiang Dao region of northern Thailand for a memorable experience trekking through the jungle and visiting several hill tribe villages, including those of the Palong, Akha, Lahu and Karen peoples. Your adventurous tour includes three days of trekking in the mountains, walking for 1-4 hours between villages. You will need a decent level of fitness to participate as you will carry your own backpack and personal gear. This cultural experience includes two nights' accommodation in bamboo huts in a hill tribe village where living conditions are modest. Your experienced guide will assist you with any questions along the way. You’ll also have two nights of accommodation at a hotel in Chiang Mai, where you’ll have plenty of time to explore the city at your leisure. Itinerary
Day 1: Chiang Mai

Arrive at your Chiang Mai hotel anytime before your 6:30pm welcome meeting. If you arrive early, enjoy exploring northern Thailand’s vibrant capital, with dozens of stunning temples, a lively riverfront, great shopping at outdoor markets and a variety of small shops, and numerous options for delicious Thai cuisine.

After your welcome meeting, you’ll have the option to follow your guide on a leisurely stroll through the old city or choose to peruse Chiang Mai on your own (all activities at own expense). / Overnight
Day 2: Chiang Mai – Palong village (Lunch, Dinner)

Your guide will pick you up from your hotel in the morning and you’ll head north to Chiang Dao. Along the way you’ll stop at a local market in Mae Malai to shop for food for your trek. Your guide will show you the ingredients used in Thai cooking as you gather the materials for your journey ahead.

Hop back in your vehicle and continue to the Mae Tang River, where you board a bamboo raft for a refreshing float down the river. Enjoy the relaxing ride and river scenery, then disembark and meet your driver. From there, you’ll take a ride through the northern town of Chiang Dao to an Akha village called Ban Huay Hok.

In Ban Huay Hok you’ll put on your backpack and set out on the first leg of your trek, a 1- hour hike to the Palong village of Pang Deng Nai. Follow your guide along lush jungle trails and hear about how the royal projects – sponsored by the Thai royal family – created villages like Pang Deng Nai to give economic and educational opportunities to hill tribe peoples. Savor lunch when you arrive at the first village, then you’ll continue to another Palong village named Pang How, where you will stay the night. After you meet your local hosts and set your pack down, your guide will introduce you to northern Thai cooking and show you how to make some favorite dishes for your dinner tonight. After enjoying your meal, head over to another home and hear stories about the history of the Palong people and the village. / Overnight
Day 3: Hill Tribe Trekking – Chiang Mai (B, L, D)

After awakening to the sounds of roosters and village life, enjoy breakfast with your guide before exploring the village. Learn about your surroundings from your guide. Afterward, say goodbye to your hosts and hit the trail for a 2-hour hike to a waterfall where you can take a dip in the water and nibble on a picnic lunch.

When you’re rejuvenated, you’ll continue along the trail for 3-4 hours, listening to your expert guide talk about the forest’s plant and animal life. Find wild ginger, rattan and pitcher plants as you walk along the jungle trail, and learn the many ways that bamboo is used locally.

Once you reach another Palong village known as Huay Bong, take time to rest and meet the local people. Have the option to help your guide prepare the night’s meal and learn more about Thai cuisine, then enjoy dinner and a campfire where you share stories with your guide and the people in the village. / Overnight
Day 4: Palong village – Chiang Mai (B, L)

Join your guide for breakfast then grab your pack and walk about an hour to the Karen village of Thakilek, the last part of your trek. Along the way you’ll stop in at a Lahu village and check out their spirit temple and blacksmith. In Thakilek, your guide shows you around the village and introduces you to the Karen people.

Bid farewell to the village community, and head back to Chiang Mai with your guide. Celebrate your trekking accomplishments with a tasty lunch at a local restaurant. Once you have refueled, stop in at an orchid nursery where you can check out the varieties of this beautiful flower. Your guide will return you by songthaew (covered truck with bench seats) to your hotel in Chiang Mai in the afternoon.

Say goodbye to your guide and settle into your Chiang Mai hotel, then enjoy the evening at your leisure. You could opt to soothe sore muscles with a traditional herbal sauna and Thai massage or indulge in a festive meal at one of Chiang Mai’s many fantastic restaurants. / Overnight
Day 5: Chiang Mai (B)

You have the freedom to leave at any time for your next destination, or set your own itinerary if you choose to stay in Chiang Mai for a few days. Explore the gorgeous temple of Wat Phrathat Doi Sutep – located on a hill above the city with stunning views, take a Thai cooking class, shop for local goods or catch live music at a riverside cafe (own expense).

title.en: 4-Day Tour from Chiang Mai to Chiang Rai

overview: See the best of northern Thailand with a 4-day tour from Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai, and explore hill tribe villages, mountain temples and local culture. Spend two days discovering the highlights of Chiang Mai, from the iconic Wat Phra Singh temple to the old city walls. Climb past the fierce naga serpents at Wat Phrathat Doi Suthep, see a fresh flower market and take in a traditional show. Experience an elephant camp, ride a longtail boat and explore the far north before finishing your tour in Chiang Rai.
highlights: Multi-Day Trip
Pickup from a centrally located meeting point
Get inside tips from a local
Ideal choice for families
Perfect introduction for first-time visitors
Step back in time on a history tour
expect: Join this 4-day tour to create a memorable touring experience and explore Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai. A round-trip transportation is included, where you will be picked up from your hotel in Chiang Mai and dropping off at Chiang Rai Airport.
Itinerary
Day 1:

You will be picked up from your hotel in Chiang Mai around 1:30pm and will explore the ancient city of Chiang Mai. The first stop is 160feet (48m) high Wat Suan Dok and you will see behind these white Chedi rises a golden bell shape edifice. A short drive to visit Wat Phra Sing located within the old city walls and continue to Wat Chedi Luang, the historic centre of Chiang Mai. You will visit the Wat Ched Yod and Wat Chiang Man before heading back to the hotel in Chiang Mai around 6:30pm. Please note, no meals included.
Day 2:

On the second day of your tour, you will enjoy the stunning panoramic views over the city at Wat Prathat Doi Suthep. If you adventures enough, try to climb up a 309 steps Naga staircase to reach the temple or you can use the cable car service. Next, you will visit a historical landmark, Wararot Market a long standing market, known for its variety of speciality Chiang Mai food and products, followed by a visit to the flower market. Enjoy a pleasant Northern Thai Khantoke dinner accompanied by an authentic Lanna traditional show and performances. You will return to the hotel around 9:30pm and overnight in Chiang Mai. Please note, breakfast and dinner are included.
Day 3:

In the morning visit the Thai Elephant Care Center, which was set up to provide care for elderly elephants retired from logging and camps. There are no rides, but visitors learn about how the old-timers are fed with ground grass and herb balls, and if time of visit is right, you could watch the bath-time, as well as visiting the cemetery for elephants who have died of old age. After lunch, join a relaxing long - tail boat to Chiang Rai through the panoramic views of surrounding mountains and jungle of Kok River. Ride past the magnificent local villages of Muser and Karen hill tribes located alongside the river. Arrive Chiang Rai in the afternoon and take a short transfer to your hotel. Overnight in Chiang Rai. Breakfast and lunch included.
Day 4:

After breakfast, we will check out of the hotel and visit Wat Rongkhun (White Temple). You will continue to the ancient Chiang Saen city and have lunch at the Imperial Golden Triangle Resort then transfer back to Chiang Rai Airport. Please note that transfer to Outer-Chiang Rai hotels will be subject to supplement charges. The tour will finish around 2pm and you are recommended depart from Chiang Rai Airport at 3:45pm. Please note, breakfast and lunch are included.

title.en: Opium Trail Trek Including Wat Phra That Doi Suthep and Hmong Village Tour

overview: Take a privately guided walk on an old opium trail in Northern Thailand, where you’re accompanied by a local Hmong guide between mountain villages. You’ll visit the Hmong communities of Doi Pui and Ban Mae Sa Mai, and learn about the people and plants of Doi Suthep-Pui National Park, whose slopes once supported a prolific opium trade. Your full-day private tour includes a stop at Phra That Doi Suthep Temple, the FORRU tree nursery and a Hmong museum, plus a picnic lunch and round-trip hotel transport by minibus.

expect: Meet your guide during hotel pickup in Chiang Mai and get comfortable in your private minibus for the drive to Doi Suthep-Pui National Park. Your first stop is Phra That Doi Suthep Temple, a 14th-century Buddhist monastery that houses an Emerald Buddha replica. Arrive before the crowds for a look at the ornate murals and classic Thai design, and climb the 300 steps for a panoramic view over Chiang Mai.

Hear about the complicated history of the local Hmong community en route to Doi Pui village, where you’ll meet up with a Hmong guide to accompany you on a hike to Ban Mae Sa Mai village, the largest Hmong community in Northern Thailand. he 4-hour trek to the Mae Sa Valley follows a leisurely pace along a nature trail, taking you through dense forest past wild banana trees and water features, and includes photo stops. Learn some plant and tree identification, and hear about the opium cultivation once prevalent in the region, which now supports fruit trees and other agricultural projects. Eat a Thai picnic lunch at a scenic spot and get a glimpse of an alleged footprint of the Buddha. Upon reaching Ban Mae Sa Mai, you’ll find few visitors in marked contrast with Doi Pui. Learn about the forest restoration project of Chiang Mai University called FORRU, which your included donation fee supports. Visit the FORRU tree nursery and a small Hmong museum before your private vehicle transports you back to Chiang Mai.

expect: Regarded as the highest mountain in Thailand with 8,514 feet above sea level, Doi Inthanon offers beautiful scenery, evergreen forests, dwarf rhododendron groves and many types of habitat. The area is also popular for bird-watching; being home to nearly 400 bird species, many from North Asia, including mountain hawks and Eurasian woodcocks. The tour starts with enjoying mountainous scenery on the way up to the National Park and preserved forest that runs all the way to the peak of the mountain and offers a very cool climate all year round. The Air Force Radar Station as well as King Inthawichayanon’s stupa is located, commemorating the last king of Chiang Mai. expect: Upon pickup by air-conditioned minivan, depart from your hotel in the morning or afternoon and head to Wat Phra Singh, aka the Temple of the Lion Buddha. You have about an hour to explore 14th-century Wat Phra Singh, Chiang Mai’s most important Buddhist temple. Observe hundreds of monks and pilgrims gathering at this major monastery, which includes a fully restored assembly hall featuring Phra Chao Thong Tip, a large seated Buddha statue cast in gold and copper, and two medieval Buddha statues. Step into the Gilded Hall, renovated in the 19th century and considered a fine example of Lanna monastic architecture and religious art. title.en: Evening Kantoke Dinner in Chiang Mai

overview: An evening one may not soon forget: culturally-enriched with a succulent dinner, northern Thai style where the beauty and grace of dance and musical performance is presented at one of the leading Kantoke restaurants in Chiang Mai.

expect: An evening filled of a culturally important even that is something typical of the northern part of Thailand. It was not until 1953 that Khan Toke became a social gathering when a local politician invited high honored guests to sit with him and enjoy this special dinner. Northern Thailand boasts a culinary tradition all its own, much of it influenced by neighboring countries. From Laos, comes a love for sticky rice and a distinctive use of chillies; from Myanmar, unique curries, generally un-thickened by coconut milk as in other parts of Thailand; and from China, a preference for noodles. The “Khan Toke” dinner is traditionally specific to the people of the northern region that has elements of it all combined into one. It is a short ride from your hotel to the venue where you will be welcomed by the staff who will guide you to your table where your Kantoke dinner is served. Dinner is served in small bowls, known in Thai as Khan and guests are seated cross-legged on cushions at a low table, known as Toke in Thai. The cuisine served is northern Thai and it is prepared with the western palate in mind as traditional Thai food can be very spicy. During dinner, entertainers will perform the intricate Forn Leb finger dance; the Forn Thien candle dance; the Ramwong circle dance; and the Ram Dab sword dance. Opt for an additional hill tribe show performed by various members of the Yao, Lahu, Meo, Lisu, and Karen hill tribes after you have finished dinner.
After this dinner and dance performance, we will bring you back to your hotel.

overview: Learn about the traditional cultures of Thailand’s hill tribes with a private, full-day trip into the countryside from Chiang Mai. Meet local Karen people who enhance their beauty with distinctive brass neck rings, and learn about the challenges facing the tribes in modern Thailand. Enjoy a river boat journey to the only village in the region with descendants of the Lahu tribe, and get a glimpse of daily life in that remote place. Finish your day by relaxing in the village’s natural hot springs before returning to Chiang Mai.
highlights: Full day, private tour of hill tribe culture from Chiang Mai
Travel to a remote village by riverboat
Meet members of the Karen and Lahu tribes
Learn about local culture and traditions

expect: You will be collected from your Chiang Mai hotel and head out to the small village of Ya Pha, home of the fascinating Long Neck Karen Hill Tribe.

Here you will learn of the significance of the brass rings worn around their necks. The number of rings increases according to age and as their shoulder blades are gently pressed lower and lower, over time, their necks appear to lengthen.

From here you will make a stop at for lunch before casting off in a motor boat to visit the Lahu Hill Tribe village at Bann Pha Yai. Remarkably, this is the only village in this region of Northern Thailand with Lahu descendants.

Natural hot springs have been discovered in several areas in Thailand, and you will enjoy your visit to these natural phenomenons. After wards, you will make the journey back to Chiang Mai and arrive at your hotel approximately 6pm.

title.en: Live Like a Local: Rice Farmer for a Day from Chiang Mai

overview: Learn what it’s like to work as a rice farmer in the fields outside of Chiang Mai. As part of this day-long interactive experience, you’ll don a traditional Thai farming get-up and help harvest or plant rice along with local farmers. This hands-on private excursion includes round-trip transport from Chiang Mai to Thailand’s Phrao district, along with a well-earned Thai lunch and the expertise of a knowledgable guide. You’ll also stop by a farmer’s home in Baan Thungdang to enjoy tea and learn about rice varitals, then pay a visit to Baan Patang to see how rice is milled and stored.
highlights: Full-day rice farming experience from Chiang Mai
Drive a scenic route past a teak forest to the Phrao district of northern Thailand with a local guide
Exchange your clothes for traditional Thai workwear and meet local farmers Work in a rice field with supervised, hands-on planting
Sip tea at a rice farmer’s house and learn about the milling process
Includes lunch and round-trip hotel transport by minivan
expect: As the world's top rice exporter, Thailand is the perfect place to gain a working knowledge of rice farming. With hands-on experience in a northern Thai community, you’ll take part in the daily work of a rice farmer, helping to plant or harvest rice and learning about the many processes involved in reaching the final product.

After hotel pickup in the morning, depart by private, air-conditioned vehicle to the Phrao district. Traveling north along a scenic route with your guide, you’ll pass a teak forest and see other trees at Sri Lanna National Park and then arrive at a farm. Change into traditional Thai farm clothes and head out to a rice paddy, nestled against a forested mountain, where you will work alongside local farmers for approximately 1.5 hours. Discover age-old techniques for planting or harvesting rice grains on the plantation, learning under the supervision of a knowledgeable local.
When your work is done, take a break for lunch featuring Thai cuisine, resting sore muscles as you appreciate what it takes to grow your grain.

Then depart for Baan Thungdang, where your guide takes you to visit a typical farmer’s home. Stop by for a cup of tea and chat with the residents (with translation by your guide) to learn about the different rice varieties and hear legends about this staple grain. Gain more insight into the processes involved in rice farming with a visit to Baan Patang, where you’ll see how rice is stored and milled into rice powder. Before heading back to Chiang Mai, visit the villages of Baan Nameng and Baan Pa Ha, passing through more farmland and orchards along the way.
Your full-day tour ends with drop-off at your hotel.
Please note: This tour does not operate March - June as local farmers do not plant rice during this time.

overview: Enjoy a two night stay in Chiang Mai that includes visits to Buddhist temples Wat Umong and Wat Suan Dok, and a full day at Elephant Nature Park, an animal sanctuary outside the city. Enjoy learning about Buddhist traditions; go in-depth experience with the majestic elephants and other animals; browse the vendors at Kad Ton Payom flea market, and have free time to explore. expect: During this 2-night small-group tour, enjoy Chiang Mai's famous regional cuisine, admire beautiful temples and learn about Thai Buddhism, and spend the day with elephants at Elephant Nature Park, an animal sanctuary outside of the city. Travel by minibus and songthaew, and enjoy the ease of complimentary airport pickup. Includes two nights at a centrally located hotel, making it easy to explore Chiang Mai during your free time in the evenings. Includes accommodation in your choice of single or shared room, and transportation, meals and activities as described in the Itinerary below. Itinerary

Day 1: arrival in Chiang Mai If you fly into Chiang Mai, you’ll be picked up from the airport and transferred to your hotel. No activities planned today, so you can arrive at any time. Upon check-in, ask hotel reception for your welcome letter, which has information about your tour.

The rest of your day is free for you to explore Chiang Mai at your leisure. Ask for dining recommendations or set out on foot (or tuk-tuk) to see some of the many beautiful temples in northern Thailand’s most vibrant city. / Overnight
Day 2: Chiang Mai – Elephant Nature Park – Chiang Mai (B, L)

Set off early after breakfast with a scenic drive by minibus to the Elephant Nature Park, a sanctuary and rescue center for these majestic animals. Travel through the picturesque Mae Taeng Valley to the park, located approximately 37 miles (60 km) from Chiang Mai. Upon arrival, an expert nature guide greets your small group and shares stories about the orphaned elephants and hundreds of other rescued animals that live at the sanctuary, including dogs, buffalo, cats, horses, pigs, monkeys and cows. Observe the free-roaming elephants, learn about their plight in Southeast Asia and efforts to protect them. Have an opportunity to feed the elephants fruit treats before enjoying your own lunch: a delicious buffet of Thai and international dishes.

Next, enjoy a refreshing activity: bath time for elephants at the river! After a safety briefing, a guide accompanies you and the elephants on the short walk to the river. Scrub and bathe a tame elephant if you don’t mind getting wet when the elephants splash around. If you prefer to stay dry, you can delight in watching their playful antics from the riverbank. After a full day at the Elephant Nature Park, return to Chiang Mai and enjoy the evening at your leisure. / Overnight
Day 3: Chiang Mai (B)

Start early with a scenic ride by songthaew to the Kad Ton Payom flea market. Your guide purchases alms from the market to offer the monks — a Buddhist tradition that your guide explains. Next, enjoy a traditional breakfast such as rice soup, fried rice or grilled pork at the market. Then drive to Wat Umong, a 600-year-old temple known for its large painted pagoda and underground tunnel. Soak up the peaceful ambiance as the abbot speaks about Buddhist precepts. Afterward, continue to Wat Suan Dok to mingle with resident monks and learn about their way of life. Practice some basic meditation techniques and have the opportunity to make another alms offering.
Your tour concludes around midday, but you can depart from your accommodation at any time. With so much to do in Chiang Mai, you may want to spend a few more days exploring.

title.en: Private Tour: Lamphun Day Trip by Train from Chiang Mai

overview: Get an in-depth look at Lamphun on this private day trip from Chiang Mai. You’ll ride a local train to the ancient capital of the Hariphunchai Kingdom, where a local guide provides an overview of Buddhist temples, markets and an on-site textile museum. Visit a longan plantation for a unique wine tasting, and enjoy a Thai noodle lunch and local snacks, before returning to your hotel via the scenic Ping River by private air-conditioned car.
highlights: Private full-day sightseeing tour of Lamphun from Chiang Mai
Ride a one-way train to rural Lamphun and return on a scenic drive along the Ping
River
Visit several Buddhist temples: Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, Wat Phra Yuen and
Wat Chama Thewi (popularly called Wat Kukut)
Learn about the Tai Yong culture at a textile museum with your knowledgeable private guide

Hotel pickup and drop-off by air-conditioned private vehicle included
expect: Meet your private guide at your hotel lobby in the morning for a transfer to the Chiang Mai railway station, where you’ll board a local train for Lamphun, located a 30-minute ride away. A driver awaits your arrival in this ancient city of northern Thailand, whose temples you’ll explore on a private sightseeing tour with your guide. Visit Wat Phra Yen, where you’ll find four Buddha statues within a chedi (stupa). Make your way to the venerated Wat Phra That Hariphunchai, dating back to the Mon kingdom of the 11th or 12th century. Stroll to a nearby market where you’ll find OTOP (One Tambon One Product) items for sale — made locally in village communities. For lunch, enjoy a bowl of khao soi, a Thai noodle dish in a curry sauce with coconut milk.

Stop at a museum to see textiles made by Lamphun’s inhabitants — mostly descendants of the Tai Yong, an ethnic group from northern Burma (Myanmar). Continue on to another Lumphun market for a snack of local specialties before a visit to Wat Chama Thewi (Wat Kukut), one of the oldest religious structures in Lamphun. Once you spot multiple standing Buddhas peeking from the niches of the temple’s tall chedi, hop back in your private vehicle for the drive back to Chiang Mai.

Along the way, you’ll make a final stop at a longan plantation for a tasting of longan wine, made from lam yai, a lychee-type fruit. Then relax with views of the Ping River before drop- off at your hotel.

overview: Experience a serene religious tradition on a sunrise visit to a Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai. expect: A long-standing tradition in Thailand is the daily offering of alms to Buddhist monks. You can take part in this ritual on a 2-hour sunrise temple visit in Chiang Mai, which begins with a pick-up at your hotel at 6am.

Each morning before dawn the monks put on their distinctive saffron robes and quietly walk along the streets in their bare feet, carrying alms bowls and receiving boiled rice and condiments from local people along the way. In return, those giving alms receive blessings from the monks.

You can participate in this very special Thai custom by personally presenting alms. First you’ll enjoy a brief visit to the Sri Soda temple, and, religious festivals permitting, see the monks praying in the early morning. This activity makes for a unique addition to your holiday in Thailand.

expect: Tour Chiang Mai's craft hotspots, and discover the traditional techniques of the region's potters and wood carvers, beginning with an exploration of the restored settlement of Wiang Kum Kam.

Wiang Kum Kam was an early settlement that became King Mangrai's capital in the late 13th century. Flooding forced King Mangrai to move, but its original location remained important until the river changed course and buried the site in mud. Wiang Kum Kam was restored as a historical park during the 1980s, and it's set in a beautiful area surrounded by rice paddies and village houses.
Continue onward to Muang Kung, one of Thailand's most well-known pottery villages, before heading to Baan Tawai which, along with its nearby towns, forms the largest woodcarving center in Thailand.

Dozens of small workshops and factories produce imitation antiques and immense wooden elephants that are sold throughout the country. Bargains are plentiful, and if you spot a sculpture that you'd like to take home with you, larger shops provide packing and shipping services.

expect: Our driver will meet you at your hotel at 8:30am for our trip to the organic coffee farm Suan Lahu.

On the way you will drive past Doi Saket and onwards to the Mae Kachan Hot Springs. Just before the hot springs we will turn right and head into the mountains toward Chaesorn National Park. This is a beautiful journey and you will have time for photo stops on the way. On arrival at Suan Lahu you will be received by your native hosts, who will brief you on Suan Lahu and organic coffee growing. A local Lahu guide will take you around the 12 hectares of coffee plantation. Arabica coffee and fruit trees make up the majority of the plantation with a forest making up the rest. The views across the plantation are amazing. Having seen lychee, lemon and avocado trees, among others, you will have time for your first volunteer activity. There are a number of seasonal activities possible at the farm, ranging from taking care of farm animals (pigs and chicken), freeing the plants from strangulating vines, to grading, roasting, and harvesting the coffee beans. One of these activities will keep you busy until lunch time where a home made vegetarian lunch prepared by your hosts awaits you. After lunch you will visit the Lahu Sheleh community. A sub-group of the Black Lahu, they are an ethnic minority originating from the Tibet/China border area. We will show you some old pictures of the Lahu from yesteryear and show you around Doi Mod, the community located next to the organic coffee farm. After this we will head back to the farm for the afternoon’s activity which can be one of your own choosing. You can join local villagers working at the farm on a seasonal basis, or support Suan Lahu project founders in their natural and cultural restoration activities. At around 4pm you will say goodbye to your hosts after an active, educational and fun day full of interesting activities, fresh air, healthy food, and the most delicious coffee. We then head back to Chiang Mai.

title.en: Chiang Rai and Golden Triangle Day Tour from Chiang Mai

overview: Take a day trip to Chiang Rai and the Golden Triangle to see where the borders of Thailand, Burma and Laos converge.

With a knowledgeable guide, you’ll drive through scenic countryside, visit local hill tribe villages and soak at the Mae Ka Chan hot springs. Marvel at the White Temple (Wat Rong Khun) and enjoy views over the Mekong River as you learn about this region, notorious for its opium trade. Lunch and round-trip hotel transport from Chiang Mai are included.

expect: After early morning pickup from your hotel in Chiang Mai, relax during a scenic drive through the countryside in the air-conditioned comfort of your vehicle. En route to the Golden Triangle and Chiang Rai, listen as your guide details the full-day itinerary ahead and shares information about this former opium-producing capital.

Make a stop at the Mae Ka Chan hot springs, where you can soak sore muscles in three natural pools. Let tiny fish nibble dead skin from your feet, or purchase quail eggs to cook in the boiling waters.

Back in the vehicle, you’re taken to where the borders of Thailand, Myanmar (Burma) and Laos meet. From a viewpoint set high on a hillside, enjoy a panoramic vista over the three countries.Your guide points out the confluence of the Mekong and Ruak rivers; watch the scene unfold below or opt for a boat ride across the mighty Mekong (own expense). Continue on to Mae Sai, the northernmost trading post located near the Thailand-Myanmar border, where a regional lunch is served.

Nearing the lovely city of Chiang Rai, your guide accompanies you to Wat Rong Khun — aka the White Temple — a contemporary complex made of shimmering glass and painted white plaster rebuilt by a local artist who began construction in 1997. On the return journey to Chiang Mai you’ll visit the hill tribe villages of Akha and Yao before drop-off at your hotel.

title.en: Whitewater Rafting Adventure in Chiang Mai

overview: Tackle some of Thailand’s best whitewater rapids on a full-day rafting adventure from Chiang Mai. Expert guides ensure your safety as you cruise through the jungle along class III and IV rapids, and an included lunch and other amenities make for a worry-free day in the wilds of Northern Thailand.
highlights: Full-day whitewater rafting trip from Chiang Mai
Navigate some of Thailand's best class III and IV rapids
Great way to experience the unspoiled jungle scenery of Northern Thailand
Course can be customized for different experience levels
Safety is a top priority for expert river guides
Includes a lunch with vegetarian options available
expect: Prepare for morning pickup at your Chiang Mai hotel, and drive around 1.5 hours to reach the rafting base camp. When you arrive, get a safety orientation and gear up with state-of-the-art helmets and life vests. The camp provides all the amenities you need to stay comfortable, including lockers, changing rooms with showers, and a minimart to pick up any last-minute snacks or supplies before launching onto the water.

The river course features three different sections, beginning with a relatively calm stretch that winds through a lush, shady jungle and contains one class III rapid to warm up your paddling skills. Next, prepare to get wet on an adrenaline-pumping section peppered with class III and IV rapids that count among some of Thailand’s best whitewater. Finally, relax and soak up the scenery during a period of calm before finishing up the 6-mile (10-km) course with a thrilling patch of near-continuous rapids.

Rafters under the age of 15 or those who are less experienced can opt to skip the more challenging sections of the course by hopping out of the river and riding in a van along a road for about 1.2 miles (2 km), then rejoining the group after the most difficult stretch. Please note that river conditions can change depending on water levels. During high water times, total time on the river will be about 2 hours, while lower levels generally result in a 2.5-hour trip. After your victorious trip down the river, shower and change into dry clothes if you like and enjoy an included lunch of fried chicken with rice, fruit, salad, coffee, and tea. Vegetarian options are also available if requested in advance. Relax on the return ride to Chiang Mai, where the adventure concludes with hotel drop-off in the afternoon.

overview: Come and join our Elephant’s Friend Day at Baanchang Elephant Park while you are in Chiang Mai. This special program is giving our visitors an opportunity to care for our elephants, visit to the Elephant Dung Paper Factory and see their natural habitat. Lunch and round-trip hotel transfer is included. Please note that riding is not allowed during this tour.

Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
See native wildlife in their natural environment
Close encounter with wildlife

expect: Our driver will pick you up from your hotel lobby in Chiang Mai city area around 8:30am and head to Baanchang Elephant Park. Enjoy an hour scenic drive passing by local shops, villages and jungle.

Next, we will visit to an Elephant Dung Paper Factory to witness the process of making paper from dung. Elephant dung is a renewable source of material and this makes it an environmentally responsible alternative to ordinary paper. You will be surprised with the paper quality made from the world’s largest land mammals.

After the short tour at dung paper factory, you will get a chance to spend some quality time with this gentle giants, gain an insight into their history and behaviors. We will allocate some bananas and sugar cane to feed to our elephants and then bring them for a walk in the jungle. Once we return back from a jungle walk, you will walk with the elephants to our pond and join them in the water for refreshing bath. You can bathe and brush them with endless amount of fun. Please remember to take some beautiful photos while elephants playing with you. To finish off you will be changed back to your own clothes and enjoy the delicious lunch prepared by our staff at the park. Our driver will transfer you back to your hotel safely around 4pm after a wonderful experience at Baanchang Elephant Park.

title.en: Opium Trail Trek Including Wat Phra That Doi Suthep and Hmong Village Tour

overview: Take a privately guided walk on an old opium trail in Northern Thailand, where you’re accompanied by a local Hmong guide between mountain villages. You’ll visit the Hmong communities of Doi Pui and Ban Mae Sa Mai, and learn about the people and plants of Doi Suthep-Pui National Park, whose slopes once supported a prolific opium trade. Your full-day private tour includes a stop at Phra That Doi Suthep Temple, the FORRU tree nursery and a Hmong museum, plus a picnic lunch and round-trip hotel transport by minibus.
highlights: Full-day opium trail tour from Chiang Mai Drive to the Hmong village of Doi Pui View Phra That Doi Suthep Temple with a private local guide Embark on a 4-hour trek through Doi Suthep-Pui National Park Visit Ban Mae Sa Mai, Northern Thailand’s largest Hmong community Thai picnic lunch and FORRU project donation included Hotel pickup and drop-off by private vehicle
expect: Meet your guide during hotel pickup in Chiang Mai and get comfortable in your private minibus for the drive to Doi Suthep-Pui National Park. Your first stop is Phra That Doi Suthep Temple, a 14th-century Buddhist monastery that houses an Emerald Buddha replica. Arrive before the crowds for a look at the ornate murals and classic Thai design, and climb the 300 steps for a panoramic view over Chiang Mai.

Hear about the complicated history of the local Hmong community en route to Doi Pui village, where you’ll meet up with a Hmong guide to accompany you on a hike to Ban Mae Sa Mai village, the largest Hmong community in Northern Thailand. The 4-hour trek to the Mae Sa Valley follows a leisurely pace along a nature trail, taking you through dense forest past wild banana trees and water features, and includes photo stops. Learn some plant and tree identification, and hear about the opium cultivation once prevalent in the region, which now supports fruit trees and other agricultural projects. Eat a Thai picnic lunch at a scenic spot and get a glimpse of an alleged footprint of the Buddha. Upon reaching Ban Mae Sa Mai, you’ll find few visitors in marked contrast with Doi Pui. Learn about the forest restoration project of Chiang Mai University called FORRU, which your included donation fee supports. Visit the FORRU tree nursery and a small Hmong museum before your private vehicle transports you back to Chiang Mai.

overview: This private day trip from Chiang Mai provides an immersive experience with local elephant conservation efforts .Tour the hospital, watch infants at the nursery, and feed and bathe the elephants. Your visit to the Friends of the Asian Elephant and the Thai Elephant Conservation Center near Lampang includes lunch and a stop at the Ban Chang Nak museum with an optional elephant ride and crafts workshop. Relax via air-conditioned transport by private minibus and enjoy the personalized attention of a private guide.
highlights: Participate in a variety of elephant-related activities

Meet rehabilitated elephants at the Friends of the Asian Elephant Foundation and the Thai Elephant Conservation Center Feed elephants, see them bathe and watch them paint and play during an entertaining show

expect: This exclusive visit to Friends of the Asian Elephant Foundation and the Thai Elephant Conservation Center (TECC) introduces you to these endangered animals and their plight. Meet your guide upon pickup at your Chiang Mai hotel in the morning and relax on the approximate 1.5-hour drive by private vehicle toward Lampang. On arrival, watch a short video about Mosha and Motala, two elephants who survived landmine injuries, including one who received the world’s first elephant prosthetic. You’ll meet these gentle giants at the elephant hospital and learn about the foundation’s efforts to improve the fate of Thailand’s elephants.

Your guide accompanies you next door to TECC, where you can interact with elephant moms and their infants at the nursery, feed and help bathe the majestic creatures. Before or after a Thai lunch at the center, you can opt for a 30-minute or 1-hour tandem elephant ride (own expense). Departing for Chiang Mai, make a brief stop at Mae Ta, a small market selling local goods. You’ll visit Ban Chang Nak, a museum and artist workshop founded by a master carver of wooden elephants. Admire hundreds of works by local artists on display, and later have the opportunity to paint your own miniature elephant during a crafts workshop at the Elephant Parade House in Chiang Mai (additional expense), before hotel drop-off in the early evening.

title.en: Private Tour: Mae Kampong Village from Chiang Mai

overview: Spend an afternoon in and around Ban Mae Kampong, a high-altitude village in the mountains north of Chiang Mai that’s known for its tea production. A knowledgable guide accompanies you on this day-long private tour, which includes a Thai massage and a trek to a nearby waterfall. You’ll also prepare a culinary feast at a village home alongside locals. Includes air- conditioned transportation to and from your Chiang Mai hotel.
highlights: Full-day private tour of Mae Kampong village
Hike a nature trail to Mae Kampong waterfall and enjoy a 1-hour Thai massage
Learn about fermented tea production on a village tour with a knowledgeable guide

expect: Start your full-day, private tour with pickup from your hotel in Chiang Mai. Depart for Ban Mae Kampong. You’re enlightened with a brief history of the village before an easy forest trek, following your guide along a nature trail past a tea and coffee plantation and fruit orchards to Mae Kampong waterfall.

Enjoy great photo ops of the wide cascade, which falls down seven levels. Then walk back to the village for a delicious home-cooked or picnic-style lunch, served while you have time to relax. Any sore muscles from your hike will be soothed with a 1-hour Thai massage, as limbs are maneuvered and rhythmic pressure is applied to your body while you remain fully clothed. Follow up with a guided village tour and learn about forest-tea orchard farming. Most of the villagers in the small mountain community of Ban Mae Kampong are engaged in the production of fermented tea, called miang, and you’ll see some being made along with handicrafts in local homes.

In the late afternoon, visit a village home and learn to cook your own Thai meal. Afterward, enjoy dinner and watch the sunset from a mountaintop before the 1.5-hour return to Chiang Mai by private vehicle with drop-off at your hotel.

overview: Learn what it’s like to work as a rice farmer in the fields outside of Chiang Mai. As part of this day-long interactive experience, you’ll don a traditional Thai farming get-up and help harvest or plant rice along with local farmers. This hands-on private excursion includes round-trip transport from Chiang Mai to Thailand’s Phrao district, along with a well-earned Thai lunch and the expertise of a knowledgable guide. You’ll also stop by a farmer’s home in Baan Thungdang to enjoy tea and learn about rice varitals, then pay a visit to Baan Patang to see how rice is milled and stored.
highlights: Full-day rice farming experience from Chiang Mai

expect: As the world's top rice exporter, Thailand is the perfect place to gain a working knowledge of rice farming. With hands-on experience in a northern Thai community, you’ll take part in the daily work of a rice farmer, helping to plant or harvest rice and learning about the many processes involved in reaching the final product After hotel pickup in the morning, depart by private, air-conditioned vehicle to the Phrao district. Traveling north along a scenic route with your guide, you’ll pass a teak forest and see other trees at Sri Lanna National Park and then arrive at a farm. Change into traditional Thai farm clothes and head out to a rice paddy, nestled against a forested mountain, where you will work alongside local farmers for approximately 1.5 hours. Discover age-old techniques for planting or harvesting rice grains on the plantation, learning under the supervision of a knowledgeable local.
When your work is done, take a break for lunch featuring Thai cuisine, resting sore muscles as you appreciate what it takes to grow your grain.

Then depart for Baan Thungdang, where your guide takes you to visit a typical farmer’s home. Stop by for a cup of tea and chat with the residents (with translation by your guide) to learn about the different rice varieties and hear legends about this staple grain. Before heading back to Chiang Mai, visit the villages of Baan Nameng and Baan Pa Ha, passing through more farmland and orchards along the way.

title.en: Evening Kantoke Dinner in Chiang Mai

overview: An evening one may not soon forget: culturally-enriched with a succulent dinner, northern Thai style where the beauty and grace of dance and musical performance is presented at one of the leading Kantoke restaurants in Chiang Mai.

expect: An evening filled of a culturally important even that is something typical of the northern part of Thailand. It was not until 1953 that Khan Toke became a social gathering when a local politician invited high honored guests to sit with him and enjoy this special dinner. Northern Thailand boasts a culinary tradition all its own, much of it influenced by neighboring countries. From Laos, comes a love for sticky rice and a distinctive use of chillies; from Myanmar, unique curries, generally un-thickened by coconut milk as in other parts of Thailand; and from China, a preference for noodles. The “Khan Toke” dinner is traditionally specific to the people of the northern region that has elements of it all combined into one. It is a short ride from your hotel to the venue where you will be welcomed by the staff who will guide you to your table where your Kantoke dinner is served. Dinner is served in small bowls, known in Thai as Khan and guests are seated cross-legged on cushions at a low table, known as Toke in Thai. The cuisine served is northern Thai and it is prepared with the western palate in mind as traditional Thai food can be very spicy. During dinner, entertainers will perform the intricate Forn Leb finger dance; the Forn Thien candle dance; the Ramwong circle dance; and the Ram Dab sword dance. Opt for an additional hill tribe show performed by various members of the Yao, Lahu, Meo, Lisu, and Karen hill tribes after you have finished dinner.
After this dinner and dance performance, we will bring you back to your hotel.

title.en: 4-Night Experience in Chiang Mai: Palong Villages Stay and Chiang Dao Trek

overview: Set out from Chiang Mai to trek through northern Thailand’s mountainous jungle on a three-day private tour. With an experienced guide by your side, you’ll explore the area around Chiang Dao, visiting Karen, Akha and other remote hill tribe villages, dining on (and if you like, helping prepare) northern Thai cuisine, and bedding down in bamboo huts. You’ll even have time to enjoy Chiang Mai and its offerings at your own pace with sightseeing tips catered specifically to your interests.
highlights: 4-night northern Thailand private tour with three-day trek round-trip from Chiang
Mai
Strap on your backpack and follow your expert guide into the jungle near Chiang
Dao
Stay overnight in two Palong villages and visit several more

expect: Immerse yourself in the Chiang Dao region of northern Thailand for a memorable experience trekking through the jungle and visiting several hill tribe villages, including those of the Palong, Akha, Lahu and Karen peoples. Your adventurous tour includes three days of trekking in the mountains, walking for 1-4 hours between villages. You will need a decent level of fitness to participate as you will carry your own backpack and personal gear. This cultural experience includes two nights' accommodation in bamboo huts in a hill tribe village where living conditions are modest. Your experienced guide will assist you with any questions along the way. You’ll also have two nights of accommodation at a hotel in Chiang Mai, where you’ll have plenty of time to explore the city at your leisure. Itinerary
Day 1:

Chiang Mai Arrive at your Chiang Mai hotel anytime before your 6:30pm welcome meeting. If you arrive early, enjoy exploring northern Thailand’s vibrant capital, with dozens of stunning temples, a lively riverfront, great shopping at outdoor markets and a variety of small shops, and numerous options for delicious Thai cuisine.

After your welcome meeting, you’ll have the option to follow your guide on a leisurely stroll through the old city or choose to peruse Chiang Mai on your own (all activities at own expense)./ Overnight
Day 2:

Chiang Mai – Palong village (L, D) Your guide will pick you up from your hotel in the morning and you’ll head north to Chiang Dao. Along the way you’ll stop at a local market in Mae Malai to shop for food for your trek. Your guide will show you the ingredients used in Thai cooking as you gather the materials for your journey ahead.

Hop back in your vehicle and continue to the Mae Tang River, where you board a bamboo raft for a refreshing float down the river. Enjoy the relaxing ride and river scenery, then disembark and meet your driver. From there, you’ll take a ride through the northern town of Chiang Dao to an Akha village called Ban Huay Hok.

In Ban Huay Hok you’ll put on your backpack and set out on the first leg of your trek, a 1- hour hike to the Palong village of Pang Deng Nai. Follow your guide along lush jungle trails and hear about how the royal projects – sponsored by the Thai royal family – created villages like Pang Deng Nai to give economic and educational opportunities to hill tribe peoples. Savor lunch when you arrive at the first village, then you’ll continue to another Palong village named Pang How, where you will stay the night. After you meet your local hosts and set your pack down, your guide will introduce you to northern Thai cooking and show you how to make some favorite dishes for your dinner tonight. After enjoying your meal, head over to another home and hear stories about the history of the Palong people and the village. / Overnight
Day 3: Hill Tribe Trekking – Chiang Mai (B, L, D)

After awakening to the sounds of roosters and village life, enjoy breakfast with your guide before exploring the village. Learn about your surroundings from your guide. Afterward, say goodbye to your hosts and hit the trail for a 2-hour hike to a waterfall where you can take a dip in the water and nibble on a picnic lunch.

When you’re rejuvenated, you’ll continue along the trail for 3-4 hours, listening to your expert guide talk about the forest’s plant and animal life. Find wild ginger, rattan and pitcher plants as you walk along the jungle trail, and learn the many ways that bamboo is used locally.

Once you reach another Palong village known as Huay Bong, take time to rest and meet the local people. Have the option to help your guide prepare the night’s meal and learn more about Thai cuisine, then enjoy dinner and a campfire where you share stories with your guide and the people in the village. / Overnight
Day 4:

Palong village – Chiang Mai (B, L) Join your guide for breakfast then grab your pack and walk about an hour to the Karen village of Thakilek, the last part of your trek. Along the way you’ll stop in at a Lahu village and check out their spirit temple and blacksmith. In Thakilek, your guide shows you around the village and introduces you to the Karen people.

Bid farewell to the village community, and head back to Chiang Mai with your guide. Celebrate your trekking accomplishments with a tasty lunch at a local restaurant. Once you have refueled, stop in at an orchid nursery where you can check out the varieties of this beautiful flower. Your guide will return you by songthaew (covered truck with bench seats) to your hotel in Chiang Mai in the afternoon.

Say goodbye to your guide and settle into your Chiang Mai hotel, then enjoy the evening at your leisure. You could opt to soothe sore muscles with a traditional herbal sauna and Thai massage or indulge in a festive meal at one of Chiang Mai’s many fantastic restaurants. / Overnight
Day 5:

Chiang Mai (B) You have the freedom to leave at any time for your next destination, or set your own itinerary if you choose to stay in Chiang Mai for a few days. Explore the gorgeous temple of Wat Phrathat Doi Sutep – located on a hill above the city with stunning views, take a Thai cooking class, shop for local goods or catch live music at a riverside cafe (own expense).

overview: See the best of northern Thailand with a 4-day tour from Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai, and explore hill tribe villages, mountain temples and local culture. Climb past the fierce naga serpents at Wat Phrathat Doi Suthep, see a fresh flower market and take in a traditional show. Experience an elephant camp, ride a longtail boat and explore the far north before finishing your tour in Chiang Rai.
