Itinerary
Day 1:

You will be picked up from your hotel in Chiang Mai around 1:30pm and will explore the ancient city of Chiang Mai. The first stop is 160feet (48m) high Wat Suan Dok and you will see behind these white Chedi rises a golden bell shape edifice. A short drive to visit Wat Phra Sing located within the old city walls and continue to Wat Chedi Luang, the historic centre of Chiang Mai. You will visit the Wat Ched Yod and Wat Chiang Man before heading back to the hotel in Chiang Mai around 6:30pm. Please note, no meals included.
Day 2:

On the second day of your tour, you will enjoy the stunning panoramic views over the city at Wat Prathat Doi Suthep. If you adventures enough, try to climb up a 309 steps Naga staircase to reach the temple or you can use the cable car service. Next, you will visit a historical landmark, Wararot Market a long standing market, known for its variety of speciality Chiang Mai food and products, followed by a visit to the flower market. Enjoy a pleasant Northern Thai Khantoke dinner accompanied by an authentic Lanna traditional show and performances. You will return to the hotel around 9:30pm and overnight in Chiang Mai. Please note, breakfast and dinner are included.
Day 3:

In the morning visit the Thai Elephant Care Center, which was set up to provide care for elderly elephants retired from logging and camps. There are no rides, but visitors learn about how the old-timers are fed with ground grass and herb balls, and if time of visit is right, you could watch the bath-time, as well as visiting the cemetery for elephants who have died of old age. After lunch, join a relaxing long - tail boat to Chiang Rai through the panoramic views of surrounding mountains and jungle of Kok River. Ride past the magnificent local villages of Muser and Karen hill tribes located alongside the river. Arrive Chiang Rai in the afternoon and take a short transfer to your hotel. Overnight in Chiang Rai. Breakfast and lunch included.
Day 4:

After breakfast, we will check out of the hotel and visit Wat Rongkhun (White Temple). You will continue to the ancient Chiang Saen city and have lunch at the Imperial Golden Triangle Resort then transfer back to Chiang Rai Airport. Please note that transfer to Outer-Chiang Rai hotels will be subject to supplement charges. The tour will finish around 2pm and you are recommended depart from Chiang Rai Airport at 3:45pm. Please note, breakfast and lunch are included.

title.en: 4-Day Northern Thailand Mountain-Biking Adventure from Chiang Mai Overview

overview: Join us on this trip to experience our most popular mountain bike route over four days of great cycling from the hills of Chiangdao to the Maekok river valley. Ride your sturdy mountain-bike through scenic areas with plenty of exciting trails and sights and discover small villages along the way, including ethnic hill tribes of Northern Thailand. This trip is a true cycling adventure, at your own pace with the full support of our dedicated staff.
highlights: Multi-Day Trip
All-inclusive tour
Small-group tour
Led by a local guide
All necessary equipment included
Vegetarian meal option available
expect: Day 1:

Chiang Mai to Chiangdao (cycling distance 30 to 45 km/ 18 to 28 miles) You will be picked up from your Chiang Mai hotel and driven north to the Chiangdao valley, our starting point. After a short briefing and bike fitting, we will start pedaling on easy dirt road trails linking hill tribe villages. Visit Lahu and Akha villages, as well as the Palaung people from Myanmar, with only a few settlements in northern Thailand. Thai set lunch at local restaurant. The afternoon will be spent riding along rural back roads and pristine landscape. The imposing Doi Luang Chiang Dao, the country's third tallest mountain being always in the background. Arrive at the Chiang Dao caves, a Buddhist sanctuary, for some exploration. Ride your bike, or transfer by vehicle to the Padeng Lodge for overnight. Enjoy a succulent dinner served at the lodge. Meals: lunch and dinner.
Day 2:

Chiangdao to Ban Thaton (cycling distance 30 to 60 km cycling / 20 to 38 miles) This morning we ride through more scenic landscape! The route is not too difficult and the escort vehicle is always with us. Our morning cycling distance will be approximately 30 km (20 miles), on a mix of dirt trails and paved roads. Lunch stop and visit at another Buddhist forest temple. Afternoon cycling distance is 25 km on paved road, followed by a vehicle transfer to Ban Thaton for overnight. Thaton is a small village located by the Burmese border on the bank of the Maekok River. Dinner at local restaurant. Meals: breakfast, lunch and dinner
Day 3:

Ban Thaton to Chiang Rai Town, with a scenic route along the river (distances 45 to 60 km cycling / 28 to 38 miles) Early morning, after breakfast, we cycle through the Maekok river valley, passing rice fields and plantations. We then follow an exciting trail winding its way along the river. Next we ride a local long-tail boat downriver, to reach a forest park and take our bike again, to continue cycling to a Karen village by the river. After a short visit, we ride, or transfer by car, to our Chiang Rai hotel. Evening and dinner free at leisure. If you are not tired, you can stroll the local night market. Meals: breakfast and lunch.
Day 4:

Chiang Rai Hhalf Day Cycling Loop, and back to Chiang Mai (Cycling distance between 20 to 40 km / 12 to 24 miles) Cycling itinerary is flexible today and to some extent will depends on the season. We ride out of the city and follow the river bank to discover exciting new trails. Cycle a loop up the mountain village, and downhill on the other side. Ride back in the valley to reach a waterfall for a local lunch. Relax and shower at the waterfall before an overland transfer back to Chiang Mai (3 hours+). Drop off at your hotel in the city. Meals: breakfast and lunch.

title.en: 2-Day Elephant Experience from Chiang Mai

overview: Experience life in a Thai elephant camp with a 2-day tour from Chiang Mai, and wash, play and hike with elephants. Sleep in a traditional village, learn about Karen culture and get a glimpse of day to day life among the Hill Tribes. Spend most of each day with the elephants, help them through their routines and hear the story of each individual creature. Float the Mae Wang River on a bamboo raft, and enjoy the serene pace of life in the Thai countryside before returning to Chiang Mai.
highlights: 2-day elephant camp visit from Chiang Mai
Sleep in a traditional Karen village
Learn about life in the countryside
Wash, hike and play with elephants
Meet Thai mahouts
Fun experience, perfect for families
All-inclusive tour
expect: Itinerary Day 1:

Pick up from your hotel in Chiang Mai before 8am. After a 90 minute drive we will arrive in the village of Mae Sapok, where you can leave your belongings in your accommodation for the duration of your stay. We stop for a quick tea break and then brief you on the planned itinerary days ahead and then take a short ride to our elephant camp. On our arrival you learn about elephants in general and about the tradition of keeping elephants in Asia. We then spend some time getting to know the elephants and hearing the stories and characters of each of our big friendly giants. This will give you a better understanding of our beloved project and everything we are trying to do. After meeting each of the elephants we take a break for lunch.

After lunch you lead your elephant to the nearby river and enjoy giving them a long bath. Your elephant keepers and your English speaking tour guides will always be around and supporting you in everything you do. With your elephant you then make your way back to the park.

Whilst teh elephants enjoy some free time you can take the opportunity to visit the village of Mae Sapok. Most residents here are people from the Karen mountain tribe. We introduce you to the lifestyle of the Karen and explain how they adapt to the challenges of the 21st century. This is not a show village for tourists. It is a very real village and will allow you to truly see how this part of Thailand lives.

After a relaxing shower in your room you can enjoy a sumptuous dinner in the dining area of your accommodation. You will then have the opportunity to attend a screening of a video film about elephants.
Day 2:

After breakfast we head straight to the elephant camp accompanied by your trainer. From there you take a walk into the surrounding forest, where you pick up the elephant from their night time sleeping areas. You lead the animals back to the elephant camp and will be getting more and more confident due to the experience gained from the previous day. On arrival our trained mahouts will show you how the elephants used to work in the logging industry. After our goodbyes to the elephants we enjoy lunch with a spectacular view from our Lodge the "White House". After lunch we drive to the starting point of the bamboo raft experience. You will appreciate this relaxed method of transportation along the idyllic and simultaneously spectacular mountain river Mae Wang River.

Upon arrival at the accommodation you have the opportunity to enjoy a shower before heading back to Chiang Mai, where you will arrive around 5.30pm with memorable impressions of a unique and amazing experience.

overview: Doi Inthanon National park with it’s highest peak rising 2,565 metres above sea level is located just one hour’s drive from Chiang Mai city. During 2 days of exploration, participants will visit Doi Inthanon main attractions and trek through valley and jungle. We will get the chance to meet with Karen hill-tribe people during an overnight stay with a local family. Watch or listen to birds in the forest, refresh in waterfalls, and visit the two pagodas near the summit.

All entrance fees included

Informative, friendly and professional guide

expect: Day 1:

Trek and overnight in hill-tribe village Meeting at your hotel with your guide and depart by private vehicle heading South-West to Doi Inthanon National park’s entrance. Enter the park and drive to the summit. Go for a short hike on a wooden pathway called the “Angka Trail”, with moss-covered tress, wild orchids and various bird species. Continue by vehicle to visit the two impressive pagodas near the summit, offering breathtaking views of the valley. Head to the park headquarter by vehicle for lunch. Visit the Royal project initiated to help the hill tribes with modern agricultural practices. The rest of the afternoon is a trek through the jungle, with its unique flora and many bird species. We will end the trek with a relaxing time at a waterfall and spend the night in a Karen village home stay. A gourmet Thai dinner is prepared by your guide. (Meals: L, D). Hiking 2 to 2.5 hours, easy trail.
Day 2 :

Trek, refreseshing water fall, and drive back to Chiang Mai At breakfast, participants will taste locally grown fresh coffee. We will drive to another Karen village, where we will trek down the mountain slopes and stunning rice terraces cultivated by Karen villagers. Meet with our vehicle and transfer to the stunning Vachiratarn Waterfall, for a local Thai style picnic lunch. In the afternoon, simply relax or visit a second waterfall equally beautiful, located by the Park’s entrance, the Mae Klang waterfall. Transfer back to Chiang Mai. Drop off at your hotel in Chiang Mai or directly to the airport. (Meals: B, L). Hiking is 2 to 2.5 hours on mostly descending trail.

title.en: 2-Day Kindred Spirit Elephant Sanctuary in Chiang Mai

overview: Come and see elephants in the most ethical way - in their natural habitat. Immerse yourself in hill-tribe culture by staying and cooking in a traditional hill-tribe homestay and learning the basic skills that have been passed down through their generation such as basket weaving and bamboo cup making. Hike through the jungle to find the elephants and spend the day with them. Eat lunch with our elephants in the forest and then return to Chiang Mai in the afternoon.
highlights: See native wildlife in their natural environment
Once-in-a-Lifetime Experience
Small group ensures personal service
Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Family friendly
Get inside tips from a local
expect: Join us at Kindred Spirit Elephant Sanctuary! We are a Non-Profit Foundation who are dedicated to giving our elephants the best life possible with the help of our visitors and volunteers. Our aim is to bring elephants home to the forest by working with the local communities to not only provide a haven for our elephants, but also provide an alternative livelihood for their mahouts and owners. Our elephants have been taken from a life of inadequate health care, poor diet, exhaustion and entertaining tourists, they were unable to just be elephants. We brought these wonderful creatures back to their natural environment where they are living in semi-wild conditions, free to roam as much as possible and live their lives how they choose – interacting and foraging. We plan to bring elephants of all ages and sizes home to the forest. Our tours run daily so you can sign up for any day of the week.
Day 1:

Pickup from Chiang Mai at 9am. Travel through a national park and stunning mountains inhabited by local hill tribes until you arrive in our unique village. Meet your homestay family, our friendly staff and the other volunteers, immerse yourself in hill tribe culture by cooking with your homestay and learning how to basket weave from one of the elders in the village.
Day 2:

Wake up early to hike in the forest and find our elephants. Feed these gentle giant mammals fruit and carry out a health check. Spend all morning and afternoon observing and learning about them and their natural behaviors. Have lunch in the forest with the elephants and return to Chiang Mai in the afternoon.

title.en: 3-Day Mae Hong Son Loop Motorcycle Tour from Chiang Mai

overview: The Mae Hon Son Loop is a comprehensive way to discover one of Thailand’s most authentic provinces. For those wanting to see the real Thailand and wanting to ride a biker´s paradise, the Mae Hong Son Loop is the perfect antidote.
Mae Hong Son is the most mountainous province in Thailand and receives little traffic due to its relatively remote location and time needed to reach it.
highlights: Multi-Day Trip
Enjoy fantastic aerial views
Step back in time on a history tour
Get up-close to native wildlife
Get inside tips from a local
Informative, friendly and professional guide
expect: This excursion will take you first to the highest peak of Thailand (Doi Inthanon with 8,415 feet or 2,565 meters above sea level). Ride along winding and narrow twisty curvy roads with high mountain scenery along the Myanmar border on perfect tarmac roads. 1,864 curves through a vast panorama view of Mae Hong Son and the charming Pai. National Parks and non-touristic places full of unique history and activities.
Day 1. Chiang Mai – Doi Inthanon – Mae Sariang (170 miles or 275 kms.)

Early morning meet and greet at your accommodation in Chiang Mai. We will provide the tour briefing, and then your riding gear and bike. We will inform you briefly of local history, geography and acknowledge any personal requirements. Lastly we have a general Q&A opportunity for any concerns you might have related to the tour.
Day 2. Mae Sariang – Mae Hong Son – Pai (169 miles or 273 kms.)

After breakfast, leave Mae Sariang to Mae Hong Son on narrow twisty curvy roads. In Khun Yuam we make a break and visit a World War II museum. Visit the long-neck Karen tribe village near the border of Thailand and Myanmar. Visit Wat Phra That Doi Kong Mu, the first temple of Mae Hong Son on the hilltop. Lunch is served at a local restaurant. Visit Lod cave, which means, “cave with stream running through”, on a bamboo raft. Then back on twisty curvy roads to Pai. Visit Tha Pai hot spring, where you can enjoy a mineral bath. Then we reach a charming accommodation with swimming pool.
Day 3

Pai – Chiang Mai (84 miles or 135 kms.) Before breakfast, in the very early morning you have a chance to offer food to the monks along the streets of Pai`s local market. After breakfast, visit the Pai World War II Memorial Bridge. Back on winding mountainous roads to Mok Fah waterfall. Lunch is served at a local restaurant. Continue along winding roads, passing farming areas before heading back to Chiang Mai City.

title.en: 3-Day Magical Golden Triangle Motorcycle Tour from Chiang Mai

overview: This excursion will take you to the most famous Golden Triangle at the Mekong river – the border between Thailand, Myanmar and Laos. You will discover the lovely Tha Ton, the impressive mountainous scenery of Doi Mae Salong, Doi Tung Royal Villa and unseen Phayao. Ride along winding and narrow twisty curvy roads with high mountain scenery. Lots of sightseeing and unforgettable memories as you pass through amazing natural, historical, traditional and cultural attractions.
highlights: Multi-Day Trip
Airport transfer
Step back in time on a history tour
Enjoy fantastic aerial views
Get inside tips from a local
Informative, friendly and professional guide
expect: Early morning meet and greet at your accommodation in Chiang Mai. We will provide the tour briefing, then your riding gear and bike. We will inform you briefly of local history, geography and acknowledge any personal requirements. Lastly we have a general Q&A opportunity for any concerns you might have related to the tour.
Day 1. Chiang Mai – Tha Ton (111miles or 179 kms.)

We take the highway, heading north of Chiang Mai to Mae Sa Elephant Camp, where you will feed the elephants, see them bathing and performing their talents. Continue to reach to Chiang Dao, where relaxing lunch at local restaurant. After lunch, visit Chiang Dao cave. Then ride along fantastic mountainous road until reach to Tha Ton, where you will visit the Wat Tha Ton on top of the mountains and enjoy the amazing sunset there. Later you relax in your charming accommodation with fantastic panorama view.
Day 2. Tha Ton – Golden Triangle (87 miles or 140 kms.)

After breakfast, we leave Tha Ton to visit the long-neck Karen tribe village near the border of Thailand and Myanmar. Riding to Doi Mae Salong, where Chinese mountain tea farmers live. Of course, you will test Thailand´s best tea there. Then back on curvy roads to Doi Tung Royal Villa. Visit the Winter Palace and the botanical garden. Lunch is served at the Royal’s Project restaurant. Continue along winding roads to Mae Sai, the northern most point of Thailand. Visit Wat Tham Pla where you can feed some food to wild monkeys. Reach the Golden Triangle to take a long-tailed-boat trip and short visit a small village in Laos (no Visa necessary). Visit the Opium museum before relaxing at your peaceful accommodation.
Day 3 Golden Triangle – Phayao – Chiang Mai (193 miles or 311 kms.)

After breakfast, ride along a scenic farming areas road to Chiang Rai City. After that, visit the White Temple (Wat Rong Khun) one of the top 10 wonder temples in the world. Continue on a long highway ride until we reach Phayao, visit Phayao lake (Kwan Phayao) one of the largest lakes in Northern Thailand. Lunch is served at a local restaurant in front of the lake. Continue riding on windy mountain roads to Tharntong waterfall and Mae Kachan hot spring. Visit a local market, stopping for refreshment, before heading back to Chiang Mai.

title.en: 3-Day Sukhothai Loop Motorcycle Tour from Chiang Mai

overview: The “Sukhothai Loop” will not only take you to see ancient historical of Thailand, unseen Phayao and Nan, Sirikit dam, Sukhothai (the world heritage historical park) and world´s first elephant hospital in Lampang. In 3 days you will also ride over 621 miles or 1,000 kms. We know what you want: great roads, no traffic, no speed cams and stunning scenery. The “Sukhothai Loop” can deliver all that.
highlights: Multi-Day Trip
Airport transfer
Enjoy fantastic aerial views
Get inside tips from a local
See native wildlife in their natural environment
Informative, friendly and professional guide
expect: Ride the famous highway No. 1148, ranked as one of the top 10 best riding roads all over the world. This amazing motorcycle road takes us through fabulous mountain scenery to Nan. Ride along the unique panorama of the border between Laos and Thailand. Cross the Sirikit dam reservoir on a wooden ferry and visit the World Heritage Historical Park of Sukhothai. A Real Motorcycle Tour for Real Riders!

Early morning meet and greet at your accommodation in Chiang Mai. We will provide the tour briefing, and then your riding gear and bike. We will inform you briefly of local history, geography and acknowledge any personal requirements. Lastly we have a general Q&A opportunity for any concerns you might have related to the tour.
Day 1. Chiang Mai – Phayao – Nan (247miles or 398 kms.)

Get familiarize the bikes by heading north of Chiang Mai. You will ride on windy mountain road to Tharntong waterfall and Mae Kachan hot spring. Continue on true bikers paradise roads until reach to Phayao, visit Phayao Lake (Kwan Phayao) one of the largest lake in Northern Thailand. Lunch serve at local restaurant in front of the lake. Ride along the impressive mountainous road highway No. 1148 to Nan, ranked top 10 for best riding fun all over the world. 120 kilometres of up and down curves through the impressive mountains and pure riding pleasure overload. Visit Wat Phra That Khao Noi (Nan Top Hill Scenic Temple) before relaxing in your lovely accommodation and jump in the swimming pool.
Day 2. Nan – Sukhothai (214miles or 345 kms.)

After breakfast, we leave Nan riding through winding mountainous roads. We then take the motorbikes on a wooden ferry across the Sirikit Dam reservoir. Sirikit Dam is the largest earth dam in Thailand. It´s used for irrigation, fisheries, flood control and as well as hydro-electric power generation. Lunch is served at Sirikit Dam. Then we continue on the highway passing through rice fields until we reach Sukhothai. Visit the Ancient Sukhothai Historical Park, designated world heritage site number 574 on 12 December 1991 by UNESCO and enjoy the amazing sunset in the old ruins. A magical and memorable scene. Later you arrive at the guest house, where you enjoy the charming accommodation.
Day 3. Sukhothai – Chiang Mai (177miles or 286 kms.)

After breakfast, we leave Sukhothai cruising along rice fields to Thoen. Then riding through winding mountainous roads to Lampang. Lunch is served at a local restaurant. Visit the Thai elephant conservation center and world´s first elephant hospital. Continue riding, passing through national parks and farming areas. Visit local market, stopping for refreshment, before heading back to Chiang Mai.

title.en: 4-Day Yoga Retreat in Chiang Mai

overview: Put down your backpack and recharge your batteries in Chiang Mai. Thailand's northern capital is the perfect place for a yoga escape with its blissfully calm and very laid-back ambience. Treat yourself with daily morning and evening yoga classes, taking place in a charming wooden house tugged away in a small quiet alley. You will have free time between classes to explore the city or to hang out with a good book and a cup of coffee at one of Chiang Mai’s many cafes. You will have a bicycle available during your stay, and your base will be at ECO Resort. A treat in itself with its calm garden setting and Olympic size swimming pool. So you just have to focus on your self – your own hideaway and treat in Northern Thailand.
highlights: Multi-Day Trip
Cycle the city streets to absorb the local atmosphere
Breakfast included
expect: Day 1

Upon arrival in Chiang Mai airport/bus/train station, you will be picked up and transferred to ECO Resort Chiang Mai. When you arrive your room might not be ready until 2pm. If so, you can store your luggage and use the swimming pool to relax and splash around. The rest of the day is free for you to do as you please.

For your convenience, you will have a bicycle available during your stay, to transport you to and from your yoga classes. The bike is not fancy, but it is your companion and key to freedom in easy-going Chiang Mai. Simply go the Travel Center to receive your bicycle key and pay a deposit of 1000THB (will be paid back when you deliver back the bike and key). / Overnight
Day 2 (B)

Wake up early for a very light breakfast (serving starts at 6:30am) before doing a gentle yoga class at 10am – 11:30am. We recommend eating no more than 2 hours before class and remember to drink plenty of water beforehand.

Ride your bicycle to the neat little yoga house tugged away in a small sub-soi. It is a slow 20 minutes bike ride and we will give you the necessary directions beforehand. After yoga catch a well-deserved lunch (own expense) and have free time to explore the city and its many charming cafes. Be back in the little yoga house for your evening class, which takes place 6pm – 7:30pm. The night will now have taken over and your first day of doing yoga has come to an end. / Overnight
Day 3 (B)
This is your second day of yoga and you may follow your routine from yesterday. Your morning yoga class is 10am – 11:30am and your evening yoga class takes place 6pm – 7:30pm.
In between and after, you have time available to explore the city. How about a bike ride to hip Nimmanhaemin where the coffee bars are plentiful? / Overnight
Day 4 (B)

Your last day of yoga has come already. Have breakfast in the early morning and check-out from your room before you head to your morning yoga class 10am – 11:30am. You can leave your luggage at ECO Resort and you will need to return to here with the bicycle and key to get your deposit back.
After this your tour is complete. If you need help deciding what to do from here visit the travel center.

Bicycle rental for 4 days (Bicycle deposit of 1000 THB (will be paid back when you deliver back the bike and key).

title.en: 5-Day Myanmar Trekking Tour from Chiang Mai

overview: Go from Chiang mai, across the border into Myanmar. In Myanmar's Shan State you will find an area called Kengtung known for its cultural diversity and colorful hill tribes. Go beyond the beaten track, out in the outskirts, explore the mountains, the villages and the local life with colorful friendly Akha ladies, Lahu men in traditional tribal costume and smiling curious Lishaw children.
highlights: Multi-Day Trip
Small-group tour
Breakfast included
expect: Day 1

Flow overland, cross the border and experience a remote corner of Myanmar’s Shan state. Leave ECO Resort Chiang Mai behind at 7am in the morning and watch the landscape change as you aim for the mountains in the North and the Mae Sai border. The drive is around 4-5 hours depending on traffic.

On arrival in Mae Sai, you will cross the border around 12:30pm-1pm and on the other side, in Tachileik, you will meet your guide. Go by shared taxi through gorgeous scenery, at a fine road to Kengtung. It’s about a 3-hours ride and upon arrival in Kengtung Town you will have the rest of the day to explore the small city. / Overnight
Day 2 (B, L)

Explore the outskirts of Kengtung and meet the local hill tribes. Several hill tribes inhabit the mountains surrounding Kengtung Town; the Eng, Lahu, Lishaw and Akha tribes. Together with your guide and a pickup truck you will visit 3 different hill tribe villages. Take in the serene mountainous surroundings and meet the local villagers at eye level.
Expect to be walking 30min to 1-hour to reach the villages in case the unpaved road is in a bad condition. Return to Kengtung at the end of the day. / Overnight
Day 3 (B, L)
Go to remote tribal villages while rewarded with serene mountain views and beautiful scenery.

Set out in a different direction to local tribal villages, where only few foreigners go. Expect to walk a bit more today and be rewarded by beautiful scenery and authentic hill tribe villages. Return to Kengtung at the end of the day.
Day 4 (B)

Free day to explore the town and local life. The day is free for you to do as you please. Start early in the morning and visit the busy market. Walk the town roads and backstreets, pass the magical temples, see the British colonial architecture and embrace life in this remote corner of Myanmar.
Day 5 (B)

Transfer to the bus station and start your return journey towards the border to Thailand. From Tachileik your onward destination is as per your own arrangement. Whatever your choice, we will be happy to help you with a piece of advice or a bit if inspiration.

title.en: 3-Day Thai Elephant Care Camp Experience from Chiang Mai

overview: Immerse yourself in the daily life of an elephant camp with a three- day experience from Chiang Mai. Learn to prepare specialized foods for the elephants, and work closely with the gentle creatures as you accompany them to their daily mud spa and waterfall bath. See the elephants’ medical care then help walk elderly elephants for their daily exercise. On your third day, visit a moving elephant cemetery and enjoy a final mud spa and bathing session before returning to Chiang Mai.
highlights: 3-day elephant camp experience from Chiang Mai
Feed, bathe and care for elephants
Interact with elephants daily
Enjoy the serenity of a rural setting
Free hotel pickup and drop-off included
Family friendly
expect: You will arrive at the Thai Elephant Care Center 45-minutes later and be welcomed by the Instructor Team. The team will provide you with an introduction on the Thai Elephant Care Center and the 3-day program you will participate in. After this, you will be taken to the Homestay to check in for the next couple of nights.

Itinerary Day 1 Your day will begin with a hotel pickup from your hotel in Chiang Mai at approximately 9am. From here, you will be taken to the Thai Elephant Care Center! You will arrive at the Thai Elephant Care Center 45-minutes later and be welcomed by the Instructor Team. The team will provide you with an introduction on the Thai Elephant Care Center and the 3-day program you will participate in. After this, you will be taken to the Homestay to check in for the next couple of nights.

You will be provided with a special outfit to wear over the next few days. After you have your outfit on you will meet with the instructors once more for a more detailed outline on what to expect. After this the real fun begins!
After lunch, you will take the elephants to the waterfall for a bath. You can even jump in with them!

Learn how elephants are treated with basic health care treatments and see how they relax after a busy morning. Feed the elephants before taking them to the jungle for the night. Return to camp to help the caretakers clean the elephant’s residences. Enjoy dinner before retiring to sleep.

Day 2 Be sure to wear your special outfit again before enjoying breakfast. Check and prepare the elephants residences before bringing the elephants back to camp. Feed the elephants their breakfast so they are ready for the day ahead. Learn how to prepare snacks made from herbs to feed the elephants. After this, take them out for another mud spa! After the elephants have had their treatment, it is time for you to enjoy some lunch.

You will get to bathe with the elephants once more before taking them out for some walking exercises. These exercises help keep them flexible in their old age. Participate in one more special, mystery activity before returning the elephants to the jungle. For dinner, you have the choice to eat a prepared meal at the camp, or participate in a Thai cooking class!
Day 3 Rise early and stroll over to a local market for breakfast. Enjoy the local atmosphere and delicious food!

Upon returning to the camp, you will help in checking and preparing the elephants residences. You will then be trusted to prepare the elephants food yourself! You will get an inside look into what happens when an elephants passes away. You will take a visit to the Memorial Elephant Cemetery.
Enjoy once last chance to bathe with the elephants and give them a mud spa before preparing yourself for the farewell. Delight in a farewell party with the elderly elephants!

title.en: 2-Day Thai Elephant Care Center Experience from Chiang Mai

overview: Have you always been intrigued by elephants and want to spend more than a few hours with them? Then you should definitely come and visit Thai Elephant Care Center at Mae Sa. Here you can feed them, pamper them and give them a nice mud bath, first learn how to cook and later getting the responsibility on your own as well seeing and get to know a lot of other fun facts over a spectacular 2-day trip!
highlights: Multi-Day Trip
Once-in-a-Lifetime Experience
Close encounter with wildlife
expect: Day 1

Your day will begin with a pickup from your hotel in Chiang Mai at 9am. Relax and enjoy the ride for approximately 45-minutes until you reach the Thai Elephant Care Center. Upon arrival, you will be welcomed by the Instructor Team. They will give an introduction on the Thai Elephant Care Center and the details of your 2-day program. Once you are aware of the excitement awaiting you, you will proceed to the Elephant Camp’s Homestay to check-in for the night. You will be provided with a special outfit to wear. At approximately 10:30am, your program will begin. You will start the day by visiting the elderly elephants. After this, you will learn how to prepare appropriate food, such as natural medicine and herb balls. As you do this, you will learn how they benefit the elephants. At noon, take the elephants out for a mud spa. Have fun with this for about an hour, then return to the camp where lunch will be served. After lunch you’ll be given the opportunity to take the elephants to the waterfall for cleaning. You will even be able to jump in and take a bath with the elephant, if you want!

After this, you will learn how the elephants are treated with basic health care treatments and then you will get a chance to feed the elephants, they particularly enjoy ground grass! See how the elephants relax after a busy day before taking them to the jungle for the night. You will help the caretakers clean the residences of the elephants before retiring for a well- deserved dinner. After this, enjoy a nice sleep at the Thai Elephant Care Center Homestay.
Day 2
Start the day early, at approximately 7am, and enjoy breakfast at the camp. Be sure to put your special outfit on again before departing to check, prepare, and clean the elephant residences.

You will enter the jungle once more and lead the elephants back to camp. Once they are back safely, you will be able to feed them their breakfast, to prepare them for the fun day ahead. Learn how to prepare special treats for the elephants, made from herbs. Once the elephants are well-fed and ready for the day, it’s time for another spa treatment. After the elephants have received their treatment, it will be time for you to enjoy lunch back at the camp. After lunch, you will be given one more chance to bathe with the elephants. Soak up the feeling of this special experience!

After this you will assist in giving basic health treatment, as well as walking exercises with the elephants to help keep them flexible. You will then participate in a special mystery activity that will surely leave you with great stories to tell you friends and family back home! Enjoy one last feeding session with the elephants, feeding them snacks and food, before enjoying a farewell party!
You will then depart back for your Chiang Mai hotel, taking your special, everlasting memories of this unique 2-day elephant experience with you.

title.en: 2-Day Ethical Choice Tour to the Elephant Nature Park

overview: Elephant Nature Park is a unique project set in Chiang Mai, Northern Thailand. This overnight stay allows you to get close and truly understand these wonderful animals.

Established in the 1990s their aim has always been to provide a sanctuary and rescue center for elephants. The park is located about 60km from the city center of Chiang Mai, and has become home for dozens of previously distressed elephants from all over Thailand. The area offers a timeless glimpse of rural life as it it is set in a natural valley, bordered by a river and surrounded by rested mountains.
highlights: Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Close encounter with wildlife
Family friendly
Dinner included
Breakfast included
Multi-Day Trip
expect: On arrival an introductory orientation video and talk where you can learn all about our herd and the park is followed by a healthy lunch of fresh local produce then watch the elephants bathe in the river that borders our park. Discover how to communicate with them and learn with our trained staff. Observe how they play and interact in each of their social groups. Full dinner is provided at the park before settling into the parks huts for your overnight stay. After breakfast you can go on an elephant walk to see the elephants roaming in the open pasture. Upon returning to the Park with the elephants you get to feed and bathe the herd. You will soon begin to identify different elephants by their shape, markings and attitude. Observe and enjoy the communications and interactions between these highly intelligent and loving elephants.

Elephant Nature Park´s Mae Taeng Valley location is naturally stunning. Combined with the company of a herd of rescued elephants you will have the chance to take numerous pictures and keep lifelong memories.

Food - Dinner and lunches at the park are casual affairs, the focus being on high quality locally grown produce prepared in Western and Eastern styles. The range on offer will suit all diets from vegetarian to Halal.

Accommodation - overnight visitors stay in traditional rustic bamboo fan cooled huts, in keeping with our natural surrounds. Mosquito nets are provided so you may sleep with your windows open; if you listen to the night you may hear the elephants whisper, rumble, snore and even the occasional trumpet. You may watch the elephants from your room or the dedicated observation platform.
Overnight stays are all about spending time with the herd and do not adhere to a strict schedule; the best way to make the most of your visit is to relax, watch and learn from the elephants.
included: Admission fees, Park guides, Overnight Accommodation

title.en: 2-Day Chiang Dao Valley Family Trek from Chiang Mai

overview: From Chiang Mai, experience this easy trekking trip, discovering small hill tribe villages and authentic rural life. Join us on this rich cultural experience and active two days trip in the heart of the Chiang Dao valley, with stunning views of Thailand’s third highest peak.

expect: Day 1:

Trek the Chiangdao Valley and Overnight at Lodge (L, D) At 8:30am your guide will meet you at your hotel in Chiang Mai. Our first destination is a local market. Continue to a small Lahu village up the mountain, to our trek starting point. The hike is mostly downhill and not strenuous. You will see many jungle trees, and a bamboo forest. Walk along a small refreshing stream. We will meet with our vehicle and transfer by car (30min) to the Chiangdao valley. Transfer to the Padeng Lodge for an overnight stay. Dinner at the Lodge. This evening, for families with children, your guide will teach them how to use bamboo to make various useful objects such as cups, whistles, forks and sticks. A fun time for youngsters.

Trek and Buddhist Cave Exploration (B, L) After a filling breakfast, a short drive will bring us to another village, inhabited by Lisu and Akkha people. From there we will follow a trekking trail leading to a Palong hill tribe village. Eventually we will stop by the local school, and walk back to the Lodge. This hike takes about two hours, but we can propose a longer trek option, depending on the season and participants abilities.

Lunch at the Lodge. After lunch, we drive to the Chiangdao Caves for a deep exploration. The caves are part of a Buddhist Sanctuary and various chambers can be discovered, with the help of local guides equipped with gas lamps. Various chambers are scattered with interesting stalagmites and stalactites of different shapes, sometimes they remind us animals or objects. Around the caves, local shops display and sell various medicinal plants and herbs. Drive back to Chiang Mai and drop-off at your hotel in town or at Chiang Mai airport. title.en: 3-Night Chiang Mai Tour: Mountain Bike, Wat Doi Suthep and Whitewater Rafting

overview: Set out on a series of thrilling adventures from the comfort of Chiang Mai on this multi-day tour. Each morning you’ll board a minibus out of the city and into northern Thailand for a completely new activity. Climb an ancient staircase to a revered Thai temple one day, mountain bike along vast fields and past rural villages the next. You’ll even get to tackle some of Asia’s best white-water rafting on the Mae Taeng River. Your group is limited to 12 people for a more personalized experience.
highlights: 3-night Chiang Mai adventure tour with an expert guide
Bicycle through the countryside along the Ping River and explore rural Thai life
Climb the steps to the summit of Doi Suthep Temple and explore the enchanting ruins of Wiang Kum Kam
Enjoy a mountain bike ride over hilly terrain
Navigate the whitewater rapids on a rafting trip down the Mae Taeng River
Small-group tour limited to 12 ensures a more personalized experience
expect: Discover the best that Thailand’s northern region has to offer — a perfect blend of energetic activities and enchanting sights that will leave you breathless. This 3-night tour includes a rafting excursion, two bicycle rides, a hike and a climb up an ancient staircase; the level of physical activity required on this adventure tour is not for the faint of heart! Your fun guide will expertly accompany you on all the exciting activities to ensure a seamless and memorable adventure. At times when there are no scheduled activities, spend time with your guide and fellow travelers or explore at your leisure.

Enjoy three nights accommodation in 2-star hotels in Chiang Mai, with complimentary airport pickup. If you arrive early or stay longer, you’ll have plenty of free time to explore Thailand's northern capital – a captivating blend of ancient temples and modern markets. Itinerary Day 1 Chiang Mai After airport pickup, check in at your hotel and enjoy a free day at leisure , laze by the pool, relax with a Thai massage or head out to explore charming Chiang Mai, Thailand’s second largest city. Venture around the northern capital on foot or on a bicycle and discover the fascinating temples, friendly people and vibrant markets, including street food at the Night Bazaar . / Overnight
Day 2:

Chiang Mai (B) After breakfast, your guide will take your small group on a tour of the temple complex of Wat Phrathat Doi Suthep, one of Thailand's most beautiful temples. Enjoy the 45-minute drive along a scenic and winding mountain road to the temple. Then, ascend the 300 steps of its stairway guarded by nagas (mythological serpents) and be rewarded at the top with spectacular panoramic views of the city Return to your hotel in the late morning and gather with your small group again after lunch (own expense) for a safety briefing and bicycle fitting, including a helmet. Once you feel comfortable with the 24 gears and front suspension on your adapted mountain bike, follow your guide to the outskirts of Chiang Mai. Your 4.5-hour ride with frequent stops covers 15 to 18 miles (25 to 30 km) of flat ground, some of it unpaved.

Journey south through pleasant green fields, following the Ping River downstream. Cycle over small country roads, riding past fruit orchards, farms and the occasional colorful village as you encounter the rural Thai way of life. Visit a former leper colony, now a rehabilitation center, and learn about the activities of the missionaries in days gone by. Explore the spectacular temple ruins of Wiang Kum Kam, the former capital of Lanna, on the way back to Chiang Mai. / Overnight
Day 3

Chiang Mai (B, L) Get ready for an action-packed day when your guide picks you up from your hotel after breakfast. Hop on a mountain bike and cycle on a dirt road, following the river for an approximate 6-mile (10-km) ride through uphill and downhill terrain. When you arrive at an upstream picnic spot, pause for a rest and enjoy a picnic lunch. In the afternoon, get ready for a thrilling whitewater rafting trip down the Mae Taeng River and its 14 gorges. The staff will outfit you with helmet and lifejacket, and prepare your small group with a briefing on river safety. Once you’re acquainted with the paddling commands, the correct way to sit in the raft and any necessary precautions, jump on and enjoy the approximate 2-hour trip.

Praised as some of the best whitewater rafting in Asia, the difficulty level on the 6-mile (10- km) stretch of the Mae Taeng River ranges from grade 3 to 5. Complete your rafting adventure at a downstream camp, where you can rest and change into dry clothes. Enjoy some hot and cold drinks or fresh fruit before the return transfer to your hotel in Chiang Mai. / Overnight
Day 4:

Chiang Mai (B) With no activities planned for the day, you are free to depart at any time. Although checkout time is at noon, you can arrange luggage storage at the hotel if you plan to depart later. Enjoy a complimentary airport departure transfer or stay on in Chiang Mai, where you can join a cooking class, shop at bustling markets or meander through more than 300 temples in the cosmopolitan city.

title.en: 4-Night Hill Tribe Village Tour with Thai Jungle Trek from Chiang Mai

overview: Explore the vast jungles and hill tribe villages of northern Thailand on a 4-night adventure trek. An experience guide leads you and your tour group of 12 or less on a multi-day hike into the local wilderness from Chiang Mai, where you’ll encounter several remote tribes, learn about their culture and customs and even assist them preparing meals. Your overnights will be split between the villages’ bamboo huts and 2-star lodging in Chiang Mai, which you’ll also have ample opportunity to enjoy either solo or along with your knowledgable guide.
highlights: 4-night northern Thailand tour including two-day trek round-trip from Chiang Mai
Lace up your hiking boots and venture deep into the Thai jungle
Interact with local hill tribes and stay overnight in their villages
Learn about unique customs as you help prepare home-cooked meals
Enjoy leisurely time in Chiang Mai with optional activities
Small-group tour limited to 12 ensures a more personalized experience
expect: Immerse yourself in this remote region of northern Thailand for an unforgettable experience! Your adventure-packed tour includes two days of trekking through mountainous jungle terrain – a moderate level of difficulty. Since you will carry your own backpack and personal supplies, you will need a decent level of fitness to participate. This cultural experience includes two nights accommodation in bamboo huts in a hill tribe village, where living conditions are basic. With two nights accommodation at 2-star hotels in Chiang Mai, you’ll also have plenty of opportunities to explore the exciting northern capital in your spare time.
Itinerary
Day 1

Chiang Mai Arrive at your hotel in Chiang Mai any time before your welcome meeting at 6.30pm. If you arrive early, embark on a discovery of northern Thailand’s vibrant capital, including hundreds of stunning temples, a picturesque riverfront, great shopping and an abundance of local eateries serving delectable Thai cuisine. After your welcome meeting, you can join your guide on a leisure walk through the old city or rent a bicycle to explore Chiang Mai on your own (all activities at own expense). / Overnight
Day 2-3

Chiang Mai – Hill Tribe Trekking (1B, 2L, 2D) Your guide will collect your small group from your hotel around 8:45am. Depart from Chiang Mai by songthaew (open pickup truck) as you anticipate the trekking adventure ahead! On your three-hour (approximate) drive heading north, you will be immersed in the locals’ way of travel through city and countryside as you are joined by various local characters. After lunch, hoist on your backpack and head into the hills on a two-day trek through tropical jungle, hiking for about four to five hours each day at a moderate but comfortable pace. Your guide will determine the exact routes and itinerary, which may change from time to time according to weather and local conditions.

Walk through green fields and stop at remote waterfalls along winding forest tracks. Pass through a variety of hill tribe villages, meeting people with their own distinct languages, clothing styles, customs and belief systems. You’ll stay in a different hill tribe village each night to interact with the locals and observe authentic village life. Feel free to explore each village, help prepare the evening meals and communicate with your hill tribe hosts (with help from your guide). During your visits, meet elephants rescued from the wild and learn about the important work mahouts (elephant trainer) do to care for and protect these gentle beasts. Join the locals for a freshly prepared dinner and then sleep in a traditional (and basic) bamboo mountain hut, awakening to the sounds of village life in the jungle as you relish your once-in-a-lifetime experience!

Meals during the daytime will be prepared by your guide during your jungle adventure. Midday through your trekking, a stop will be made, allowing for relaxation and a simple lunch of rice and noodles with your fellow travelers. / Overnight
Day 4

Hill Tribe Trekking – Chiang Mai (B) Your hill tribe adventure comes to a close as you complete your trek through the jungle terrain of northern Thailand. Your guide will return your small group by songthaew to Chiang Mai in the afternoon. Enjoy your evening at leisure, perhaps with a trip to the Night Bazaar or a traditional Thai massage to soothe those sore muscles
Day 5

Chiang Mai Without any planned activities for the day, you are free to leave at any time. Say goodbye to your fellow travelers or choose to stay in Chiang Mai for a few extra days. Explore ancient temples – ride to the gorgeous hilltop temple of Wat Phrathat Doi Sutep for stunning views of the city – or sign up for a Thai cooking class and savor the regional Thai cuisine.

title.en: 3-Day Chiang Mai and Golden Triangle Tour Including Doi Mae Salong

overview: Experience Thailand’s famous Golden Triangle on a 3-day tour cultural tour from Chiang Mai. Visit the border where Thailand meets with Laos and Myanmar (Burma), tour the Hall of Opium museum and marvel at the natural limestone formations within the Chiang Dao Caves. You’ll sail upon the Khong River in a longtail boat and soak in the waters of Maoe Ka Chan hot springs. This guided small-group tour also includes a visit to Doi Mae Salong, a hillside village steeped in Chinese history. Includes round-trip transport from Chiang Mai.
highlights: 3-day tour of northern Thailand and Golden Triangle, round-trip from Chiang Mai
Catch a glimpse of the borders Thailand, Laos and Myanmar (Burma) from the Golden
Triangle and enjoy an opportunity to step foot in all three
Explore hilltribe villages and sip tea at a Chinese teahouse in Doi Mae Salong
Wander through the caves of Chiang Dao National Park and head down the Khong
River on a long-tail boat
Learn about the opium trade at the Hall of Opium museum exhibit
Soak in the hot springs of Mae Ka Chan
Small-group tour limited to 12 people ensures a personalized experience
expect: Your three-day journey to the far reaches of northern Thailand takes you to its best attractions. At the Golden Triangle, you’ll catch a glimpse of three borders – Thailand, Laos and Myanmar (Burma) – with a chance to set foot in each! Enjoy the scenic beauty, natural splendor and fascinating cultures of this less-traveled region. This exciting small-group tour includes 4-star hotel accommodation in Doi Mae Salong and Chiang Rai with five meals plus round-trip transport from your Chiang Mai hotel by minibus./ Overnight Itinerary Day 1:
Chiang Mai – Doi Mae Salong (L)

Meet your friendly local guide and small group upon pickup from your Chiang Mai hotel in the morning, and set off by air-conditioned minibus toward the charming town of Doi Mae Salong in northern Thailand.

After lunch with your small group, head to Chiang Dao National Park for a guided exploration of the Chiang Dao Caves – a series of 100 interconnected limestone caverns that span seven miles (12 km) into Doi Chiang Dao mountain, five of which are open to the public.

Follow your guide up the steps toward the entrance before descending into the first two caves, which are lit with electric lights; your guide will lead the way by lantern as you walk – and crawl – into the last three. Admire the many Buddhist statues and shrines, as well as the crystal-like stalactites and stalagmites underground.

Afterward, drive to Doi Mae Salong, a remote village located in a northern Thai region famous for its Chinese tea traders. Relax with a cup of tea in a traditional Chinese teahouse as you take in the views of the nearby mountains. In the late afternoon, you’ll have free time to explore – stroll through the markets to find fresh produce and crafts made by local hill tribes, or simply settle in at another teahouse and sip more tea as you enjoy the vista.
Day 2:

Doi Mae Salong / Chiang Rai (B, L) After breakfast, your guide will take your small group to the region known as the Golden Triangle – where the borders of Thailand, Myanmar and Laos meet – on the way to your destination of Chiang Rai.

First, stop in Mae Sai near the Thailand-Myanmar border. You’ll spend a bit of time in Thailand’s northernmost town, a well-known trading post where you can explore the local market along the main street. Among the jade and other gems, search for Burmese lacquer ware and goods from nearby Laos. If time allows, you’ll have the opportunity to cross the border into Myanmar to browse a similar market on the other side. (A temporary visa will cost 500thb. Please note that you will only receive a 15-day entry visa when crossing back into Thailand.) Afterward, continue to the Golden Triangle and stand at the confluence of the Mekong and Ruak rivers while your guide points out the borders of each neighboring country. Then, delight over mouth-watering regional dishes as you enjoy lunch overlooking the mighty Mekong River and watch the scene unfold below.

Then, it’s time to dig beneath the surface of the scenic beauty and bold landscapes to uncover facts about the area’s checkered past. Visit the Hall of Opium, a modern museum with fascinating exhibits that detail the notorious history of this former opium-producing capital. Hear stories from your guide about the more recent cultivation of other crops by the hill tribes who used to grow the once-flourishing poppies.

In the afternoon, climb aboard a long-tail boat for a ride down the Khong River to the old city of Chiang Saen, the ancient capital of the Lanna Kingdom, now famous for the local rice whiskey sold from distilleries on the riverbanks. With no official border crossing between Thailand and Laos along this river, you may pull off to one side and have a chance to step foot into Laos When you reach Chiang Rai, a lovely city with a small-town ambiance, enjoy your evening at leisure – perhaps visiting downtown or the night market on your own.
Day 3:

Chiang Rai / Chiang Mai (B, L) Enjoy a delicious breakfast before driving to beautiful Wat Rong Khun (white temple) near Chiang Rai. Unlike most centuries-old Buddhist temples in Thailand, this temple’s construction began in 1997 and isn’t expected to be completed until 2070. As you tour the complex with your guide and small group, admire the buildings painted pure white, as well as the interior murals of Superman, Batman and Neo from the movie The Matrix – all designed by Thai artist Chalermchai Kositpipat. Next, head to the Mae Ka Chan hot springs, with a lunch stop along the way. Located at a rest stop between Chiang Rai and Chiang Mai, the three pools of these hot springs are a great place to ease sore muscles or relax. Enjoy a foot massage fish-spa style – while dozens of tiny fish nibble dead skin from your feet -- or purchase quail eggs to cook in the boiling waters as you soak!

title.en: 3-Day Chiang Dao Mountain Trek

overview: Doi Chiang Dao mountain range lies to the North of Chiang Mai. The area is home to many ethnic hill-tribe villages, and down to the west of the mountain flows the Mae Tang river through scenic forest and valley. This adventurous and strenuous mountain will take participants off the beaten track across the mountain range, down to the Maetang River valley on trails regularly used by villagers. Trekkers will enjoy scenic views from the mountain as a significant part of the hike is on the mountain ridges.
highlights: All-inclusive tour
Multi-Day Trip
Small-group tour
Hotel pickup included
All necessary equipment included
Get inside tips from a local
expect: Day 1:

Mountain trek and overnight at homestay (L, D) Pickup (8:30am) from your accommodation in Chiang Mai before driving north to escape the city and experience the beautiful Chiang Dao area. Along the way we will stop at a local market where your local guide can introduce the ingredients they will use for cooking delicious Thai meals over the next few days. Our next destination is a peaceful valley further north and the start of the trek. After a short briefing, we’ll set off on an hour’s trek and you will have your first close encounter with Northern Thailand’s natural environment. Next we make a lunch stop at a peaceful fruit orchard before continuing our hike, gaining altitude and a noticeable change of flora. We will cross a large tea plantation under the shade of tall mature trees and eventually arrive at a local homestay to spend the night. Your guides will cook a tasty Thai dinner for tonight, then you have the evening to relax and soak up your new surroundings. Today’s hike is approximately 4 to 5 hours, mostly ascending.
Day 2:

The longest trekking day (B, L, D) Wake up to the mountain melodies and enjoy breakfast with locally grown tea or coffee from the surrounding plantation. Today you are in for a challenging day through a variety of jungle and criss-crossing trails. We will follow mountain ridges under the jungle canopy, with occasional clearings offering breathtaking panoramic views of the lower valley. Around noon, refuel with a packed lunch in a nice spot along the trail. The afternoon trek will bring more bamboo forest, shade under tall jungle trees and a refreshing river crossing. The last climb for the day will take us to our overnight destination, a tiny Lahu village where you can interact with local people and learn a bit about their way of life. Once again, your guide will prepare Thai cuisine for your dinner while you put your feet up after a long day! Tonight you will be staying in basic accommodation (dormitory house) and be able to get a feel for village life. Today’s hike is approximately 5 to 6 hours, mountain trails with mix of ascents and descents.
Day 3:

Morning trek, lunch by the river and drive back to Chiang Mai (B, L) Enjoy breakfast on the mountain before we start our final leg of the trek. Today is a three- hour descent to the Maetang River valley below where you will notice a change in scenery. Once you arrive at our riverside camp, you can enjoy a succulent Thai lunch in a tranquil setting. Relax at the camp, or take an optional activity before saying goodbye to the Northern jungle and driving back to Chiang Mai where we drop you off at your city accommodation. Today’s hike is approximately 3 hours, mostly downhill.

title.en: 4-Day Chiang Mai to Chiang Rai Cycling Adventure

overview: Travel elephant trails and back roads on a 4-day cycling tour from Chiang Mai to Chiang Rai across the spectacular mountains of Chiang Dao. Enjoy the support of an air-conditioned minivan as you pedal 80- miles (130-kilometers) to riverside villages and isolated waterfalls, duck into hollow limestone caves and ride paths built by the region’s hill tribes. Visit a temple retreat and riverside resort, then catch a ride on a longtail boat before cruising into Ban Ruam Mitr and Chiang Rai.

Family friendly

expect: Explore the northern provinces of Thailand on this exciting cycling tour, and discover the stunning countryside and unspoilt nature of Chiang Mai and Chiang Rai. We ride back country dirt roads and elephant trails through the spectacular limestone mountains of Chiang Dao and to the scenic village of Mae Salak, straddling the Mae Kok River. After a visit to the village we head over to Bua Thong waterfall for a refreshing swim before riding to our charming Thai-style lodges.

We embark on a cave exploration of Chiang Dao caves on our second day, and ride on a mixture of dirt paths cut by local hill tribes. The peaceful trails offer fantastic scenery of the ancient Lanna kingdom as well as a chance to experience the Thai way of life as we make our way through small villages and are greeted by friendly locals. On day 3 after breakfast we cycle to Tub Tao Caves and a temple retreat. We then continue on back roads through quaint villages before lunching in Fang. An easy afternoon ride takes us to the sleepy town of Mae Salak and our riverside resort.

The fourth and last day we ride an off road trail to Lakhu village where we hop on a long-tail boat down the river before cycling off road to Ban Ruamitr and later Chiang Rai. We ride a total of 80mi (130km) over the course of four days, each day with none of the distances being overly long.

This fairly gentle cycling tour is suitable for riders with some off-road biking experience, but can be tackled by anyone with even a moderate amount of fitness. An air-conditioned minivan travels behind the group to support us and participants can cycle as much or as little as they like and still enjoy the same views as the rest of the group.This 4- Day/3-Night tour includes breakfast-3, lunch-3 and dinner-3

title.en: Chiang Mai Adventure: Zipline, Whitewater Rafting, and Long-Neck Hill Tribe

overview: Experience the best of rural Chiang Mai on a full-day excursion that combines several activities. Raft the whitewater rapids of the Mae Taeng River, float on a bamboo raft, zipline through the jungle, and learn about northern Thailand’s hill tribes on a visit to a local village. Top off the trip with a stop at the Elephant Poo Poo Paper Park, an eco-friendly outdoor museum. A buffet lunch is also included.

expect: After pickup from your hotel, head to your whitewater rafting adventure on the Mae Taeng River. After you receive safety gear and a briefing from your river guides, prepare to get wet on an approximate 40-minute ride. Then, relax aboard a traditional bamboo raft as you float down a calm stretch of the river.

After changing into dry clothes, you’re driven to the Mae Sa Valley for your zipline tour through the forest canopy. Fuel up with Thai dishes at a lunch buffet before you’re fitted with a safety harness and given an orientation. Follow your guide to the first platform where you’re attached to a safety line before you take off through the treetops. The 16-zipline course includes a nature walk between sections of the park.

Continue on to a local village, where your guide describes some of northern Thailand’s hill tribe cultures, including the Long-neck Karen, Lahu, Hmong and Lisu peoples. Finish up the day at the Elephant Poo Poo Paper Park, an outdoor museum that explains the process of converting elephant poop fibers to paper products. Learn more about the eco- friendly space from your guide, as well as the plight of the Asian elephant. Afterward, you’ll return to Chiang Mai with drop-off at your hotel.

Begin the day with a hotel pick up and upon arrival at your base, you will have your safety briefing, bike and safety gear fit out. Then you begin the hike up to the old Hmong Hill Tribe Village at the summit of Doi Pui National Park.

The trek takes you through stunning highland jungle, filled with the huge primary Mai Yai tree, indigenous to this area. After 3 hours steady walking, you reach your destination to find your bikes and gear are already waiting for you at the village. After a well-earned lunch break, you begin your descent through the National Park on your mountain bike, toward Lake Huay Tung Tao approximately 2 hour ride away. In contrast to the hike up, gravity rewards you now with a cool ride downhill with views of the beautiful Mae Ping Valley.

Awaiting you lakeside, is a proper late lunch with cool drinks. Take a dip before it’s time to jump back in the truck and you head out of the National Park. 3.30pm: You will be delivered back to your hotel around 3.30pm.

expect: We have the privilege of offering this exclusive tour that takes you through Doi Suthep – Pui National Park. This is a tour not available to those who wish to do things on their own as you must be accompanied by an experienced Doi Suthep Park Ranger as well as one of our English speaking tour guides. Exploring this jungle on your own is not allowed. It was designed for those interested in exploring both the must see temple of Doi Suthep and for those who would like to enjoy a trek without having to ride an elephant, go bamboo water rafting, or be surrounded by other tourists. These characteristics are what make this trek extremely unique. It is not often you will get to experience nature in a foreign land without the burden of begin surrounded by others all while having the luxury of a well trained and experienced Park Ranger to entertain any of your curiosities. Chances are you and your group will be the only ones on the trail. Conveniently located only 10 minutes outside the city this tour offers quick access to the beautiful forests of Chiang Mai. Your day will begin with one of our English speaking guides picking you up at your hotel or guest house for an 8am departure. You will be delivered to Mon Tha Than Waterfall where your trek will begin. Experience the grandeur and breathe taking views the trail offers as you walk among forests of bamboo, tall hardwoods, a variety of colorful flowers, and a diverse bird population. Make sure you bring a swim suit as there will be opportunities to cool off in the pools of several waterfalls you will see. The hike itself is a moderate one but proper footwear is highly recommended.

Your hike will end at Chiang Mai’s most sacred temple, Wat Phrathat Doi Suthep (1383 AD). The temple is located 16 Km’s from the city and 3,500 feet (1,066 meters) above sea level. Its large golden chedi attracts Buddhist pilgrims from all over the world throughout the year. While you are there enjoy the panoramic view of Chiang Mai City and the Ping Valley from this beautiful mountain temple. overview: Learn the basics with an expert guide, in a full-day introduction to rock climbing course in Chiang Mai. Start by practicing knot tying and belaying alongside your instructor, then try out climbing moves while secured by a sturdy top rope. expect: We have the perfect course for any beginner. This introduction to Rock Climbing course is designed to be a fun day out on the rocks where you will be introduced to the basics of rock climbing and rappelling (abseiling).

The morning part of the course will be spent introducing you to the basics of top-rope climbing. Top-rope climbing is the easiest, simplest, and safest way to climb. During this course we won’t just take you climbing; we will introduce you to the mechanics of the top- rope system, teach you how to belay, and help you develop the fundamentals you need to be a responsible and knowledgeable climber. You’ll get lots of time climbing, and our instructors will coach you on technique and help you have a successful and fun day on the rock! In the afternoon, you will get a chance to learn the basics of rappelling (abseiling). Applying your new skills of top-roping and belaying, you will help build a rappel and then step out over the edge and lower yourself to the ground. We finish the day with an exhilarating rappel into the mouth of a huge cave. Rappelling is a distinctly different activity from climbing, and this course will ensure that you are introduced to rappelling in a safe way so that you can learn best practices and good habits that will keep you safe on future rappels. overview: Challenge yourself to go deep in a full-day introduction to caving in Chiang Mai. Practice single rope techniques that will get you in — and out — of the imposing Anxiety State Crisis Cave, a massive cavern that stretches more than 230-feet (70-meters) underground. Lower past gleaming stalactites, crawl through narrow passageways and discover high-arched chambers lined with magnificent flow stones. In this course, you will be taught single rope techniques (SRT) in the anxiety state crisis cave at crazy horse buttress, a beautiful and massive cavern that lies in the heart of the mountain. This caving course is a true introduction, and will give you a survey of the basics of caving. In addition to the technical rope aspects, our instructors will introduce you to the local geology and and explain the formation of the fantastic flow stones, stalactites, and stalagmites that will surround you all day. The goal of this course is for rigorous, comprehensive, technical instruction to combine with a beautiful backdrop to teach SRT in a safe, awe-inspiring, and fun way.

Your day will begin with basic rigging techniques as you prepare your equipment and rig the ropes for your 40 meter descent into the earth. Enjoy a delicious thai lunch of sticky rice, northern thai sausage in the company of bats by the light of your headlamp. finish your day by ascending the rope back to the surface using SRT. expect: Chiang Mai Province is as rich in culture as it is in history. This excursions captures both making for an inspiring day set among a spectacular northern Thailand backdrop. Itinerary:

8.30 AM: Be collected from your hotel and embark on your scenic drive to the mountains in search of Suthep Hill. At 3000 feet (915m) sits the most venerated Temple in Chiang Mai, Wat Phra That Doi Suthep.

To reach the shrine inside the temple, you are free to climb the 306 steps or you can take the tram. Allow yourself time to take in the magnificent view before your drive downhill to visit the famous Wat Umong.

Wat Umong sits among 15 acres of woodlands and is dated circa 1297. Most famous for the network of underground tunnels with original wall paintings that are still visible today. Next stop will be Wat Chiang Man. An ancient temple built for King Mengrai in 1296, proudly holds the title as the first temple of Chiang Mai.

Your leisurely drive back to the city will deliver you to the Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Centre before a visit to the temple, Wat Phra Singh. Heading further south toward your final stop for the day, is Wat Chedi Luang, once home to the Emerald Buddha of Siam. 5PM: Your hotel transfer awaits.

expect: Following a hotel pickup from your hotel in Chiang Mai City at 8:30am by your English speaking guide, you will depart for Wat Chedi Luang.

This temple is the site of an enormous pagoda, originally 280 feet high, and which was partially destroyed by an earthquake in 1545. At one time, Wat Chedi Luang housed the revered Emerlad Buddha image now enshrined in Bangkok's Wat Phra Kaew. One of Wat Chedi Luang's most striking architectural features is a magnificent Naga staircase adorns the chapel's front porch.

Visit Wat Phra Singh which dates from 1345 and is one of the focal points of Songkran festivities. The temple compound includes the lovely Lai Kham chapel with its exquisite woodcarving and northern-style murals.
Enjoy Wat Suan Dok. This temple was built in the 14th century. Several of the white chedis contain ashes of Chaing Mai's former royal family.

Explore Wat Chiang Man. The oldest temple and was the residence of King Mengrai who founded Chaing Mai, and is noteworthy for a chedi supported by rows of elephantine buttresses, and a small ancient Buddha image, Phra Kaeo Khao. Next you head to Wat Jed Yod. This temple dates from 1458. The seven-spired square chedi was inspired by designs at Bodhagaya, the site of Buddha's Enlightenment in north India over 2,500 years ago.
At approximately 12:30pm, you'll arrive back at your hotel in Chiang Mai City where the tour will end.

title.en: Private Tour: Chiang Mai Arts and Cultural Center with Trishaw Ride and Wat Phra Singh

overview: Overview Important Info Experience northern Thailand’s cultural and royal history on a private half-day tour that includes round-trip air-conditioned transportation. You’ll visit the 14th-century Wat Phra Singh, which houses the important Buddha statue for which the temple is named, and arrive by private trishaw at the Chiang Mai Arts and Cultural Center. This museum features scale models highlighting the region’s past and future. A knowledgable guide will accompany you throughout, answering any questions you may have.
highlights: Private half-day monastery and museum tour in Chiang Mai
See the Lion Buddha and other significant features at Wat Phra Singh, Chiang Mai’s most revered Buddhist temple
Take a private trishaw ride with a friendly guide through city streets

City Arts and Cultural Center
Round-trip hotel transport by private minivan included
expect: Upon pickup by air-conditioned minivan, depart from your hotel in the morning or afternoon and head to Wat Phra Singh, aka the Temple of the Lion Buddha. During the roughly 30- minute drive, chat with your knowledgeable guide about the half-day itinerary ahead; the advantage of a private tour is that what you learn can be tailored to your interests. You have about an hour to explore 14th-century Wat Phra Singh, Chiang Mai’s most important Buddhist temple. Observe hundreds of monks and pilgrims gathering at this major monastery, which includes a fully restored assembly hall featuring Phra Chao Thong Tip, a large seated Buddha statue cast in gold and copper, and two medieval Buddha statues. Step into the Gilded Hall, renovated in the 19th century and considered a fine example of Lanna monastic architecture and religious art. (Lanna was a kingdom in northern Thailand from the 13th to the 18th centuries.) Your guide will point out the Phra Singh (Lion Buddha) and the mural- and stencil-covered walls containing illustrated stories. Admire the opulently carved gables and ornate red-and-gold designs, and ask any questions you’d like. After your temple tour, take a foot-pedal trishaw ride with your guide to the Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Center. During your 1.5-hour visit, stroll through the elegant building and pore over the exhibits at your own pace. The museum houses a permanent exhibit that takes visitors through the region’s culture in chronological order, from prehistory to the present, while another section houses short-term local exhibits of all types. At the modernized, multimedia cultural education center, guides dressed in traditional Thai clothing welcome you to watch an orientation video about Chiang Mai and northern Thailand. Then gain insight into religious traditions, agricultural history, hill-tribe peoples and other regional cultures, as well as the history of the royal dynasty via videos, scale models, life-size models, photos, wall murals and text.

Learn about development plans over the next two decades at the ‘Chiang Mai in the Future’ exhibit, where your guide can translate the Thai descriptions and point out parts of the city, before your tour ends with drop-off at your hotel.

overview: Visit the famous and most sacred temple in Chiang Mai – Doi Suthep Temple with our local guide. Enjoy the scenic panoramic view of Chiang Mai city on the mountain top. expect: Our driver and guide will pick you up from your hotel in Chiang Mai around 6:40am. We drive to the Cultural Road nearby Chiang Mai University to participate in Tak Bat ceremony. Tak Bat means giving alms to monks and you will see many locals and visitors here offering free food to monks. You need to remove your shoes before pouring the food in the monk bowl, and a short prayer shall be said. While offering food to monks, please note that female cannot touch monks as they are the symbol of purity.

Then, we continue to Chiang Mai most sacred temple, Wat Phrathat Doi Suthep (1383 AD). The temple is located 16 Km’s from the city and 3,500 feet (1,066 meters) above sea level. Its large golden chedi attracts Buddhist pilgrims from all over the world throughout the year. While you are there enjoy the panoramic view of Chiang Mai City and the Ping Valley from this beautiful mountain temple. You can take the cable car if not able to climb the 306 steps stairs up to the temple. Cable car tickets is included.

Next, we will drive down to the hill and visit local market – Warorot Market, and this is the place to go buy cheap and better quality goods in Chiang Mai. Enjoy it vibrant atmosphere and a place you can still see the old and real Chiang Mai. After the tour, our driver will transfer you back to your hotel around 11:30am.
