title.en: Private Half-Day Hmong Nong Hoi Village and Botanic Garden in Chiang Mai

overview: Thailand’s Royal Family has worked tirelessly for decades in supporting local communities to find sustainable means to make a living. Particularly around Chiang Mai, the Royal Projects at a Hmong settlement and a botanic garden are wonderful examples.
highlights: Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Choice of morning or afternoon departure
Get inside tips from a local
Private tour is operated with just your party and a guide/driver
Family friendly
Informative, friendly and professional guide
expect: North of Chiang Mai is where true natural beauty can be found. The mountainous regions are not only the home of various hill tribes but also to a large collection of plants, flowers and trees – some of them indigenous to the region. This half day venture away from Chiang Mai combines both how local hill tribes have shifted their source of income from their former opium trade to agricultural means and a collection of the finest flowers and plants at the Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden. The garden honors the work done by H.M. the Queen of Thailand in working sustainable and showing the beauty of Thai flora. We leave your hotel and head in northern direction to one of the leading Hmong Hilltribe villages, high in the mountains. Quite a number of these indigenous communities have their ancestral roots from southern China. It is not uncommon to see still Chinese traits and cultural elements being proudly displayed at Baan Hmong Nong Hoi Mai. This village is particularly special as it has been granted the title of Royal Projects; with the support of the Royal Family, these villagers have turned the slopes and fertile landscapes in a patchwork of agriculture and plantations.

We follow the road further to one of the other projects that has been named out of the deep respect the Thai people have for the Royal Family. The Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden (formerly known as the Mae Sa Botanic Garden) has been primarily set up as a conservation and research center for Thai flora. It is one of the first botanical gardens in the country that supports education for those keen in pursuing a career in not only the botanical side but also those interested in biodiversity and environmental conservation. Outside of these values, the garden is a fabulous collection of plants, flowers and trees that continue to attract visitors from around the country. Part of the project is the nearby orchid farm where various species of this delicate flower are on display.
This royal-tinted half day tour comes to an end and we will bring you back to your downtown Chiang Mai hotel.

expect: Drive through different parts of the city, passing through old city walls, gates and city moat, market, residential areas, foreign Consulates, Government buildings and Tapae Chiang Mai’s tourist attraction area. Then, drive up to Doi Suthep to visit Wat Prathat Doi Suthep (built in A.D. 1384), containing a holy relic of the Lord Buddha. Tucked away in the mountains at an elevation of 1,056 meters (3520 feet), the temple is reached using a Naga (7- headed dragon head serpent) railing rising along both sides. King Gue-Na built the monastery in 1383. The centre is a big Chedi, containing partial relics of Lord Buddha. The temple compound – reachable via a 300+ steps stairs offers an exhilarating view of Chiang Mai city and surrounding countryside.

After your visit, we head out to one of the main and most significant of Hmong hill tribe village on Doi Pui. You will encounter these ethnic Hill tribes, originating from the border with neighboring Myanmar who has called this region near Doi Suthep now their home. Here you see them in their colorful costumes, selling their wide range of antiques, curious decorative ornaments and fabrics.
Via the same way as we came back, via many turns and bends, we head back to the base of Doi Suthep and to your Chiang Mai hotel.

expect: Spend the day in the tropical hills surrounding Chiang Mai on this full-day sightseeing tour, and explore some of the present-day gems of the historic Kingdom of Lanna in northern Thailand.

Following a pick-up from your hotel in Chiang Mai, drive along a mountainous highway to the Lampang Elephant Conservation Center. Here, you will watch a thrilling elephant demonstration and visit a nearby elephant hospital to learn about the pioneering conservation work.

After a local lunch, take a sightseeing trip around the city of Lampang by horse carriage and discover one of the 3 most important towns of the Lanna kingdom. Known as “Mueang Rot Ma (“Horse Carriage City”) in Thai, Lampang is popular for its period buildings and atmosphere.

Continue to Wat Pra Kaew Don Tao (Monastery of the Emerald Buddha) and the ancient fortress of Wat Phra Dhat Lampang Luang to explore the 2 most important historical temples of the city. En route back to Chiang Mai, you will stop at Lampoon to see several ancient and revered temples, such as Wat Prathad Hariphunchai. The final leg of your trip includes a beautiful drive along the old Lampoon-Chiang Mai Road.

title.en: 1-Hour Tok Sen Massage in Chiang Mai

overview: Experience the healing power of a 60 minute traditional Tok Sen Massage at Chiang Mai's award winning day spa. Tok Sen is a Northern Thai (Lanna) style massage that originates in Chiang Mai. Its therapeutic emphasis is based on ancient Lanna wisdom. Tok Sen Massage aims to clear blocked energy using a special wooden instrument similar to a hammer and chisel that are tapped along your muscles to ease muscle tension using mechanical and sound vibration, working deeply through tissue and muscles. Tok Sen therapy relieves muscle aches and pains, relieves energy blockages, helps poor circulation and nerve problems.
Tok Sen is a medium - strong form of massage. It combines elements of Traditional Thai Massage with acupressure and stretching. If you prefer gentle and soft massages, this may not be for you.

title.en: 4-Day Yoga Retreat in Chiang Mai

overview: Put down your backpack and recharge your batteries in Chiang Mai. Thailand's northern capital is the perfect place for a yoga escape with its blissfully calm and very laid-back ambience. Treat yourself with daily morning and evening yoga classes, taking place in a charming wooden house tugged away in a small quiet alley. You will have free time between classes to explore the city or to hang out with a good book and a cup of coffee at one of Chiang Mai’s many cafes. You will have a bicycle available during your stay, and your base will be at ECO Resort. A treat in itself with its calm garden setting and Olympic size swimming pool. So you just have to focus on your self – your own hideaway and treat in Northern Thailand.
highlights: Multi-Day Trip
Cycle the city streets to absorb the local atmosphere
Breakfast included
expect: Day 1

Upon arrival in Chiang Mai airport/bus/train station, you will be picked up and transferred to ECO Resort Chiang Mai. When you arrive your room might not be ready until 2pm. If so, you can store your luggage and use the swimming pool to relax and splash around. The rest of the day is free for you to do as you please.

For your convenience, you will have a bicycle available during your stay, to transport you to and from your yoga classes. The bike is not fancy, but it is your companion and key to freedom in easy-going Chiang Mai. Simply go the Travel Center to receive your bicycle key and pay a deposit of 1000THB (will be paid back when you deliver back the bike and key
Day 2 (B)

Wake up early for a very light breakfast (serving starts at 6:30am) before doing a gentle yoga class at 10am – 11:30am. We recommend eating no more than 2 hours before class and remember to drink plenty of water beforehand.

Ride your bicycle to the neat little yoga house tugged away in a small sub-soi. It is a slow 20 minutes bike ride and we will give you the necessary directions beforehand. After yoga catch a well-deserved lunch (own expense) and have free time to explore the city and its many charming cafes. Be back in the little yoga house for your evening class, which takes place 6pm – 7:30pm. The night will now have taken over and your first day of doing yoga has come to an end.
Day 3 (B)
This is your second day of yoga and you may follow your routine from yesterday. Your morning yoga class is 10am – 11:30am and your evening yoga class takes place 6pm – 7:30pm.
In between and after, you have time available to explore the city.
Day 4 (B)

Your last day of yoga has come already. Have breakfast in the early morning and check-out from your room before you head to your morning yoga class 10am – 11:30am. You can leave your luggage at ECO Resort and you will need to return to here with the bicycle and key to get your deposit back.
After this your tour is complete. If you need help deciding what to do from here visit the travel center.

overview: Discover wildlife after dark on this Chaing Mai night safari through Doi Suthep-Pui National Park. Glimpse the predators that roam Thailand’s native jungle from a safe distance, and encounter gentler animals up close on this 3-hour experience. Giraffes, deer and zebras are free to roam throughout the park, and you’ll feed them from your palm as you travel through the night on an open tram.

It is not a true safari however, although there are some free-ranging animals, but essentially a large zoo. Still, the feel of exploring through a thick jungle at night and seeing nocturnal animals is a unique experience.

In the evening, pick up from your hotel then drive to the southern outskirts of Chiang Mai. At the Chiang Mai Night Safari, enjoy your 1.2 km walk along the Jaguar trail by the lake, followed by a ride on the tram to explore Savana Zone and Predator Prowl.

overview: Paddle a jungle fringed river in Northern Thailand on a full-day kayaking trip to the Mae Wang valley from Chiang Mai. Navigate fun Class I and Class II rapids, spot elephants at the water’s edge and hunt for birds in the lush, tropical forest. Advanced kayakers can continue into the lower Mae Wang River, where challenging Class III and Class IV rapids carom off boulders and riverbanks.

expect: Meet your guide at your Chiang Mai hotel, and enjoy views of the scenic countryside during the 45-minute drive to the Mae Wang valley, in the shadow of Doi Inthanon, Thailand’s highest mountain. Learn the basics of technique and safety, then launch your boat into the upper portion of the Mae Wang River, whose rapids are suited to even beginning boaters. Choose a river kayak or a sit on top boat that’s the best fit for your skill level. Follow a course that passes a series of elephant camps, and spot the friendly animals who come to the river to bathe and drink. Look for butterflies, birds and even jungle mammals along the way, and soak up the sun on easy going stretches of water between the rapids. The lower part of the river is a good fit for advanced boaters, who shouldn’t miss the boulders and white water of Lost Canyon.

expect: We touch the very heart of the spiritual and cultural heart of Chiang Mai. Early morning risers will enjoy the cool morning air of Chiang Mai at dawn when your guide and driver await you at your hotel lobby.

One of the most unique experiences in Thailand is a visit to a Buddhist temple to offer alms to the Buddhist monks. Each morning before dawn, the monks put on their distinctive saffron robes and quietly pad in their bare feet along the streets, carrying alms bowls and receiving boiled rice and condiments from the citizens of Thailand In return people receive the monks’ blessings. A brief exploration at the Srisodain temple may be made as well, religious festivals permitting.

We return back to your hotel for breakfast and some time to reflect on an amazing morning. After finishing that important first meal of the day, we head to the city ruins of Wiang Kum Kam, one of the latest discoveries around Chiang Mai. Wiang Kum Kam was a settlement long before King Mangrai’s capital around 1287- 90. Frequent flooding caused Mangrai to move, but the place remained important throughout the Lanna period. The area was restored as a historical park during the 1980-iess.Surrounded by paddy and village houses, the extensive site has a pleasant rural feel, yet it is very close to Chiang Mai. We will tour the ancient city ruins aboard a horse-drawn carriage before moving on to the riverbanks of the Ping River, the main water artery that flows through Chiang Mai. We will sail over the river for approximately 45 minutes before disembarkation and a short drive back to your hotel.

expect: An early morning visit to a Buddhist temple to offer alms to the monks is one of the most unique rituals a tourist can experience in Thailand. Each morning, monks in saffron robes, carrying their alms bowls, walk silently along the virtually empty streets to receive rice and condiments from local people. Guests have the opportunity to participate in this very special Thai custom by personally presenting alms at the Srisodain temple and receiving the monks’ blessings in return. After this enlightened morning, we head by local minivan back to your hotel for breakfast before we move on to Chiang Mai’s oldest and largest market – the Warorod Market. With our guide, we wander along the stalls where trade still goes on like the old days. One will not only find fruit, vegetables and spices here but plenty of other goods and perhaps you may walk into a nice souvenir.

From the market, we settle ourselves in an awaiting trishaw and head towards the Chiang Mai Art and Cultural Centre. This landmark is dedicated to the various forms of traditional art and handicraft of which Chiang Mai and surrounding regions are so well known for. From here, we leave our trishaw behind and board a so-called ‘scorpion-tail’ boat (also known as a long tail boat) for a 45-minute relaxing morning journey over the Ping River. Follow your guide along back lanes as you learn about the city’s culture and history. Explore Wat Chiang Mun and discover Chiang Mai’s ‘navel’ before meeting the city’s three royal founders. Pause at a roadside market for fresh juice and Thai sweets, take in the ancient stones of Wat Chedi Luang, then pass through Tha Phae Gate on your way to a Somphet Market for local snacks.

title.en: Half Day Colors of Chiang Mai Biking Tour

overview: Pedal through Chiang Mai’s scenic countryside and experience local culture on a 4-hour guided bike tour. Learn about Thailand’s religious heritage at a small Buddhist temple, and visit a former leper colony that shelters people with physical disabilities. See an elementary school that serves the region’s hill tribes, then watch local craftsmen shape pottery in a traditional studio. Set a relaxed pace as you pass rice fields and a gentle river, with plenty of breaks to enjoy local treats, cool drinks and a light Thai meal.
highlights: 4-hour bike tour of Chiang Mai's countryside
Learn about local culture and traditions
Visit a temple, school and studio
Enjoy the serenity of the lush countryside
Snacks, beverages and lunch included
expect: The route will take you on quiet and green land roads, passing the historic settlement Wiang Kum Kam, founded in 1286 by King Mengrai. It was the capital of the Lanna empire for a period of only 10 years. See temples and ruins dating back hundreds of years. You will make a stop at a local temple en-route. The guide can tell you everything about this temple and about Buddhism in general.

Then, you will stop at the McKean rehabilitation center; a former leper colony, once cut off from the outside world. Nowadays it is a rehabilitation center for people with many kinds of physical disabilities.

You continue the ride and stop at an elementary school mostly attended by hill tribe children. However, the visit to the school may not be available during school holidays. The ancient Lanna Empire produced some of the finest ceramics ever to have been made. These days the northern region still is the major center of Thailand’s pottery industry. At a small pottery we watch the craftsmen make different shapes of pottery by hand. Riding along the Ping River and explore the green scenery surrounded by beautiful flora and fauna. You will stop at a local bakery and take a delicious sweet bun while watching the baker produce many other different products.

At the market you will see the same products back in small traditional shops; and here you have the opportunity to sample some of the most delicious and exotic fruits and other snacks. We will stop every hour for a short rest and provide you with drinking water or a soft drink. Halfway through the trip a small Thai meal (Khao Soy Kai) will be served in a local restaurant.

Discover the hidden places of Chiang Mai through this recreational, cultural and educational half day Chiang Mai bicycle tour. Join this adventure to the unbeaten paths and to sites where old traditions continue to live on.

title.en: 1 Day Bike and River Kayak Adventure from Chiang Mai

overview: Get the best of land and water on this leisurely four-hour bike and river kayak adventure from Chiang Mai. Journey into the picturesque Mae Ngat Valley for an up-close look at rural Thai life. Paddle through the peaceful landscapes of the Mae Taeng Forest Reserve and learn about the incredible countryside that lies before you. This popular tour combines exploration by boat and bike and is ideal for travelers of all fitness levels.
highlights: 4-Hour Bike and River Kayak Adventure from Chiang Mai
Experience stunning landscapes by bike and boat
Ideal for travelers of all fitness levels
Round-trip hotel transport and water included
expect: Your day starts with being collected from your hotel at 8.30am and the short 45 minute drive north of Chiang Mai brings you to the beautiful Mae Ngat Valley. The amazing Ban Den Temple, located at the entrance of the valley, is hard to miss and makes a great starting point for your ride.

Heading further into the valley you will pass through open rice fields with local farmers tending to their crops using traditional farming techniques. The ride is leisurely and the pace is just right, so when it is time to cool off, you will make a stop at a local produce market and see what is on the menu.

Then you continue riding through the rural villages to the south of the valley where you can splurge on local fruits and snacks to re-energize for a change of pace with the kayaking leg of your adventure ahead.

With help of the favorable current of the Mae Ping River you will be steering your kayaks into the Mae Taeng Jungle Reserve. Only accessible by boat, as a nature lover, you will find your peace in this serene, quiet setting.

As bird life accompany you through the forest reserve, you will reach the far south end of the Mae Ngat Valley, where you may be greeted by a kayaking monk, and friend of your guide. From the river bank, in a beautiful plantation setting, you find a cozy restaurant with a well- deserved meal and a cold drink waiting for you.
Nature lovers and sport enthusiasts of all levels, will thoroughly enjoy this biking and kayaking combination tour, in northern Thailand.

title.en: Chiang Mai City Culture Half-Day Cycling Tour

overview: Pedal through Chiang Mai's narrow alleys and atmospheric neighborhoods on a half-day cycling tour that explores the city’s history, culture and crafts. Follow a 16-mile (25-km) route through the city, and pause to visit centuries-old temples and a local silversmith. Stop at Chiang Mai’s Women’s Correctional Institution for refreshments, then continue to Wat Phra Sing, the city’s holiest place. Leave the city center to visit a vibrant Chinese community and fresh food and flower markets filled with products from around the region.
highlights: Half-day bike tour of Chiang Mai
Explore the city with an experienced guide
Visit important landmarks and hidden gems
Get a local's perspective on life in the city
Great overview of the city, perfect for first time visitors
Lunch included
expect: Meet at a central Chiang Mai meeting point in the morning. During this 16 mile (25km) ride, you'll bike as much as possible over quiet roads and small lanes, passing beautiful temples and colorful markets while seeing local people continue their daily activities. Ride through small back roads and alleyways around and through the center of Chiang Mai. Stop at a silversmith that fabricates beautiful jewelry in different shapes and sizes (no shopping) then visit the adjacent Silver Temple to see the monks keeping themselves busy making decorations of alloy used for the renovation of this temple. Continue the ride through narrow alleys and small lanes to the center of the city where you'll visit the 14th century Wat Chedi Luang. Thailand’s most revered Buddha statue, the Emerald Buddha, used to reside in this temple until the Laotian took it to Luang Prabang (Laos) in 1545. Nowadays, this Buddha statue can be found in Bangkok’s Wat Phra Kaew. After shooting pictures of this remarkable Chedi, stop for refreshments at the Chiang Mai Women’s Correctional Institution. The aim of this institution is to reform and rehabilitate inmates who have almost done their sentences. The residents are serving light sentences for minor crimes and come from poor backgrounds, with many being hill-tribe women. Next, stop at the most visited temple of Chiang Mai, the beautiful Wat Phra Singh. The temple is very impressive and very picturesque with plenty of photo opportunities. The grounds are well maintained with multiple structures within, including the Wiharm Lai Kam assembly hall, Ho Trai library, Ubosot ordination hall and the main prayer hall. The journey continues to the outer circle of the center, passing through a fresh flower market where you will see the most beautiful flowers of the North. This area is called “China Town of Chiang Mai”.

Ride across the river and stop for more refreshments at a local market where your guide will have more time to examine some local exotic fruits and snacks with you. After this stop, take a surprising route back to the starting point.

title.en: Doi Suthep National Park Beginner Downhill Bike Ride from Chiang Mai

overview: Get back to nature and enjoy the thrill of an off-roading adventure on this Doi Suthep National Park bike ride that's perfect for beginners. Enjoy the convenience of round-trip hotel transport, professional-grade equipment and traditional Thai lunch with this popular tour that departs from Chiang Mai. Experience a shot of adrenaline as you cruise down a 5249 ft (1600m) peak that offers up incredible views of the Mae Ping Valley.
highlights: Lunch included
All necessary equipment included
Informative, friendly and professional guide
Free hotel pickup and drop-off included
expect: One of the most scenic and popular Mountain Bike rides in Chiang Mai, your mountain bike adventure kicks off with a transfer from your hotel and a comprehensive safety and bike fit- out briefing. Then you are all set to enjoy a 25 km ride, without the traffic. Itinerary:

You will be collected from your hotel and after registrations are done, embark on the 45 minute drive to the top of Doi Pui Mountain. It is here, at the summit of the Doi Suthep National Park, you will make the final preparation on your bike, take in a thorough safety briefing and then a short test ride to get comfortable with your equipment. Heading off toward the Coffee Plantation, along the jeep track, your guide will evaluate your riding ability and will help you with your downhill riding technique. Following the track, you will pass through spectacularly large trees and enjoy the cooler temperatures until your arrival at your first resting point, the Coffee Plantation. Home to the Hmong Hill Tribe People, you will be able to engage with the local community while enjoying the beautiful views of Chiang Mai and the Plantations below.

Setting off along the challenging terrain, this route now requires your full attention, as the wild growth of the forest hugs the track tightly. For the more experienced riders, there are single tracks paralleling the jeep route where you can take a little detour and get your technical single track fix.

With plenty of viewpoints and lightly mixed terrain to challenge you, the ride continues towards Lake Huay Tueng Tao, at the base of Doi Pui Mountain. The Lake is a favorite lunch spot and it is here you will enjoy a well-deserved meal, a cold drink and the local seasonal fruit. After another refreshing cool drink or maybe even a swim in the lake, take a glance back at the mountain that just gave you an awesome 3 hour mountain bike descent adventure. Time to make a move and you head back to Chiang Mai, the lazy way, in the truck. 3.30pm: You will be delivered back to your hotel for a well-earned rest.

title.en: Full-Day Hike and Bike Tour in Mae Sa Valley from Chiang Mai

overview: Hike and bike through Mae Sa Valley during this active tour from Chiang Mai. Start with a 2.5-hour morning hike that takes you past hill tribe villages and rice paddies, and into the lush rain forest of northern Thailand. Rest by a waterfall and refuel with a buffet Thai lunch before your afternoon bike ride. Ride down a combination of paved and dirt roads that lead through the rural valley to an orchid farm where your bike ride ends. Transfer to your Chiang Mai hotel to wrap up a memorable day.
highlights: Full-day tour with hike and bike ride in Mae Sa Valley from Chiang Mai
Take a morning hike in Mae Sa Valley to experience local life up close

expect: Your day trip starts with hotel pickup in Chiang Mai for the roughly 1-hour drive to Mae Sa Valley.

When you arrive on the outskirts of a hill tribe village, follow your guide on a 2.5-hour hike with a gradual climb past some village houses. Before long, you'll be surrounded by the unspoiled jungle environment as you continue along the local trail, which provides the opportunity to encounter local members of the hill tribe going about their daily routine. Throughout the hike, admire the variety of native vegetation and wildlife, and pass by a cabbage farm and another hill tribe village. Your guide tells you about the area and explains the customs of village life in northern Thailand as you go.

At midday, after you've worked up an appetite, head to a picturesque waterfall to enjoy a picnic lunch of homemade Thai cuisine. Then begin your cycling tour from the waterfall, riding mostly downhill on a paved road at first. As you turn off the main road, pedal along village alleyways, rice fields, and rural roads of Mae Sa Valley—an excellent way to see the local way of life. You'll also take a few off-road trails to get off the beaten track. Finish your bike ride at an orchid farm, where you can refresh and have a quick look around before the drive back to Chiang Mai for hotel drop-off in the evening.

overview: Pedal through traditional communities, rice paddies and orchards on a full-day bike tour along the Ping River from Chiang Mai. See villagers make traditional paper garlands at a Buddhist temple, and learn about Thai farming and mushroom cultivation. Sample local treats and have lunch in a neighborhood restaurant, then keep riding through gently rolling vegetable fields and bamboo forests. Enjoy a relaxing pace with plenty of time to stop for refreshments, and visit a centuries-old chedi and bustling fresh market before returning to the city.
highlights: Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Small group ensures personal service
Snacks and Beverages included
Lunch included

expect: Meet your guide at Moo Baan Nai Fun in the morning to gather your bikes. The route takes you over quiet country roads, and through small villages, where farmers work the rice fields, while their wives fill their days making terracotta. Stop at an old temple, where the oldest people from the village make flowers and garlands of paper and textiles, which are used during Thai weddings and Buddhist ceremonies.

Continue the ride to the rice fields making a short stop at a farm where mushrooms are cultivated. See women from a local village making rice crackers, banana chips, soy bean paste and other traditional Thai products. You can taste some of the local delicacies during the trip. The lunch will be served at a typical local restaurant around noon. While the chef is preparing the food, you can stroll over the market next to the restaurant, and explore different goods that are available.

The journey continues, following the Ping River and over country roads. Have you ever wondered what is in the pieces of bamboo they sell alongside the roads? Here you’ll learn the answer as well as how many different variations there are. In this area, most of the farmers grow lettuce, cabbage, ore other vegetables.

After another nice ride, arrive at a small restaurant beside the water to taste a cup of local coffee or some herb juice. Visit a 700 year old Chedi, and see how the two styles, Lopburi and Burmese, are combined. After a stop at the local market, where you can sample some local fruits or snacks, head back to the starting point at approximately 4:30pm. During the trip, take a break every hour for a short rest and drink. The stops and places of interest may vary depending on seasonal activities. This excursion will leave you with an unforgettable experience and memories of your stay in Chiang Mai which will last for a lifetime.

title.en: Full-Day Advanced XC Downhill Biking at Doi Suthep National Park Chiang Mai

overview: Enjoy the challenge of an advanced level full-day mountain bike ride near Chiang Mai. Start biking from the top of Doi Pui mountain, where landmarks below include the village of Doi Pui, revered Doi Suthep temple and Bhubing Palace. Your guide leads you on a ride along rough dirt tracks with plenty of ruts, roots and altitude changes to negotiate. Stop for coffee at a plantation in the forest, then end your ride at Lake Huay Tueng Tao, where you celebrate with a delicious Thai lunch.
highlights: Half-day advanced mountain bike ride near Doi Suthep, from Chiang Mai
Choose an advanced level ride that tackles rough terrain with challenging descents and ascents
See Doi Pui village, Wat Doi Suthep and Bhubing Palace from the Doi Pui summit

Have lunch at Lake Huay Tueng Tao after the ride
Includes biking equipment, lunch, round-trip transfer from Chiang Mai and informative guide
expect: You will be picked up from the hotel at 9:30am. After preparations and signup at the shop, a 45 minute drive takes you to the top of Doi Pui Mountain, 5250feet (1600m) elevation. Your journey start at the Doi Suthep National Park. A safety briefing at the top confirms that participants are ready to tackle this hard XC ride. An easy descent brings with a couple uphills on the way to the coffee plantation, here we regroup and some might choose to switch to a less strenuous and technically demanding ride, for those ready to go, the short break at the plantation gets us ready to head on.

Riding DH on flowing jeep track you will then turn west at the forest intersection, enjoying higher speeds and reach the High Country Royal Planting Project, enter the great divide, a barely used and unmaintained path. What once was double track has over the years turned into very technical single track riding.

We will practice our art of mountain biking, moving in and out of ruts, over rocks and roots, and quickly arrive in the deep jungle gully between the two mountains. Now at 3200 feet (975m) elevation, you will notice the tropical forest emerging from the pine woods, with huge banana leaves and plenty of bamboo filtering the light.
Once at the bottom of the gully we begin a long and rewarding uphill back to 4100feet (1250m), some ride, some walk, concentrating and preserving energy on the way to the summit.

A 200 year old bamboo grove greets us at the top, where a lengthy and well deserved break is taken. Continuing along the high road with fantastic views of the valley below we ride a gradual, long downhill. Warmed up we play in and out of ruts and holes, sand traps and rocks. The challenging terrain forces us to maintain full concentration on riding and moves us into “the zone” of the sport. Soon the Lake appears below us and the final run is all single track to the bottom, where a well-deserved lunch awaits us.

expect: A 4 wheel drive transportation will take you to the top of Doi Pui Mountain 5400 feet (1646m) above the Palace and Doi Suthep Temple. This first part of the trip helps you to evaluate your riding ability and we talk about techniques to make your downhill bike trip even more enjoyable. Everyone is encouraged to practice the newly learned techniques.

After the coffee break at the Plantation we keep riding downhill until reach our route west into the next valley. Fantastic forest riding with great views from open plantations, as you pass refreshing mountain creeks.

With only short steep up hills we wind our way across the valley, past small farm houses while witnessing the local hill tribes in their natural environment. Then we ride further downhill between plantations and forest with beautiful pine trees changing to eucalyptus growth on the way down to the Mae Ping Valley floor. The rarely used forest road presents the rider with plenty of challenges.

This forest road is hardly traveled and is perfect for mountain biking, allowing speed, but challenging your riding abilities. This is very secluded riding and you will feel deep appreciation for the local ecology.

Arriving at Lake Huay Tueng Tao we are expected at our favorite restaurant right at the lake where everyone meets up again. After a good lunch, drink and a taste of the local fruit we will travel back to the city the lazy way by truck and good memories.

On route, stop at the forest-swathed Wat Umong, a 700-year-old Buddhist temple unique for its system of tunnels. Head inside the underground corridors and see the caverns filled with golden Buddha statues. Next, cycle over rolling hills, and tackle the steep, but short, climb up Doi Gom. Break for refreshments, stop by at the Wat Ban Pong village temple, and cycle through rice fields to a Beekeeping Training Center. Head inside to see the hives, and learn about the bees and the different products made from their honey.
Then, back on your bike, pedal past botanical gardens and hit the same route back to Chiang Mai, where your tour ends at the start point.

overview: Get ready for adventure on this full-day white-water rafting trip in northern Thailand, with round-trip transport from Chiang Mai. Navigate the brisk waters of the Mae Taeng River, paddling downstream past verdant mountain scenery, terraced rice paddies and hill-tribe villages. Expert guides will assist you in tackling the class 2 to 4 rapids (sometimes reaching class 5) on this 2-hour journey, which also includes a visit to Sai Nam Phung Orchid Farm, home to a variety of rare orchids and hundreds of butterflies. highlights: White-water rafting on the Mae Taeng River

expect: Your full-day trip from Chiang Mai begins with hotel pickup in the morning. En route to the rafting point, you’re driven through a village in Mae Taeng District, with a stop at Sai Nam Phung Orchid Farm. Meander the scenic farm on foot for an hour with your guide and learn about the great array of orchids in bloom. Visit the orchid nursery and gape in awe at the colorful varieties being raised.

On the way to the Mae Taeng River, take in the beautiful surroundings of the northern Thai countryside, replete with quiet villages nestled in forested mountains. When you arrive at the camp, river guides offer instruction on river safety and basic paddling techniques to prepare you for the upcoming ride.

First, enjoy a Thai lunch, with seasonal fruit and provided bottled water. Then slip on your life jacket and helmet to start your 2-hour whitewater rafting adventure. The fast-flowing Mae Taeng River provides a thrilling ride with unforgettable views of the jungle blurring past. This powerful river north of Chiang Mai travels through a mountainous landscape that’s home to remote hill-tribe villages and terraced rice fields. The 6-mile (10- km) white-water rafting route winds through gorges and canyons featuring numerous waterfalls.

Expect to get wet as you bump over class 2 to 4 rapids; usually the weather is warm, so you’ll dry out soon, depending on the season and water levels. During the rainy season, from August to October, the fast-flowing river can get wild, guaranteeing an adrenaline-boosting ride over rapids that sometimes reach class 5. (Note: rapid classes run from 1 to 6, with 1 being the easiest and 6 being virtually unnavigable.) Complete your recreational tour with some time to refresh before you’re driven past traditional villages, orchards, valleys and rice fields back to Chiang Mai, with drop-off at your hotel.

overview: Discover Thailand’s oldest seaside national park, Sam Roi Yod (literally translated as 300 peaks) which features a unique collection of flora and fauna along the shores of the Gulf of Thailand. Also, limestone mountains rising steeply as high as 1985 ft (605 meters) make this part of the coast especially beautiful. Sam Roi Yod National Park covers 90 square kilometers and features the incredibly beautiful Phrayanakorn Cave.

Inside the cave stands a stunning pavilion created by one of the Rama kings (Rama V) who was so impressed by the cave he decided to build this pavilion. During certain hours of the day, when the sunlight shines from a certain angle, the sinkhole opening illuminates a nice tone of light over the pavillion, creating a spectacular view. He did revisit it several times during his reign. After a deserved lunch, we will leave you to enjoy a leisurely afternoon on the white sandy beach.

Offer alms to orange-clad monks in the shade of a Khmer-style stupa, and wander the atmospheric grounds of King Mongkut’s mountain palace. Buy a snack for the local monkeys as you slip into the hushed cool of Khao Luang Cave, where Buddha shrines glimmer in pools of natural light, then relax over a buffet lunch in Petchaburi before descending again to Hua Hin’s tropical coastline.

expect: The province of Petchaburi has been described as a place where Siam’s golden era of Ayutthaya still lives on. This is amply demonstrated in the magnificent architecture of its palaces and ancient temples.

On this full-day tour, you’ll drive north for around an hour from Hua Hin to Wat Mahathat Worawihan, one of the oldest and most notable temples in the area, built by the Khmer civilization. Part of the temple is more than a thousand years old. Prior to the procession of monks, we will prepare alms for you to offer the monks and receive their blessing. Continue on to Phra Nakorn Kiri, also known as Khao Wang or Palace Mountain. Here, on the top of the mountain, is a complex of buildings that includes the summer palace of King Rama IV, or King Mongkut. A cable car takes visitors up and down the mountain. Next you’ll visit Khao Luang, or Royal Mountain, which is actually a small hill with a cave that’s filled with ancient Buddha images. There is also a beautiful temple to the right of the cave entrance.

You can buy bananas and corn from the local vendors to feed the monkeys that gather at the entrance of the cave. Please exercise caution as some may become aggressive. Enjoy a buffet lunch at a hotel in Petchaburi before returning to Hua Hin.

Watch for the park’s playful wildlife: Irrawaddy Dolphins, Dusky Leaf Monkeys and Serow Goat Antelopes thrive in the protected area, which is also home to an extraordinary array of birds.

Following a pick-up from your hotel, transfer by luxury vehicle to Sam Roi Yot, which literally translates as “300 Peaks.” One of Thailand's largest freshwater marshes, the park is home to a rich diversity of wildlife.

Admire the limestone mountains rising steeply to heights of up to 2,025 feet (605 meters), making this part of the coast especially beautiful. You will pass an abundance of pineapple plantations en route to the park entrance, and once inside discover the beautiful pavilion inside the Phraya Nakhon Cave, built by King Rama V.

After lunch, enjoy some free time to take a leisurely afternoon stroll along one of the white sand beaches. Look out for resident birds and mammals, such as the dusky leaf monkey (langur) and native serow goat antelope, as well as visiting Irrawaddy dolphins.

overview: Discover the wild waterways and dense mangrove forests of Pranburi on this 4-hour rural retreat from Hua Hin. Get a taste of life in the Thai countryside with a visit to a tropical fruit plantation and sample freshly picked pineapples, mangoes, papayas and coconuts. Then, hop on a motorboat for a scenic cruise along the Pranburi River and stop to explore the mangrove swamps from a raised walkway.
highlights: 4-hour Pranburi River tour from Hua Hin
Soak up the scenery on a motorboat cruise along the Pranburi River
Visit a fruit plantation and sample delicious seasonal fruits Enjoy a close encounter with wildlife on a walk across the mangrove swamps
Free hotel pickup and drop-off included
Great choice for families!
expect: Following a 1/2 hour drive from Hua Hin we visit a typical Thai fruit plantation that grows bananas, pineapples, mangoes, coconuts, papayas and more. Some fruits will he prepared for you to taste too! From here board a small motor-boat for an hour's leisurely ride down the river. Witness the constantly changing scenery and birdlife and as you approach the entrance to the Gulf of Thailand pass by the myriad of fishing boats that have returned to dock after a night of work.
We then take a fascinating walk on an elevated platform over a mangrove swamp. The local guide will point out interesting details about the flora and fauna here.

title.en: Half-Day Afternoon Bicycle Tour in Hua Hin

overview: Explore Hua Hin attractions on this English speaking bicycle tour. Meet at Hua Hin Railway Station and discover the history of this history building, ride past the Fisher Bridge and follow your guide along to Khao Takieb Temple and Rajabbakti Park. Small group are limited to 8 people for a more intimate experience.Please note the price is per group.
highlights: Enjoy a day away from the hustle and bustle of the city
Enjoy fantastic aerial views
Pickup from a centrally located meeting point
Step back in time on a history tour
All entrance fees included
Family friendly
expect: Our English speaking guide will meet you at Hua Hin Railway Station at 1pm. We will provide the tour briefing and then provide you with bicycle. We will take some photos at Hua Hin Railway Station, one of the oldest and beautiful railway station in Thailand. The main features of the station is the Royal Waiting Room, this was once used to welcome the king and his court upon their visit to Hua Hin. From here, we will ride pass Fisher Bridge and visit the Sew local lifestyle before reaching at Khao Takiab Temple. Upon arrival at Khao Takiab Temple, you will see a 20-meter tall golden Buddha statue overlooking the sea. The figure can be seen from the beach but it is much more striking up close. Enjoy the boundless beaches views of Hua Hin from this height and great opportunity for photography.

Last stop, we will ride to 7 King at Rajabbakti Park, and you will see seven giant statues of great Kings from Thai history standing in line against a backdrop of forested hills. Each statues carries a plate with the name of the King and period of reign. Learn more history of Thai before we ride back to your hotel in Hua Hin. Alternatively, our driver will transport you back by car.

title.en: Hua Hin Night Tour by Night Including Dinner

overview: Discover Hua Hin after dark, on a night tour of the city by samlor, Thailand’s traditional three-wheeled bicycles. Relax on the passenger street as your guide leads you through the old town’s atmospheric streets, and pause to take in Hua Hin’s most iconic sights. Explore railway stations and a bustling night market, barter for local handicrafts, and end your evening with a traditional seafood dinner; enjoy the breeze off the Gulf of Thailand while lingering over beautifully-prepared fresh fish.
highlights: Informative, friendly and professional guide
Dinner included
Free hotel pickup and drop-off included
Perfect introduction for first-time visitors
expect: Enjoy a fun night out in Hua Hin wheeling through the city on a special samlor vehicle, or a 3-wheeled bike with room for passengers. Let your knowledgeable guide take you through the vibrant city, stopping at some of Hua Hin's interesting sights. Visit the beautiful railway stations, one of the symbols of the town, and visit Hua Hin's lively night markets. Barter and admire the colorful selection of goods, including fun souvenirs and delicious food.

Before the night is over, stop in at one of Hua Hin's famous seafood restaurants for some freshly caught fish. Look out over the beautiful Gulf of Siam and sink your teeth into the freshest fish you've ever tasted before you set off into the night again.

title.en: Full Day Snorkeling at Talu Island from Hua Hin Including Lunch

overview: Explore Hua Hin’s extraordinary coastline on a full-day snorkeling trip to Talu Island, whose ochre cliffs are a vivid backdrop for lush vegetation and azure bays. Board a speedboat across the Gulf of Thailand to the secluded isle, then slip into clear water to snorkel over coral gardens, swim with a school of fish, or simply relax on Talu’s pristine beaches. Enjoy lunch at sea, then while away the afternoon on an unspoiled tropical idyll.
highlights: Informative, friendly and professional guide
Lunch included
Free hotel pickup and drop-off included
expect: With clear, blue water and scenery that you are the only one on this island, clients are free to make it a very relaxing day out for sun bathing, swimming or snorkeling, being together with gardens of coral and the fish, swimming around you.

We will provide a delicious lunch. The rest of the time is for you to relax on the white sandy beach or swim in the crystal clear water before taking the speed boat back to the main land and comfortably bring you back to your booked accommodation.
